# Behavior specification

Scope: multiplayer only, meaning PvP and Exterminatus co-op (see CLAUDE.md). Record singleplayer-only behavior only if multiplayer depends on it.

Each entry records what it controls, its value, units and timing basis, provenance, confidence, and kind.

**Kind:** `extracted` (read from the install) · `observed` (measured from running the original) ·
`inferred` (derived from other evidence) · `public` (community or press description, not yet checked) ·
`provisional` (placeholder we chose; must be configurable and replaced).

Keep original internal units when their physical meaning is unknown. Never assume capture frame rate equals the simulation rate.

### Brace and vent (fidelity gap 7)

The heavy bolter's braced stance and the plasma weapons' heat vent, both on Reload (R). Simulation `SmSim/Brace.cs`, `Vent.cs` (hooks in
`Combat.StepPlayer`, `Reaction.CanReact`); reads `WeaponTuning` (wargear), `BraceTuning` and `VentAnimations` (behaviour graphs; `smtool graph-dump --brace`);
client `NetworkView.Brace.cs`; protocol 29. Synthetic tests: `BraceVentTests`. The owner described both from memory on 2026-10-28 ("while braced, you
could not walk and only turn on the spot. you could not cancel the brace once initiated until you were fully braced, at which point you could then
fire with the increased rate of fire and accuracy or cancel the brace"; "venting cooled the gun on top of normal cooling and it was approximately 6
seconds to fully cool while venting. everything but walking at normal walk speed stopped venting"; "heavy bolter expertise sped up getting into and
out of the brace"; "stuns and hit did not knock you out. the fire rate was increased to a moderately high degree") and asked for those notes to be
marked as estimations to be reviewed later: the rows that rest on them have kind "estimate (owner's recollection)" and source "owner 2026-10-28".

### Owner's bolter balance (2026-10-28; deliberate change from the original)

Stalker bolter (owner, 2026-11-02): armour head multiplier 10 instead of the data's 2.5, both races and variants (`OwnerBalance.StalkerShieldHead`, ours as the value that meets the owner's target).

The owner (2026-10-28): "buff that true grit bolter to be moderately more dps than bolt pistol. it should be powerful to use. buff the
standard bolter as well to match the dps of the bolt pistol as well." Applied in one table, `SmContent.OwnerBalance` (rules for both races and
the gold twins), after the classes and the Ork are read (`GameplayTuning.WithClasses`; the Ork's parity reference stays the data's bolter);
`GameplayTuning.Load(ownerBalance: false)` and `smtool weapon-dps <game-dir|auto> --data` give the data's values. Measured with
`smtool weapon-dps auto` on build 7412325 (body hits at 15 m; cooldowns in whole 30 Hz ticks as the simulation fires them: bolter 0.133 s →
4 ticks, pistol-slot bolter 0.155 s → 5, bolt pistol 0.25 s → 8; sustained = clip × damage / (clip × cooldown + reload); "vs marine" = the rate
at which a full marine's 100 shield + 100 health goes, shield first at the weapon's shield multiplier).

### Blind grenade (M37, used by the simulation)

The item the files call the krak grenade (`<race>_mp_eq_krak_grenade`) is the **blind grenade**: its ammunition type is
`blind_grenade` and its UI name is "Blind Grenades" (locale 104894 Space Marine, 111304 Chaos; the description, 104895,
calls them flash grenades that blind or disorient), extracted 2026-10-28 on build 7412325. The owner's knowledge of the
original (2026-10-28): it does **no damage and no stun**, neither on impact nor from its explosion, and when it goes off it
blinds everyone with a line of sight to it, even at medium or longish range. The blueprint's `do_damage` (10) and
`reaction_mp_stun` are therefore not applied. This follows the original; it is not listed in docs/changes-from-original.md.
One part is a deliberate change (owner's decision 2026-10-28, listed there): the blast blinds only players **facing** it (row "Facing"); the original blinds by distance.
Reader: `WeaponTuning.ReadThrown` → `BlindGrenade` (keyed on `common_data/ammunition/entry/ammunition_type` = `blind_grenade`);
rule: `World.BlindBlast` (`ReactionWorld.cs`), `SplashSpec.BlindOnly`, `ThrownSpec.IsBlindGrenade` / `PlayerName`.

#### The middle jump (M45, the owner's knowledge of the original; protocol 27)

Superseded on 2026-10-29 (feel/jump-pack-2, the owner: "revert to the old jump behavior"): the read packs have the cut off and the three jumps on (section "The three jumps, the dash attack's walls and the air slash's swing"); the rule below stays in the simulation as an option.

The owner (2026-10-28): there is a middle jump that does not go as high as the full jump; let go of the jump key (Space) mid-jump and
you stop rising any higher; after a brief delay you lose upward acceleration and start dropping. Searched first: the default `jump_info`
entry (`sm_mp_abil_jumppack`, `data/packages/wargear.oppc`: the height map, gravities, hang, power, smash and action fields) and the
behaviour graph `MP_SM_NAV_JP_Sim` (`smtool graph-dump`: transitions on `JumpPack_Land`, `BTN_Melee_Attack`, `BRANCH_In_Jump`,
`BRANCH_To_Jump`; the flight clips are posed by the vertical angle of motion) have **no release field, tag, branch or condition**, so the
rule is the user's knowledge and its timing ours. Read by `JumpPackTuning` (`ReleaseStopsRise`, `ReleaseRiseDelay`, `ReleaseRiseDecay`)
into `JumpPackSpec.ReleaseCut`, `ReleaseCutDelay`, `ReleaseCutDecay` for every pack read from the data (synthetic specs default to off:
the M14 rules); simulated by `JumpPack.Begin` / `Move` (`PlayerState.JumpCut`).

### The charge: the bull rush (M29, used by the simulation; protocol 18; M31: the sprint rule, protocol 20, superseded in protocol 39; M32: the charger's hyper armour, protocol 21)

Sources: the owner's description of the original (user's knowledge of the original, 2026-10-28): "running forward with W and
pressing F is the charge: a straight-line rush forward that, if it connects with an enemy player, stuns them and deals damage;
with an ally it just collides; the stun is negated by hyper armour". Data (read on the install, buildid 7412325, 2026-10-28):
every multiplayer melee weapon's `ability_bullrush_01` (knife, chainsword, power sword, axes; the same values on each), the

### Charge directions (feel/charge-directions; protocol 39, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner's playtest of 2026-10-29 (user's knowledge of the original and the owner's decision): "when right click running charge mid
short-hop as assault marine/raptor, you can only running charge forward no matter what keys you're pressing. you should be able to hold A or D or S
and go in other directions, as well as the usual combinations for more directions W+A, S+D as examples. also charge shouldn't require you to actually
sprint to initiate charge, just be holding w when you press f to initiate forward charge. also, you should be able to hold A or D while holding W and F
to charge a bit to the left or right." Supersedes M31's sprint gate (section "The charge"). Rules: `SmSim.Rush` (`CanStart`, `StartYaw`, `DashYaw`),
`Combat.StepPlayerCore` (a locked charge); client `NetworkView.TurnInPlace.cs`, `NetworkView.ChargeDirections.cs`; tests `ChargeDirectionsTests`.

### Falls, the airborne charge, the dash attack and the sword slash (protocol 30, used by the simulation; branch sim/jump-pack-and-falls)

Sources: the owner's descriptions and answers (2026-10-28; user's knowledge of the original): "in sm1 when a player walks off a ledge he drops as
if gravity pulls him straight down"; "when charging in front of a ledge ... the player should maintain their charge acceleration/momentum forward
until they hit the ground" (answer: hold the speed the charge had when it left the ground, no end by time or input until landing); "the assault
marine and raptor, while doing a short ground hop by tapping space bar, can right click to extend his hop into a running charge" (answer: stun by
default, "an estimation that needs to be reviewed by me later"); "the assault marine and raptor ground pound should have a smaller 'sword slash'
variant ... does not stun, only knocks the enemy off balance. damage done should be in the game files" (answers: the data's light interrupt; pound or
slash by the height at the press). Data (install buildid 7412325, read 2026-10-28; research notes kept outside the repository):
the jump-pack wargear (`sm_mp_abil_jumppack`, identical in `csm_mp_abil_jumppack`): `ability_dash_attack`, `ability_melee_dash`, `ability_hammer_dash`,
`jump_info/action_land_smash_by_height`; the marine rig's `SM_Base_MP` ("Jumppack Evade" and "Jump Dash Attack" states) and `MP_SM_NAV_JP_Sim` ("MeleeDash").
Readers: `SmContent.JumpPackAttackTuning`, `EvadeTuning.ReadDash` (the window); rules: `SmSim.Movement.Step`, `Rush`, `JumpPack`, `World` (`ResolveRush`,
`ResolveMelee`, `ResolveJump`). Measured on the install's Manufactorum with the real config (scratch probe, `Combat.StepPlayer` on the map's collision):
see the rows.

| Parameter (protocol 30) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |

### Jump-pack feel: fuel, air control, the air slash and impact effects (feel/jump-pack; protocol 31, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner's requests of 2026-10-29 (verbatim): "controlling all the characters feels quite janky. as an example, the 'air slash landing' (mini ground pound,
i'll refer to it as air slash from now on) feels terrible to use. improve the look and feel of the gameplay and animations. also the assault marine/raptor when flying
around should be able to somewhat move around in the air with WASD and combinations such as WA, SD. add more asm fuel baseline 300."; "when air slash landing you should
also move forward a bit, add a hit effect that shows roughly where the attack hitbox landed similar to the ground pound landing. for both intensify the effect and make
sure that textures aren't poking through the dust and smoke effects. its jarring visually."; "use the falling animation for when a player has charged off a ledge and
is 'accelerating/gliding'"; "there should be a bit of 'stickiness' to the gameplay. everything feels very floaty and disjointed/disconnected." The requests are the owner's
decisions (deliberate changes from the data where they differ); every value that makes them concrete is ours. Readers: `SmContent.JumpPackTuning` (`OwnerCapacity`,
`AirControlSpeed`, `AirControlAcceleration`), `SmContent.JumpPackAttackTuning` (`SnappySlash`, `SlashRecovery`, `SlashDive*`, `SlashLunge*`); rules: `SmSim.JumpPack`
(`AirSteer`, `SlashDirection`, `Begin`, `Move`); client: `NetworkView.DashAttack.cs`, `NetworkView.Jump.cs`, `GroundPoundFx`, `GroundShards`, `FxBatch`, `NetworkView.Fall.cs`.
Measured with a scratch probe (`Combat.StepPlayer` on the install's config, flat ground and Manufactorum's point B; "before" = the same config with the values below off,
which is the protocol 30 behaviour exactly) and live headless bots (`--slash-test`).

### Input buffering and slower movement (feel/buffer-speed; protocol 33, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner's requests of 2026-10-29 (verbatim): "when approaching the end of any animation the player should be able to buffer the next inputs. As an example,
when landing the air slash an assault marine/raptor should be able to hold space bar during the landing so that in the first frame possible after the recovery animation
for the landing he jumps immediately. Movement feels a bit too fast. Can you slow movement including flying and jumping hopping speed a by a small degree? Don't change
charge or lunge attack speed." Both requests are the owner's decisions (deliberate changes from the original: its own buffering is not in the data, its speeds are the
data's); every rule and value that makes them concrete is ours. Code: `SmSim.InputBuffer` (rules), `Combat.StepPlayer` (the replay and what counts as started),
`SmContent.MovementScale` (the speeds), `GameplayTuning.Load(ownerFeel)` (both on by default; `ownerFeel: false` gives the data's speeds and no buffer). Measured with a
scratch probe (`Combat.StepPlayer` on the install's config, flat ground; "before" = the same config with `ownerFeel: false` or the window 0) and `InputBufferTests`,
`MovementScaleTests`.

| Buffer: what is buffered | a press edge of Jump (evade, roll, hop, jump-pack take-off, dash), Melee (attack, combo step, dash attack, slash, pound), heavy Melee (stun strike, heavy chain, the charge), Grenade (throw), Switch or a slot key naming the holstered weapon (switch; replayed as the Switch toggle) and Reload (reload, brace change, vent, detonation) that starts nothing this tick while the player is held by an action or recovery: a melee step, a throw, a switch, an evade, a reaction, a charge or dash attack, any jump-pack phase (take-off to landing, pound and slash recoveries), a brace transition, a pending charged shot or a weapon raise; for Jump also the evade spacing and being in the air; for a grenade its cooldown. Fire is never buffered (a held control: full-automatic and charge weapons already fire on the first allowed tick while held; a click would replace a held Space or melee press) | — | per tick | `InputBuffer.Pressed`, `Locked`, `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (`used`) | the owner's request; the list ours | ours | low |

### The three jumps, the dash attack's walls and the air slash's swing (feel/jump-pack-2; protocol 38, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner's requests of 2026-10-29 (verbatim): "revert to the old jump behavior. space bar tap makes a hop dash, space bar medium hold makes a small
jump, and space bar long hold is a full jump."; "when an assault marine or raptor hops and then right clicks into a running charge, he should collide with walls and
play the same 'impact ricochet' animation that plays when a charge locks on to and sticks to and hits a target."; "the air slash landing currently plays the beginning
of the animation correctly, then performs the air slash backwards? i think. review the reference assault marine gameplay in the youtube video and make it feel more like
that." (the reference video could not be watched here: the fix rests on the data's clips, crops, tags and branch times); and, in a further message, "i generally feel too
locked out of movement.. reduce generally the animation timings so i can jump or hop out of things more easily. mark that as a estimation for later review." Code:
`SmSim.JumpPack` (`HoldTiers`, `TierCutGravity`, `TierTicks`, `MoveLock` / `JumpLock` with `SimConfig.LockTime`), `SmContent.JumpPackTuning` (`ThreeJumps`), `SmContent.JumpPackAttackTuning`
(`DashWallsFromStart`, `DashWallHitAngle`; the slash clip's crops), `SmSim.Rush.Begin` (the dash attack's exits with `SimConfig.LockTime`), `SmNet.SlashPose`, `client/NetworkView.Jump.cs`, `NetworkView.DashAttack.cs`.
Tests: `JumpTierTests`, `DashAttackWallTests`, `SlashPoseTests`, `JumpPackTuningTests`, `JumpPackAttackTuningTests`.

### Action lock scale and the sprint stop (feel/locks-sprint-stop; protocol 36, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner's requests of 2026-10-29 (verbatim): "i generally feel too locked out of movement.. reduce generally the animation timings so i can jump or hop out
of things more easily. mark that as a estimation for later review." and "a 'slowdown' when you stop sprinting where an animation plays of the character model slowing
down from the sprint back to a stop, if movement keys are let go of entirely." Both are the owner's decisions (deliberate changes); the factor 0.7 is an **estimate (owner's
request)** for the playtest to refine, and every rule that makes them concrete is ours. Code: `SimConfig.ActionLockScale` / `LockTime` (the gates), `Combat.MoveAtOf`,
`MeleeEvadeOpen`, `MeleeGateAt`, `ThrowHolds`, `Evade.Begin` / `LockTicks` / `JumpAllowed`, `Reaction.EscapeAt`, `Rush.Begin`; `SmSim.SprintStop` and
`SimConfig.SprintStopTime` (the stop); `MeleeTuning` (`BRANCH_Evade`), `SprintStopTuning` (the stop clip), `GameplayTuning.Load(ownerFeel)` (on by default; `ownerFeel: false`
gives the data's times and no stop). The install's values before and after are printed by `LockScaleSprintStopTests` (install test); `smtool graph-dump --root-motion` prints the
stop clip's root motion.

### Scoreboard ping on the HUD scoreboard (net/scoreboard-ping; protocol 50; ours)

The owner (2026-10-31): "add ping (ms) value in the scoreboard for each player". Server `GameServer.NoteSnapshotAck`, `SmNet/RttEstimator.cs`, the scoreboard row
(`ScoreEntry.PingMs`), client `NetworkView.PingCell`; tested in `ScoreboardPingTests`.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scoreboard ping: measurement (protocol 50, net/scoreboard-ping) | the server times each snapshot it sends to a peer (per peer, a ring of 64 ticks: 2.1 s at 30 Hz; an older snapshot's acknowledgement is not timed) and takes one round-trip sample when an input batch first acknowledges that snapshot: the network both ways, plus the client's wait for its next input send (up to one tick, 33 ms at 30 Hz) and the server's packet loop; a repeated or older acknowledgement gives none. ### Death and ragdoll (M23; protocol 15)

The ragdoll is client-side cosmetics (not simulated or synchronised by the server). Reader: `HavokRagdoll.ReadPhysics`;
content: `SmContent.RagdollModel.Load`, `SmContent.DeathTuning.Load`; layouts in docs/discovery.md ("Ragdoll and hit shapes").
Space Marine and Chaos players use the same rig (`havok_sm_base_mp__hkxx`, the only rig in `ebp_sets__mp_versus_set`).

The joint's zero is the pose at death, so each limit is shifted by the child frame's start angle relative to the parent frame (Godot Euler order XYZ) and widened to include the start (lower = min(limit − start, 0), upper = max(limit − start, 0), clamped to ±(π − 0.01)). ### Effect rendering (M25b; client only, not simulated)

The client plays the effects named in the M25a table with `client/FxPlayer.cs` (sprites from the original atlas, a few pooled
lights, Godot decals with the original decal textures). Which effect plays, its scale, marker and lifetime are the install's;
how the renderer reads an element's fields is not documented anywhere we have, so every rule below is an interpretation.
`--placeholder-fx` restores the old spheres; `--no-fx` draws nothing.

| Effect axis | local +Y: out of the barrel (muzzle), toward the target (tracer), along the surface normal (impact) | — | per effect | `FxPlayer` | ours | interpretation | medium |

Measured in the `--fx` view (frag, `--smoke on`, `--fx-hard`, camera 4 m up, 8 m away): the screen's lower half (the floor in front of the cloud's centre) is pixel for pixel the smoke-off picture, the upper half (behind it) is covered | — | per frame | `FxBatch` shader | measured (our test view) | observed | high |
| Lines on the floor through smoke: the fix | every alpha-blended camera-facing card is depth-tested at a plane moved toward the camera by 0.5 x its half size, at most 1 m and never closer than 0.5 m to the camera, shrunk by the same perspective so it covers the same pixels (the floor inside the front part of a cloud or a debris card is covered). Additive cards are not moved (they cannot hide anything, and moved they lit thin walls in front of a blast; review S1). The near-camera fade reads the card's own depth, the soft fade the moved plane (review S2). The 1 m cap (3 m in the first cut) bounds the leak through thin surfaces: in the `--fx` view a frag 0.6 m behind a wall with `--smoke on` adds a little smoke over the wall (mean 1.6 of 255, at most 32, on top of what its sprays already throw in front), 1.5 m behind adds nothing, and with the smoke off nothing changes. `--smoke on` reproduces the pre-branch picture pixel for pixel in the test views measured (a frag 8 m away, a wall impact 3 m away), except where geometry lies inside the first metre in front of an alpha card's centre; `--smoke on --no-fx-pull` is the pre-branch renderer exactly (test aid) | m | per quad | `FxBatch.PullShare`, `PullMax`, `PullKeep` | ours | estimate | low |

### Sound playback (M26b; client only, not simulated)

Content: `SmContent.AudioCatalog` (Wwise banks of the install, read-only), `SoundTriggers` (BAF `post_sound_event` commands),
`MapAudio` (`a_audio` and other layers); client: `SoundSystem`, `NetworkView.Sound.cs`. Decoded audio lives only in
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\audio\ogg\`. Coverage on the install (`smtool audio-coverage`, 2026-10-27): 238 event names from
64 files and Manufactorum's layers; 197 resolve to media, 27 are stop, state or LPF events without media, 14 are not in the
loaded banks (`play_health_stage_*`, `play_iron_halo`, `play_sm_heavy_bolter_drop/pick_up/ringout`, `play_sm_sk01_bodyslam`,
`play_sm_stomp_displace_build`, `play_grenade_launcher_fire_lv3`, `stop_ch_plasma_pistol_charge`, `Play_Music_R200_Shaft`, and the
layer names `er`, `rer`).

Owner's report: the footsteps "sound nothing like the original". Content: `SoundTriggers`, `AudioCatalog`, `InstanceLimiter`; client: `NetworkView.Sound.cs`, `NetworkView.Sound.Log.cs`, `SoundSystem.cs`. Evidence and commands (`smtool audio-event|audio-mix|audio-levels|audio-tags|audio-surfaces|audio-rtpcs|audio-node|audio-objects`): docs/discovery.md, "Footsteps (the event graph and what was wrong)". Test aid: `--log-sound footstep` prints the tag, event, variant, surface, speed and each voice's mix per step; `--sound-limits none|footsteps|all`.

Rule: an instance of a node is one post's play of it (a layer's two sounds started together count once and never kill each other); age is the post's number, not the start of its voices (a voice that decoded late never kills a newer post's instance: when its own post is the oldest it is dropped); a new voice that finds the node at its limit kills the oldest instance (the same emitter's, or any emitter's with the global flag), its delayed voices below the node are cancelled and its voices fade out over 30 ms (ours); kill-newest drops the new voice (and no kill is carried out for it); a node that ignores its parents hides their limits, also with no limit of its own. Only voices that will really start take part: an inaudible one never evicts an audible one. 2,945 of 17,875 MP-bank nodes have a limit (kill-newest 9, global 834, ignore-parent 374; values 1 to 80) | instances | per post | `InstanceLimiter`, `SoundSystem.ApplyInstanceLimits` | banks | extracted (flags and values; byte order of the flags: interpretation); the instance = one play: interpretation; fade 30 ms: ours | medium |

Threshold −60 dB not counting the master bus (ours). **Modes of `--sound-limits`:** `none` = exactly the behaviour before the fix (no instance limits, no culling of non-positioned voices); `footsteps` (the default from this fix to the polish pass P1) = instance limits and the culling of non-positioned voices under the threshold for the posts of `is_footstep_sound` commands (footsteps and landings) only; `all` (**the default since P1**, the owner's decision of 2026-11-10 after the A/B clips; `--sound-limits footsteps` restores) = both for every post. Positioned voices keep the old rule (beyond the curve's end or under the threshold) in every mode. A sound whose byte is 0 (keep playing) is never culled. The match-flow music (the four stingers `play_mp_{sm,chaos}_{victory,loss}`: segments with volume -3 to -6 dB, below-threshold byte 0, and `max 1 kill-newest global`; the countdown `play_mp_countdown`: below-threshold 1, levels -24 to -27 dB) is never posted as a footstep, so `footsteps` mode touches none of it; only `all` would apply the stingers' limit (a second stinger while one plays is dropped, as the data says) | dB | per voice | `VoiceAudibility.IsAudible`, `SoundSystem.Audible` | banks | flag extracted (reading: interpretation); threshold: ours | medium |
| The advanced settings' last two bytes | read as `TrailingA`, `TrailingB` (`smtool audio-rtpcs --limits`). Statistics over 17,875 nodes: (A,B) = (0,0) on 16,924, (1,0) on 414, (1,1) on 515, (0,1) on 22. A = 1 goes with a limit (783 of 929 nodes with A = 1 set one, against 2,162 of 16,946 with A = 0) and a limit that differs from the parent's (12 % equal when A = 1 against 42 % when A = 0; the parent has none in 53 % against 22 %); B = 1 goes with a below-threshold byte that differs from the parent's (10 % equal against 65 %). Not proof of "override parent" flags: nodes with A = 0 also carry their own limits (2,162 of them; the footstep layers `231a537b`, `31633ea0`, `1dd10a86` have A = 1, but the `Random 127aa7b3` with a limit of 2 under them has A = 0), so a node without the flag is **not** made to inherit: every node's own limit and byte are used, and the parents' limits apply through the chain walk of every ancestor (Wwise counts all ancestors). If the flags are overrides, nodes with A = 0 and a limit would be overstated; the effect is not visible on the footsteps | — | per node | `HircNodeBase.TrailingA/B` | banks | interpretation, not adopted | low |

### Footsteps, second pass (sound/footsteps-2; client and content only, not simulated)

Owner's report 2026-10-29: the footsteps "still sound atrocious ... like hard boots banging on loose metal flooring"; wanted: the original's sound exactly, slightly quieter (a deliberate change). Content: `VoiceMixer.PeakNormalised`, `VoiceMixer.CapRtpcVolume`, `RtpcVolumeCap`, `RtpcVolumeCaps`, `FootstepLevel`; client: `SoundSystem.RtpcCap`, `NetworkView.PostBinding`. Evidence and commands: docs/discovery.md "Footsteps, second pass". ### Shield sounds (sound/shield-regen; client and content only, not simulated)

Owner's report 2026-10-29: "the shield regenerating starting sound is playing constantly on a loop. am i hearing other players armor regenerate or is my own looping?" Answer: **your own**. The repeating sound is the broken-shield warning of the local player (other players' shield sounds are not played: the data makes them local-player only). Content: `ShieldSoundTracker`; client: `NetworkView.SoundOwnShield`, `SoundSystem.StopLoops`. Evidence: docs/discovery.md "Shield sounds". Test aid: `--log-sound armour` (every change of the own shield with the triggers it fires, every armour post, loops ended at a death or spawn).

**Regen sound level (owner decision 2026-10-31; kind owner decision, confidence: owner's rough figures):** "the armor regen sound should falloff past a certain distance. call it 20 feet roughly. also make it about 50% of the current volume." Value: regen start / restored sounds -6.02 dB (50% amplitude, relative to the previous level, own player). Other players' regen: the same -6.02 dB with a smoothstep amplitude fade to silence at 6.096 m (20 ft, "roughly"); today no other player's regen is posted (check: `--log-sound armour,post`, six bots, only the local player's armour posts), so this is guard only. Unit: dB / metres. Source: owner. Switch: client `--regen-sound-old` (earlier level, no falloff). Code: `RegenSoundLevel`, `NetworkView.PostBinding`.

### Tag-started sounds end with their action (sound/regen-loop-2; client and content only)

Owner's report 2026-10-30: a continuous hum or buzz in matches, thought to be the shield regeneration. The regeneration sound is not it: `play_armor_restore` is a one-shot (Random container, 0.75 s Stop) and the warning loop is ended by it, by a death and by a spawn (sound/shield-regen); a headless run (Seize Ground, 2 sound clients and 6 bots, 5 minutes) showed the warning's continuations rise only between a shield break and the next regeneration or death, then stay flat. The endless sound found instead: a behaviour tag's `post_sound_event` names a start and a stop event; the client never posted the stop. The chainsword swing (`swing_x1` -> `play_sm_chainsword_swing_x1`, stop `stop_sm_chainsword_swing`) contains an endless continuous container (the motor layer, wem 305337544), so every swing added a chain that only a death ended: 774 continuations by 80 s, 17 to 40 a second, the 64-voice cap reached (the chaos side: `play_ch_chainsword_swing_x4`, stop `stop_ch_chainsword_swing`). Test aid: `--log-sound tag` prints the binding's stop and every `TAG STOP`.

The same stop owed twice is posted once. ### Sound hunt: the repeating sound (fix/sound-hunt; owner 2026-10-31; client only)

Owner: a sound heard over and over, like a hum that builds up. A census of every posted sound (new `--log-sound census`: per event posts, voices started, 2D voices, looping voices, mean volume, continuations, emitters; a line every 30 s) in headless Annihilation and Seize Ground runs on Manufactorum (6 bots, 2 sound clients, 5 to 20 minutes) found no map emitter, no ambience bed, no music, no weather, no announcer loop and no HUD tick in a match (the client plays none of those; map noise is off since decision 56). The one defect: **`play_mp_countdown`**, an endless container, was posted once per round and never stopped when the countdown ran out, so one 2D voice replayed about every 10 s for the rest of the match and each new round (the match restarts every few minutes) stacked another chain: the pre-start swell "builds" with the rounds. Fixed by posting it once. The non-defect candidates silenced behind a restore switch are Seize Ground's per-second capture and score ticks.

Before: the swell looped for the whole match, one 2D voice about every 10 s at -24 dB, and every round (the match restarts) added a chain (62 continuations in 630 s of an Annihilation run; 185 in 1200 s of a Seize Ground run, the rate doubling with each round). ### Hit sound by the victim's armour (fx/hit-armour-sound; owner's item 59, 2026-10-31; client only)

The data has no separate "armour crack" hit event: `play_iron_halo` (the blueprint's `armourshield_hit`) is in no bank, and `play_armor_break` is the own shield breaking. The armour hit sound is inside each weapon's hit event: `play_bolter_hits` (bolters, bolt pistol, storm and heavy bolter), `play_stalker_hits`, `play_plasma_rifle_hit`, `play_plasma_pistol_hit`, `play_melta_gun_hit`, `play_sm_lascannon_impacts` and the others (`smtool audio-event`, `audio-coverage`) switch on `material_type`: `ceramite_armour` = a random container of 7 hard metal clangs (-3 dB, `202447d8`), `flesh` = two layers of short wet impacts, and a last action plays a six-sound flesh layer only while the impact state `set_state_impact_broken_armor` is set (`set_state_impact_armor` otherwise). The client now picks by the victim's armour bit, for every weapon, for the shooter's own hits and for other players' shots (so the victim hears it too, positioned at the hit).

### Sound loudness: louder and farther (sound/louder-farther; owner 2026-11-08; client only, both modes, not simulated)

Owner (2026-11-08): "the sound of all game sounds (weapons shooting, melee attacks, grunts, explosions) should be clearly hearable and relatively much louder from much further away. currently the game seems much too quiet. both game modes"; "the game in general is too quiet. make everything much louder". Checked first for a bug that makes us quieter than the data (smtool audio-mix on the install): none found. The output bus chain is the data's (e.g. the bolter's -10.3, -3, -2 and the master's -7 dB, -22.3 dB in all; each bus's two volume fields are never both set, so nothing is counted twice), node volumes are 0, no RTPC curve touches these events (the peak cap does not apply), the options default to full volume, and the curves are read once. The quietness is the data's mix played as it is: a remote bolter shot is -25.5 dB at the voice at 5 m and -60.9 dB at 60 m.

### Classic soundscape: hearing the other players (sound/classic-soundscape; owner's interview 2026-11-13; client only, Annihilation and Seize Ground, not simulated)

Owner (2026-11-13): "its difficult to hear other player's footsteps and actions (charges, rolls, assault marine/raptor jumps and hops, etc.) around the player's vicinity and the map as a whole. these sounds are important to keep track of players around the map using their sound effects". Interview answers: footsteps and other movement actions, grunts and barks are heard 50 m away; weapons fire of all kinds, grenade explosions, jump-pack take-offs and hops and ground pounds carry farther; in a firefight "never cut off"; other players' reloads within about 20 m; evade rolls from the install's sounds; "others louder, own as now"; direction: clear by default with a launch option back to the natural softer feel. Measured with `smtool audio-mix <event> --distance d --loudness [--step]` (before) and `--scape movement|movement-far|gunfire|reload` (after, `ClassicSoundscape.Apply`): the loudest layer's level at the voice in dB (master bus -7 and the +9 loudness gain counted).

### No firing while sprinting (sim/no-fire-while-sprinting; protocol 51, no wire change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-01, with a recording of a Devastator sprinting with the lascannon and shooting: "lascannon devastator can currently shoot while sprinting.
you should not be able to shoot while sprinting." Cause: M27's rule ("Simulation rule: firing ends the sprint", above) let a held trigger take the Sprint bit away and fire in
the same tick; a weapon that waits for its raise (rifles, pistols) showed 6 or 5 ticks of slowing first, but the always-ready weapons (lascannon, which fires on the press since
sim/instant-fire, heavy bolter, plasma cannon, melta, grenade launcher) fired in the press tick while the body still moved at sprint speed. Code: `Combat.StepPlayerCore`
(`sprintNoFire`), `Combat.SprintApplies`. Tests: `NoFireWhileSprintingTests`, `HipFireTests`, `OwnerRulesTests`. Supersedes M27's "firing ends the sprint" on the ground and
the extracted "Sprint and shooting" row's sprint-to-fire transition. No client change: the own muzzle flash, tracer, recoil and fire sound follow the prediction's fired events and clip / cooldown / heat changes (`NetworkView.Fx.FxOwnShots`, `NetworkView.Sound`), which a blocked trigger does not produce.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No firing while sprinting (protocol 51) | while the sprint is applied (Sprint held with the stick forward, on the ground; not in aim mode, a jump-pack phase, an evade, a reaction, the charge, a brace, or a melee attack's movement lock) the trigger does nothing, **for every weapon**: no basic shot, no charge start, no raise, nothing buffered; a held full-auto trigger stops on the sprint's first tick. The held trigger no longer takes the sprint away (the player sprints at sprint speed) | - | per tick | `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (`sprintNoFire`) | the owner's rule, 2026-11-01 (user's knowledge of the original); against the extracted sprint-to-fire transitions of the behaviour graphs (above) | owner's recollection | high |
| What the sprint cancels | on the sprint's first tick: a held charge (no shot; the heat it built stays), a pending charged shot, a raise and the shot waiting for it, a burst's later rounds. A release during the sprint, or on the tick the sprint starts, fires nothing. Nothing is carried over to after the sprint | - | per tick | `Combat.StepPlayerCore` | the rule applied to the charge (owner: no shot while sprinting); cancel rather than keep the charge: ours, as a melee attack or an evade cancels it | ours | medium |
| After the sprint | unchanged exit timing: the sprint lowered the weapon (M31), so the first shot after it waits for the family's raise (rifle 0.2 s = 6 ticks, pistol 0.167 s = 5); the always-ready weapons fire on the first tick out of the sprint (a charge weapon's tap on its release tick). A trigger held through the sprint's end: a full-auto weapon fires on (after the raise); a semi-automatic or charge weapon (the lascannon included) needs a new press, as after any cancel | ticks | per tick | `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (`PlayerState.FireHeld` stays the real button) | raise: extracted / owner (M31, M32); the new-press rule for a held trigger: ours | ours | medium |

### Custom classes, end to end (customizer T9; summary) and in the match (T7)

**What the customizer does, from the profile to the other players' screens.** The player keeps up to 10 custom classes (a role, weapons, equipment,
two perks, one Space Marine and one Chaos appearance each) and up to 10 appearances per race (9 armour pieces, three colours and a pattern bit per
slot, a badge or a custom 128 x 128 emblem per shoulder pad, an eye-lens colour) in `customization.json` next to `emblems/<hash>.bc3`
(`%APPDATA%\sm-reimpl`, or beside the file `--profile` names; never the repository or the install; `ProfileStore`, repairs, atomic writes). The front end
(`client/FrontEnd`, `client/Customizer`) edits it; a Join turns the active class into wire indices for the side asked for (`JoinPlan`: class by role, every item
found by name, the perks, both races' `AppearanceCode`) and the Hello carries them (protocol 22/23). The server validates every field (bad ones default one by
one), spawns the class, keeps the appearance with a version (0 = the default look) and applies a later `Setup` at the next respawn. Other clients learn the
version from the 1 Hz scoreboard, ask for the appearance (`AppearanceQuery`) and pull a custom emblem in chunks from the server, which pulled it from its owner
(content-addressed, verified, rate limited; section above). The client resolves each player's code with the same `AppearanceResolver` the customizer's preview
uses and dresses the shared rig with it (`AppearanceAssets`, section "Armour rendering of a customized look"); the match view (this section) decides who wears
what and when. In the match Esc opens the same creator to change the loadout and look for the next life (the C key was removed on 2026-10-30, owner). Everything is unlocked
(`UnlockMode.All`); the perks work (section "Perks"). Open owner questions are listed in docs/customizer-architecture.md section 10; the ones that change
what is drawn, both decided by the owner on 2026-10-28: the Chaos default left pad follows `pattern_enabled` (red; `SchemePatternFlagHidesSecondary` stays true) and the Chaos Havoc and Raptor default to `chaos_default` plus their class parts.

Code: `client/NetworkView.Appearance.cs` (looks), `client/NetworkView.Loadout.cs` (picker), `client/CharacterViewer.SetLook`; engine-free rules and their tests:
`client/Looks/LookLogic.cs`, `tests/SmNet.Tests/NetworkLookTests.cs`. Numbers below were measured on this PC (debug build, Manufactorum, a windowed client at
1280 x 720 off screen, the other players headless bots on 127.0.0.1).

### Appearance slots (ui/appearance-slots; client and profile only, no protocol change)

The owner's request of 2026-11-06: "Ability to create appearance - separate from loadouts. Otherwise if you want the same appearance for all your loadouts you have to remake the
appearance 9 more times. you should be able to make an appearance, save it in one of 10 slots, then apply that appearance to any loadout." The appearance editor's first section,
MY APPEARANCES, shows the side's ten slots; Enter on an empty slot saves the open loadout's look there (the loadout then wears it), Enter on a filled one opens its page: wear it on this
loadout, save this loadout's look over it (asks first), apply to all loadouts, put it on or take it off each loadout, rename, delete. The data has the text "Appearance %1NUM%" (111828),
so the original had numbered saved appearances; how many and how a loadout took one is not in the data. Code: `client/Customizer/Model/AppearanceSlots.cs`,
`client/Customizer/AppearanceView.Slots.cs`; checks: `--ui-selftest` (`UiSelfTest.AppearanceSlots.cs`), `CustomizerModelTests` (the slot tests).

### Weapon spread (weapons/spread; the owner's decision 2026-10-28; used by the simulation; no protocol change)

The owner (2026-10-28): "Add the game data's weapon spread, so Bolter Targeter, Improved Twin-Link, Burst Fire and Lascannon Stabilizers can
work." This **reverses M27's "hip fire = aimed, no scatter"**. Data (Verified-local, buildid 7412325): every MP firearm's delivery has
`kick_back_and_scatter_values/{standing|aiming|crouching}/{idle|walking|running}`, each an entry list (a default entry plus perk entries, chosen
like every other tuning entry, `UpgradeScope`) naming a `tuning_set` `climb_sway_scatter\<name>` in `data/packages/climb_sway_scatter.oppc` (242
sets), a file of three blocks: `scatter` (initial horizontal / vertical angle, increase per shot, max horizontal / vertical, decrease per second,
decrease delay, two empty `target_speed_to_scatter_*` tables), `climb` (permanent and temporary climb per shot, max temporary climb, climb rate,
recovery rate) and `sway` (min / max temporary and permanent sway per shot, sway rate, recovery rate, max temporary sway, temporary sway
increase / decrease / delay). Read by `SmContent.SpreadTuning` (kept out of `WeaponTuning`) into `WeaponSpec.Spread` (`SpreadSpec`: the basic
shot's six standing / aiming × idle / walking / running sets and each charge stage's), part of the config hash. Per weapon (Space Marine
names; the Chaos weapons name the same sets): scatter rested / per shot / max (degrees); recovery °/s after the delay (s):

| Wire | nothing new (protocol unchanged): the bloom is not in snapshots; the client keeps its predicted bloom for the snapshot's tick when it reconciles (`Spread.Carry`); it rests the bloom instead when the prediction and the record disagree on life, class, slot or chosen weapons, when it has no prediction for that tick (before the first one, after a stall), and when a round began since the previous snapshot with everyone respawned in place (the match block went from warm-up or an ended match into the countdown, from an ended match into play, or Seize Ground's warm-up into play: `SpreadReconcile`). **Approximation:** after a stall the client restarts its bloom from rest while the server's may still be warm, so the predicted bloom can lag the server's (never exceed it) until both settle; and the ticks predicted before a round restart's snapshot arrives keep the old bloom for about one round trip. This changes only the own tracer and impact picture, never the server's authoritative shot. Reconcile outcomes are counted (`GameClient.SpreadOutcomes`). ### Perks (M43; protocol 23)

Owner's request (2026-10-28): every perk of the original, functional; no level progression (every perk available, `UnlockMode.All`); two
slots, any class perk in either (our default). Data: docs/customizer-and-perks-data.md section 2. `smtool perks <game-dir|auto>` prints every
perk with its classes and status and every variant read with the fields it changes (install, buildid 7412325: 47 upgrade strings, 128
variants, 7 player-blueprint upgrades).

**Mechanism (Verified-local layout; the combination rules interpretation):** a perk applies one upgrade string (`apply_upgrade_string`); a
tuning entry that requires it replaces the default entry. The content loader reads every weapon, thrown item, jump pack and melee combo a
class carries **again with each perk string the file requires granted, and each pair of them** (`SmContent.UpgradeScope`; every reader's entry
choice: "the entry whose required upgrades are all granted, preferring the one that requires the most"; a block's entries are exclusive, so
two perks touching the same block give the entry listed first); reads that differ become `UpgradeVariant`s. The simulation picks each
player's variant from its two perks' strings (`Loadouts.Weapon/Equipment/JumpPack/Melee*`, `Variants.Pick`). The player blueprint's perk
entries become `SimConfig.PlayerUpgrades` (`SmContent.PlayerUpgrades`; read from `sm_space_marine_player`, the Chaos blueprint compared):
received-damage multipliers by `damagetype` (ranged, melee, explosive; the whole hit, its armour part included: ours), regeneration
additions, the Iron Halo shield, death and armour-break blasts (`Loadouts.Body`). Server-authoritative; the recipient's own record carries its
two perks and a burst's rounds left (protocol 23: a 2-byte perk word, perk indices 0..126; worst-case snapshot 1200 = the budget), so the
prediction picks the server's variants (tested at 150 ms RTT, 5 % loss: no mismatch). Others' perks are not sent (server effects only).

Columns as the rest of this file: value (base → with the perk; data values unless the kind says otherwise), units, timing basis, where
in the code, source, kind, confidence; then the status. Classes: SA/CR Assault Marine / Raptor, ST/CT Tactical, SD/CH Devastator / Havoc.
"Not in the data" rows have no value to record (owner questions). Confidence is for the value as read; the combination rules are listed
below the table.

### Classic PvP: Deploy, respawn choice, heavy bolter count (fix/pvp-deploy-spawn; protocol 58)

The owner, 2026-11-06 (classic PvP = Annihilation and Seize Ground; Musou Mode unchanged): "When pressing the deploy button in the loadout Customizer (while in game
classic PvP mode only), suicide the player so they immediately respawn the the new loadout. You should never respawn in clsssic PvP mode on top of your ally. Always in
the main spawn room, or choose to spawn at a captured point. You can also choose to spawn on a player but only if they have the perk teleport homer on and they're alive.
In clsssic PvP mode heavy bolter currently has infinite ammo. It should cap at 400." Why allies spawned on top of each other: Teleport Homer (protocol 44) placed every
respawning ally next to the nearest living carrier automatically, and the Tactical classes carry the perk by default, so most respawns landed 1.5 m behind a living Tactical.
Why the heavy bolter looked infinite: the simulation always spent the data's 400 rounds a life (`capacity_clip` 400, no `capacity_reserve`; 400 shots in about 140 s of held
fire with its overheats, then nothing), but the HUD's weapon box showed the movie's endless sign (`infinity_mc`) and no count for it. Code: `src/SmSim/SpawnChoice.cs`
(`World.SetSpawnChoice`, `SpawnOptions`, `RequestDeploy`, `TryChosenSpawn`, `PointSpot`), `World.Step`, `TryStartAreaSpawn`, `SmNet.SpawnChoiceRules`,
`Protocol.Spawn.cs`, `GameServer.Spawn.cs`, `client/NetworkView.SpawnChoice.cs`, `NetworkView.Loadout.cs` (`DeployFromPicker`), `WeaponBoxRules`. Tests: `PvpDeploySpawnTests`.

### Combat stims (perks/inert-2; protocol 40, the config hash changes)

The equipment `sm_mp_eq_stimpack` (both sides; locale 104400 "Combat Stimulants") had been read but not offered (no thrown delivery). It is now a
thrown-slot item that throws nothing: `SmContent.StimTuning` reads it into a `ThrownSpec` with a `StimSpec` (`ThrownSpec.NoProjectile`), offered as the
classes' third equipment choice; the simulation runs the use as a throw with the stim's own times (`ThrownSpec.ReleaseAt` / `DurationOf`) and at the
release sets `PlayerState.StimLeft` (`SmSim/Stims.cs`). Not on the wire (the snapshot budget is full): at a reconcile the client derives it from the
record's item cooldown (below); others' stims are shown from their slim Throwing flag and the scoreboard's equipment byte (protocol 40). Every effect is server-side.

### Time-faithful capture and the smoothed render clock (M40 T0, T2; client only, not simulated)

From the M40 audit (its section 2 and finding D7; the audit report is not in the repository): Movie Maker footage of live play was not real time (the network
clock follows the wall clock, Godot time advances 1/30 s per frame: 0.56x to 20x), and remote players stepped at the 20 Hz snapshot
rate. Code: `SmNet/Demo.cs`, `SmNet/DemoPlayback.cs`, `SmNet/RenderClock.cs`, `client/NetworkView.Demo.cs`, hooks in `SmNet/GameClient.cs` and
`client/NetworkView.cs`. The simulation and the protocol are untouched. **All of it is a client capture / presentation aid, ours (no original
behaviour is involved).**

| Parameter (M40) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Demo file** (`--record-demo <file>`) | magic `SMDEMO\0\0`, format version 1, protocol version, config hash, content fingerprint, nonce, tick rate, a reserved empty map-name field (the map is named by the first packet, the Challenge), then records: packet (every received datagram with its arrival time), input (every sampled input per tick, before `Sanitized`), view (yaw and pitch per frame), session (player id, handshake round trip), end. Times are the recording client's clock. A cut-off file (killed recorder) ends at its last complete record. About 11 KB/s (a 60 s, 4-player Manufactorum match: 0.65 MB). Relative names go under the private data folder. **Recording safety (review S3, S4):** a path inside the repository or the game install is refused, links resolved (junctions and symbolic links, component by component) and the repository found both from `res://` and from the running code (a Movie Maker shadow project lives in the cache), case-insensitive; the file is created with `CreateNew` (never truncates or writes through an existing file or link); a path, create or write error (disk full ...) is logged once and recording stops, the client plays on (the packet is still handed over, nothing is allocated for later records). **Reading (review S2):** a file over 2 GB is refused before it is read; records whose time is not a finite number in [0, 1e7 s] or goes back before the previous record, views with non-finite angles, sessions with a round trip outside 0..60 s, and packets over 65535 bytes are dropped (counted in `Demo.DroppedRecords`; a bad End record leaves the file flagged cut off); playback indexes inputs in O(n log n) however the ticks are ordered. **Privacy:** a demo holds every other player's state, appearance codes and custom emblem images the client received; keep demos private and do not share them without thinking. A new `PlayerInput` field needs a format bump (a test compares `Demo.InputFields` with the type) | s | per packet, tick, frame | `SmNet/Demo.cs` | ours | implemented, tested (`DemoTests`) | high |
| **Replay** (`--play-demo <file>`, no server) | a client on the recorded packets with the demo clock set from Godot's frame time (`DemoPlayback.Advance`); inputs answered by tick (the nearest earlier one if a tick is missing, idle before the first); the recorded view; the recorded Welcome rewritten so that the client measures the recorded handshake round trip (so it starts predicting from the same tick). Before the first frame the client takes the Challenge (loads the map) and waits for the background loads, so no movie frame is spent on loading. The run ends after the recorded duration (the last frame is the one whose span reaches the end) and quits (`--demo-no-quit`); prints a DEMO-REPLAY line. Camera and HUD options (`--spectate`, `--no-hud` ...) apply | s | per frame | `SmNet/DemoPlayback.cs`, `NetworkView.Demo.cs` | ours | implemented; engine-free test: a 20 s session recorded at 1 ms steps and replayed at 1/30 s ends at tick 604 vs 605 and 0.17 m from the recording client, render tick 596.75 vs 596.80 | high |
| Replay fidelity | what is not reproduced: the client's own sends (Hello, Setup, appearance queries, emblem pulls) are dropped, so in the protocol 22 flows the replayed client never asks for others' appearances or emblems, and the recorded answers (appearance versions, emblem chunks) arrive at times that may not match what the replayed client expects and can be rejected: footage can show the fallback badge instead of a custom emblem, frame-quantized packet delivery (a packet arrives at the first frame at or after its recorded time: up to one frame late), the recorded stalls of the recording client. `--connect` flags that shape the session (class, loadout, side) are in the recorded packets, not applied again | — | — | — | — | implemented but untested for emblems | medium |
| Movie Maker acceptance (`movie.cmd --movie-size 1920x1080 --write-movie x.avi --fixed-fps 30 --position -4000,-4000 --play-demo f --test-window`) | the AVI holds exactly the demo's duration in frames (60.007 s demo: 1800 frames at 30 fps, 0 pre-roll frames); the server clock (render tick) advances 1.0004 to 1.0018 s per demo second and the match clock counts down 56.833 s over 56.767 s of demo time (the span between the first snapshot and the end; a 4-player Manufactorum demo, 1920x1080, 342 MB AVI; a steady remote runner: step / frame time CV 0.7 % and 1.3 %; the own marine 2.5 to 6.7 %, the high one with wall stops while the sim speed reads 10 m/s) | frames, s/s | per frame | measured (`DEMO-REPLAY`, `--motion-probe`) | ours | measured (`DEMO-REPLAY`) | high |
| **Smoothed render clock** (`SmNet/RenderClock.cs`) | the server tick remote players, projectiles, detonations and shots are shown at advances by the update's elapsed time and follows the raw estimate (newest snapshot's tick + time since it was processed - interpolation delay) with a correction proportional to the error (time constant **0.5 s**) and at most **5 %** of the step, so it runs at 0.95 to 1.05 of real time and never backwards; **divergence cap (review S1):** it never trails the raw estimate by more than **0.1 s (3 ticks)** (it jumps forward to that distance) and never runs ahead of it by more than **0.2 s** (it waits), because a 5 % slew alone could leave the view tick 6 to 12 ticks behind the raw estimate for seconds after a latency spike and below the server's lag-compensation floor (the acknowledged snapshot minus 7 ticks), which clamps it and loses hits on moving targets (`ViewTickBoundTests`: with the cap 0 of 782 inputs below the floor, at most 5 ticks behind; without it 59, up to 11); an error beyond **0.5 s** (the first snapshot, a stall) is taken at once. Fixed within one update (it used to move between calls in a frame). `--old-render-clock` restores the per-snapshot anchoring (before / after numbers) | s, factor | per client update | `GameClient.StepRenderClock` | ours | provisional approximation (constants chosen, not tuned further) | medium |
| Render clock, engine-free test | jittered arrivals (0 to 12 ms) with a 120 ms late packet every 5 s over 60 s at 60 fps: step / real time 0.950 to 1.048, never backwards; the raw estimate's worst step was 800 % off real time; in a client on a jittery link (40 ms +-25 ms, 2 % loss) the shown tick moves 0.950 to 1.050 of real time per 60 Hz frame, the old clock -1.9 to +3.7 | factor | per frame | `RenderClockTests` | ours | tested | high |
| Remote displacement, replay (same recording, 60 fps, headless `--fixed-fps 60`) | a steady runner at 10 m/s, coefficient of variation of step / frame time: **new clock 2.8 %, old clock 24.7 %** (own marine 3.3 % in both) | % | per frame | `--motion-probe` | ours | measured | high |
| Remote displacement, live (headless `--max-fps 60`, flat ground, a `--bot-gait` runner at 4.5 m/s, one observer with each clock, same server) | **new clock 3.0 %, old clock 35.2 %** | % | per frame | `--motion-probe` | ours | measured | medium (one run; combat runs on Manufactorum gave 4.5 to 8 % new, 35 to 40 % old, the new ones including knockbacks and reactions) |

### Cameras that never clip or cut (M40-T6; client only, not simulated)

Replaces the single-ray, instant pull-in follow camera (M19) and the collision-free spectator views. Everything here is ours: the
original's camera collision (the rig's `resolves camera collision`, see above) is not decoded. Code: `client/NetworkView.Spectate.cs`
(sphere cast, damped pull-in, body push-out, spring, `FollowCamera`, `SpectateFollow`), `NetworkView.Camera.cs` (rig), `NetworkView.Death.cs`
(death camera), probe `NetworkView.CameraProbe.cs`. The casts see both collision meshes of `CollisionWorld` (the shots' and the
characters' layer), which hold the level's collision layers and the M39 props (the green ammo crates and door buttons); a prop with no
collision shape in the install's data, such as the overhead girder in the audit frame, is in neither mesh and not seen.

| Soft / hard radius | soft 0.28 (what the camera tries to keep clear); hard 0.13 (never violated: the near plane's frustum corner is 0.065 to 0.082 m from the camera at near 0.05, fov 40 to 65, 16:9; margin included) | m | per frame | `CameraSoftRadius`, `CameraHardRadius` | ours; near plane 0.05 m is the client's | provisional | — |

### The follow camera at walls and in the hop (camera/hop-and-walls; client only, not simulated)

### Lighting overhaul and god-ray blending (M42; client only, not simulated)

The owner's request (2026-10-28): blend the god rays in and give the map a modern lighting pass "in the vein of WoW Forever's overhaul of
WoW Classic", keeping the original's art direction (a smoky, warm-cold imperial forge world). This is a **deliberate upgrade beyond the
original renderer** (docs/changes-from-original.md section 1). Code: `client/FxBatch.cs` (card fades), `client/MapLightingView.cs`
(preset, shadows, fog, sky, grade), `client/RenderQuality.cs` (argument logging), `client/ModelViewer.cs` (anti-aliasing for every view).
`--lighting off|low|medium|high` (default **medium**: it fits unknown GPUs; high is opt-in; off = the M40-T7 look; `--look classic` = before T7), `--fx-hard` draws the effect cards without
the fades, `--look-set key=value,...` overrides any constant below by its key (logged once: applied keys and ignored ones). Every value is
**ours** (a choice) unless the source column names the data.

| Parameter (M42) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Effect-card soft particles** | the quad fades where it nears the scene behind it (depth buffer, Forward+ reconstruction) over 0.3 x its fade size (clamped 0.05-2.5 m); fade size = the short side of a quad more than 3 x longer than wide (tracers, beams), else the long side. Phased in between fade sizes 1 and 2.5 m (smaller sprites: none, so impacts, sparks and muzzle flashes are untouched); except for god rays the comparison starts 0.75 x the soft distance in front of the quad, so a large sprite flush with a wall (impacts and blasts sit 0.02 m off it) keeps most of its opacity; flat rings (ground shockwaves, M41) have none. The kind of quad comes from the effect element (`FxBatch.QuadKind`: camera billboard, axis billboard, flat card, flat ring, god ray) | m | per frame | `FxBatch` shader (`SoftK/Min/Max`, `SoftPush`), `FxPlayer` | ours | choice | provisional |

### Clip entry cross-fade (M40-T3; client only, not simulated)

From the M40 audit (defect D5): when a clip took over from another clip or from the stance blends (reaction, charge, melee step, jump, roll,
toss), the pose changed in one frame (bots, 80 s, headless at 60 fps: 66 of 69 and 71 of 74 clip entries turned a bone by more than 25 degrees
in one frame, median 102 degrees, up to 180). `CharacterViewer.Play` / `Pose` now cross-fade from a snapshot of the pose shown at the entry
(rotation slerp, translation and scale lerp, per bone the new clip drives) over a blend time of real time; the clip's own time may be driven
from outside meanwhile (`Pose`). Stance-to-stance and clip-to-stance fades are unchanged (`Stance`, `StanceFadeSeconds`); the reload / recoil
pose layers are applied after the fade as before. `ClipBlends` holds the times; the callers pass them. Nothing here changes the simulation or the protocol.

Which transition belongs to the client's stun / stagger / interrupt / blast clips: our mapping | graph (value), interpretation (mapping) | medium |
| Charge entry blend | 0.1 | s | per entry | `ClipBlends.Rush` | `SM_Base_MP`: bull-rush states are entered by "Default 3 Frame Transition" (344 of the base graph's transitions; the death state's `Bullrush Death` too) | graph (value), interpretation (mapping) | medium |

The live list goes out in a tick where it changed, an event happened or a client joined, and every 30 ticks (1 s) while pickups lie or a change is under 60 ticks old; events every 3 ticks while under 30 ticks old, without the list in between. Clients keep the newest list minus the pickups removed by later events, hand each event out once (by sequence), queue at most 256 (the oldest go), drop the events of the first message they accept (a late joiner does not replay the last second) and drop events while the view is not loaded. Measured (synthetic, PickupTests): 64 lying and nothing changing 5 messages in 5 s, 775 bytes/s per client; worst case, one drop per tick over a full world (a list and an event every tick), 30 messages/s, 29 970 bytes/s per client, largest message 1031 bytes. Collections and drops only in warm-up and play (and the tick a match ends); expiry always. only when the work is done. Everything is ours (a performance choice, not an original rule). Code: `client/NetworkView.Prewarm.cs` (budget, weapon
models, collision, ragdoll, animation prefetch), `client/JitPrewarm.cs`, `client/MarineAssets.cs` (animation table), `client/NetworkView.Death.cs`,
`client/FrameProfile.cs` (the measuring aid), `NetworkView.cs` (a few call sites). `--no-hitch-fixes` switches the spreading and the warm-ups off in the same build; it is not byte-identical to the build before T9 (the reused sets and lists, the finer phase marks and the shared animation table stay on).

### Responsive controls (feel/controls; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the owner (2026-10-29): "responsiveness of controls, smoothness of visuals"; earlier: "everything about character motion and movement still feels
janky". Measured first with `--latency-probe` (a human client, headless; the script's key, mouse-button and mouse-motion events go through Godot's own
input queue and are delivered at the next frame like a device's). Findings: the 30 Hz input sample read the buttons held, so a press and release between
two samples was lost (15 to 16 of 16 one-frame clicks, every one-frame melee tap; 40 ms presses lost now and then when a frame stalled); a press waited
for the next scheduled tick (0 to 33 ms, jitter of the same size); the converged shot used the camera as the previous frame placed it (5.1 degrees
behind the crosshair at 60 fps and 300 degrees a second, 2.2 at 144 fps); the own attack clips were posed at the tick-stepped timers (the drawn time
stood still in 50 % of the frames at 60 fps, 76 % at 144). Not ours to change and untouched: the data's raise delay before the first shot, the melee
clips' timings, the reload times, the jump pack's take-off delay. The mouse look was already right: the view turns in the frame the motion arrives (no
smoothing, no tick quantization; the simulation's yaw follows at the next tick, the own model is drawn at the view's, M36). Code:
`SmNet/ControlFeel.cs` (rules, tested in `ControlFeelTests`), `SmNet/GameClient.cs` (`Update(.., tickNow)`, `DrawPair`, `ClipFraction`),
`client/NetworkView.Controls.cs`, `client/NetworkView.LatencyProbe.cs` (test aid). Each change can be switched off for before / after comparisons;
`--old-controls` switches off all five (with the camera casts' origin, below).

Two whole taps of one button within one tick count as one. `--no-tap-latch` reads the buttons held as before | ticks | per input sample | `SmNet.InputLatch`, `NetworkView.LatchButtons` | ours | ours | high (tested) |
| **Client: early tick** | a press or release of a game button or a movement key (W A S D) runs the next client tick in the frame the event arrives, when no scheduled tick ran in that frame (it already sampled the edge) and the client is not already a tick ahead of its schedule (early ticks can follow one another, one per scheduled tick); the input keeps its tick number, the simulation steps one tick for it, the server applies it at that tick, and the next tick is due at its own scheduled time (the client is at most one tick ahead of its schedule; the input lead steering is unchanged). Human players only (not bots, not replayed demos). its frame queue) adds one or more frames after the feedback frame; `--disable-vsync` or Godot's `--max-fps` before `--` are the engine's own switches
for a lower-latency check. The two-taps-within-one-tick limit and the run start's position (drawn on the schedule) are the remaining ours rules above.

### In-game HUD (M44; client only, not simulated)

The owner asked for the in-game HUD to look like the original and for the jump pack meter to move under the weapon box. Layout values are
measured on the owner's gameplay footage (800 x 450 captures of a 1600 x 900 view, so 1 frame pixel = 2.4 units of our 1080-high virtual
space; reference frames kept outside the repository, never committed). The pictures are the original's: the Scaleform exporter left the
in-game movie's bitmaps as DDS next to `Hud.gfx` in `data/packages/ui_ingame.oppc` (`SmContent.UiArt`, rectangles in `HudSprites`; the movie
itself, which places them, is not read). Everything is drawn in the 1080-high space scaled by the window height; the panels are anchored to
their corners, the bar and the cards to the centre (1280 x 720, 1600 x 900, 1920 x 1080 and 2560 x 1080 checked by screenshot).

### World decorators and the kill feed's pictures (fidelity gap 10; client only, not simulated)

The original draws indicators over players and control points in the world and a weapon picture in each kill-feed line. Their movies are in the
install (`Decorator.gfx` in `ui_common.oppc`, `HudEventLog.gfx` in `ui_ingame.oppc`); what they contain was read by walking their tags (names, frame
labels, timelines, bitmap rectangles; no ActionScript decompiled): docs/discovery.md "HUD indicators". The engine code that decides **when** a decorator
shows and **which** state it takes is not in the data, so those rules are ours or interpretations of the state names. Nothing here changes the
simulation or the protocol (`SmContent.FeedIcons`, `DecoratorSprites`, `DecoratorRules`, `HudRules.FeedLabel`; `client/HudDecorators.cs`,
`NetworkView.Match.cs`). `--show-markers` brings back the old placeholder name tags and side rings (test aid); `--no-markers` still hides them.

### HUD from the movies (ui/hud-fidelity; client only, not simulated)

The owner asked for crosshairs identical to the original and for a true-replication pass on the HUD against the reference footage (owner, 2026-10-29). The original HUD is a
set of Scaleform movies in the install: `Hud.gfx` (reticles, hit marker, weapon box, reward lines), `HudText.gfx` (the versus score panel, the interaction prompt) and
`HudEventLog.gfx` (the kill feed) in `data/packages/ui_ingame.oppc`, `Decorator.gfx` (control point decorators) in `ui_common.oppc`. The client reads them at runtime
(read-only, nothing extracted or cached: `SmContent.HudMovies`) and draws their pieces with the engine-free renderer (`GfxRaster`, now with clip layers and images placed as
characters), at the movies' own places (stage 1280 x 720 scaled by the window height), with the text fields' own sizes, alignment and colours (`GfxMovie.EditTexts`; our font,
Bahnschrift, stands in for "Bourgeois") and the clips' own frames at 30 fps. No action (ActionScript) is read. What the movies leave to their scripts is measured on the
reference footage (640 x 360 copy of a 2011 match video, frames kept outside the repository) or ours. `--old-hud` draws the M44 HUD (before / after);
`smtool gfx-dump <game-dir|auto> [--movie m] [--package common] [--grep w] [--frames sprite] [--path a/b --frame n --out dir]` prints and renders the movies' structure.

### Locomotion blend space (M40-T4; client only, not simulated)

From the M40 audit (defect D4): a moving marine showed one discrete clip, the nearest of eight directions in one speed band (M36, M27), so
between two directions' headings the feet slid by up to half the speed (planted-foot speed median 1.2 to 1.4 m/s at the headings between the clip
directions, steps of 30 to 45 cm), and the clip flickered when the heading reversed. Now the relaxed run, the ready (hip-fire) run and the sprint
are a **blend** of the neighbouring clips with weights from the ground velocity, phase-synced by the feet, with the legs corrected where the
blend bends them. **The sprint is not blended by default** (review S1): on the first sweep demos its standing foot slid more than the old three-way blend, so it keeps the
M36 blend; `--gait-sprint` turns the gait blend on for it (a **regression** there until it measures no worse). Same for the own marine and remote ones (it needs only the state's velocity, facing and pitch). Nothing here changes the
simulation or the protocol. Code: `SmContent/ClipGait.cs`, `GaitBlend.cs`, `GaitLibrary.cs` (engine-free; tests `tests/SmNet.Tests/GaitBlendTests.cs`,
synthetic numbers only), `client/NetworkView.GaitBlend.cs`, `CharacterViewer.cs` (`BlendStance`), `CharacterViewer.LegIk.cs`, `NetworkView.Locomotion.cs`,
`NetworkView.HipFire.cs`. `--no-gait-blend` (test aid) restores the M36 / M27 nearest-clip poses, `--no-leg-ik` the plain rotation blend, `--gait-sprint` blends the sprint too, `--log-footsteps` prints the footstep tags that fire. The M36 rows
"which clip shows (relaxed)", "which clip shows (sprint)" for the clip choice and "playback rate" are replaced by the rows below whenever the gait data is
loaded (they remain the fallback). The graphs blend these clips continuously too (`FLT_Nav_Motion_Angle_DAMPED`, `FLT_Input_Nav_Speed_DAMPED`,
`FLT_Nav_Motion_Angle_SPRINT_DAMP`); what the original's blend does with its sync events and variables is not decoded, so everything below that is not a
clip's measured number is **interpretation**.

| Parameter (M40-T4) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |

Pose only: the movement, the camera and the simulation are not delayed. Cause it fixes: a reversal (strafe, forward / back, diagonal) takes the damped velocity through zero, where its heading turns 180 degrees between two frames, so the weights flipped to the opposite direction's clips in one frame (the idle share below 0.35 / 1 m/s covered one to three frames). `--old-gait-snap` restores the old flip. The share is the blend layers' fade, so cross-fades from other stances ease in. While one clip plays the correction is 0.2 cm on average. Not the ground-adaptive foot IK of the audit's T11 | m | per frame | `CharacterViewer.LegIk.cs` | choice: ours | interpretation | medium |

| Demo | Planted-foot speed median, worst heading (m/s) | Step slide median, worst heading (cm) | All steady frames: speed median / step median (m/s, cm) | Clip changes during steady strafing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 142 s relaxed run, before | 1.24 | 37.3 | 0.68 / 14.2 | 16 in 53 s |
| 142 s, after | **0.28** | **11.8** | 0.21 / 4.3 | 3 in 53 s |
| 75 s ready run, before | 1.14 | 40.0 | 0.67 / 15.8 | 8 in 26 s |
| 75 s ready run, after | **0.29** | **14.9** | 0.20 / 4.1 | 2 in 26 s |

| 75 s, after | 0.30 (22.5 degrees, 63 frames; the others 0.17 to 0.29) | **12.8** | 0.23 / 4.6 | 1 in 26 s |

The other weapon families (75 s demos, shots every 3 s): **heavy bolter** (`--class devastator`, always ready; its ready run has four directions 90 degrees apart) before 3.20 m/s and 71 cm at the worst heading, after 0.40 m/s and 19.5 cm (worst at the back and the back diagonals; all steady frames 1.13 to 0.26 m/s, steps 32.4 to 3.9 cm); **pistol** (`--class tactical --bot-slot pistol`) before 1.16 m/s and 34.1 cm, after 1.07 m/s (135 degrees only: the pistol's back-right run clip has stretches where the foot stands still against the body while the body moves, so no single stride fits it; every other heading 0.17 to 0.40) and 16.0 cm (180 degrees; all steady frames 0.71 to 0.29 m/s, steps 20.9 to 5.4 cm). Not met for those two families.

**Cost** (sixteen headless sweep bots on one machine against one server, 60 s, the measured client logs `--anim-probe --frame-stats`; every client runs the same code, so the machine is saturated and the frame times are noisy): the characters' pose work per rendered frame (stances, clip samples, leg correction; 16 marines drawn) median 0.52 ms, mean 0.67, p99 2.77, worst 97.0 before (`--no-gait-blend`) and median 1.30, mean 1.53, p99 6.82, worst 96.2 after (about 0.07 ms more per moving marine and frame); frame time median 6.90 / 6.94 ms, p99 36.1 / 32.2, p99.9 121 / 76, worst 140 / 122 before / after, i.e. no difference the noise does not hide. The 97 ms worst pose frame is in both runs (a first-use hitch outside this work). Samples of a frame use one buffer (no allocation per clip); the clips the worker decoded are handed to the rig cache instead of decoded again on the main thread.

Without the leg correction (`--no-leg-ik`, 142 s demo) the worst heading is 1.05 m/s and 56 cm, the toe sinks to -8 cm (after: -1.8 cm; before: -16 cm, from the old
stance cross-fades). With the toe alone as the planted test (stricter on the toe roll: it counts the toe-pivot at the end of a stance) the worst heading is 0.29 to
0.33 m/s and 17.5 to 25.3 cm. The noise of the measure is about 0.03 m/s and 1 to 2 cm (re-tuning the stride estimate moved the demos by that much). The measure's
floor is about 0.2 m/s: the toe rolls and the drawn body moves in 60 Hz steps.

Not met or not better: the **sprint** with `--gait-sprint` (planted-foot speed of the standing part of the stance 0.37 m/s against 0.17 to 0.28 before; the sprint's flat foot lasts 4 to 6
frames, and the swing foot grazes the ground at up to 20 m/s for 1 to 2 frames of every step in both versions, which the height test counts as planted, so its step slides
are 30 to 34 cm in both) is therefore off by default: the shipped sprint is the M36 blend, 0.21 m/s against 0.20 on the 142 s demo; the **dominant clip** changes more often (flip-flops 52 against 14 in the 142 s demo, 31 against 1 to 4 in the shorter ones: at a reversal the
walk and run weights of the same direction cross as the speed passes through zero; the pose between them is continuous, the stances were not); the largest
one-frame bone turns are the clips' authored loop seams on the prop bones `RIG_Prop_M_Rhand` / `RIG_Prop_LHand` (112 / 113 degrees once per cycle before and after; the
weapon mount bones are `RIG_Prop_M_Chest` and `RIG_Prop_LHand`: the left-hand seam that fired 52 times before fires 0 times now). Knee angles while moving are unchanged
(median 118 against 120 degrees, 1st percentile 52 against 49, 99th 152 against 157). Aim-walk (Left Ctrl) is still the nearest of its eight clips.

### Action clips hand the legs to the locomotion (M40-T4 follow-up; client only, not simulated)

From the owner's live playtest: after an F stun strike, when the player moved again as soon as allowed, the character slid along the ground. The simulation lets the
player move while some actions are still playing; the clips are whole-body and stand in place. Sweep of every action (a bot doing each in turn with the stick held
forward, `--action-sweep`, then `--anim-probe`'s action table on a recorded demo, before = `--no-handoff`): the melee attacks from their `MoveAt` and the grenade
throw were the only ones that kept the whole body under a moving marine. Code: `client/NetworkView.Handoff.cs`, a few lines in `NetworkView.cs` `Place`
(the attack and the throw call `HandoffAttack` / `HandoffThrow` before posing the clip), `NetworkView.HipFire.cs` (the cross-fade override), the probe in `AnimProbe.cs`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Without the mask (the hip-fire data not loaded yet, `--no-hip-fire`, a family without a reload blend) nothing is handed over and the whole-body clip shows as before; the body must be alive, grounded and not in a jump-pack phase. The clip's tag sounds keep firing from its own time (`SoundLayerTags`). Rules: `SmNet.ActionHandoff` (tested). Covers light steps, combo ends, heavy and stun strikes | s, m/s | per frame | `NetworkView.HandoffAttack` | data (`MoveAt`), the rest ours | data (when), interpretation (how) | medium |
| Hand-off of a grenade throw | the throw never locks movement: from the first moving frame (> 0.5 m/s, grounded) the toss clip is an upper-body layer over the locomotion (weight in over 0.1 s when the throw starts moving, out over the last 0.15 s of `ThrowDuration`) | s | per frame | `NetworkView.HandoffThrow` | choice: ours | interpretation | medium |

The probe's table: per action clip that still shows (a clip drives the pose, or lies over the locomotion as the upper-body layer) while the body moves (>= 1.5 m/s over 0.1 s): clip frames, seconds moving, longest run, planted-foot (flat) slide median and p90 | m/s, s | per frame | `NetworkView.ActionSweep.cs`, `AnimProbe.cs` | test aid | - | - |

### Turn in place, aim-offset idle, stop foot pins and run start (M40-T5; client only, not simulated)

From the M40 audit (defects D8 and D9): a standing marine's body took the view's yaw at once (180 degrees in one frame on a flick), its idle was one clip that ignored the aim, a
stop was the run cycle cross-fading into the idle (the planted foot slid 22 to 37 cm) and a start the idle cross-fading into the walk and run blend. Now (the same for the own marine
and remote ones; the simulation, the hit volumes, the shots and the camera keep the view's yaw; **owner's decision still pending: the shown body may lag the aim**) the graphs' own
turn, aim-offset and start states are read (`smtool graph-dump --turns`, `SmContent.TurnAnimations`; engine-free rules `SmNet.BodyYaw`, `SmNet.AimOffsetGrid`, `SmContent.StartMatch`;
tests `TurnInPlaceTests`, `TurnAnimationsTests`) and the client drives them (`NetworkView.TurnInPlace.cs`, `NetworkView.RunStart.cs`, `CharacterViewer.Turn.cs`,
`CharacterViewer.FootPin.cs`). Test aids: `--no-turns` (the old rigid body and single idle; also turns off the pins and the start), `--no-foot-pins`, `--no-run-start`,
`--bot-turn-sweep` (with `--bot --bot-gait`; `--turn-sweep-fire` keeps the weapon up), `--anim-probe` (adds `TurnProbe`: body yaw per frame, planted-foot slide after stops and starts,
barrel against the aim; `--turn-probe-events`, `--turn-probe-trace <s>`), `--run-start-log`.

The weights are the two neighbouring columns by the angle and in each the two neighbouring clips by the pitch, linear (`AimOffsetGrid`; Havok's blender normalises the same two children). The pistol ("Twist Idle") and the heavy bolter ("Heavy Idle") have only the pitch clips (`SM_1HR_NAV_IdleL_S_*`, `SM_NAV_TB_Idle_S_*`) and a twist modifier bound to the clamped horizontal angle: done here as a rotation of `RIG_SpineA` (40 %) and `RIG_SpineD` (60 %) about the vertical axis, up to 90 degrees. Measured barrel against the aim while standing (rifle, headless bot, 0 to 90 degrees off the body): median 1.1 to 2.5 degrees (the old ready idle 0.5; the old relaxed idle 48: `SM_NAV_IdleL_S_01` carries the rifle low) | degrees | per frame | `TurnStandPlace`, `AimOffsetGrid` | graphs (clips, angles, pitch keys); the linear weights, the twist split and its limit: ours | data (clips, keys), interpretation (weights, twist) | medium |
