### Fall pose, hard landing, walk-on-the-spot and the layer stack (animation pass 1; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the animation audit of 2026-10-28 (items 1, 5 and 10, and its shared prerequisite) and the owner's description ("in sm1 when a player walks off a ledge he drops as if gravity pulls
him straight down, with a falling animation"). Until now a marine that left the ground kept its run or idle pose for the whole fall and snapped on landing, the zero-speed end of the relaxed
speed blend was the idle pose and the client had one extra pose layer. Now (the same for the own marine and remote ones; the simulation, the hit volumes and the shots are not touched; the
simulation still keeps horizontal speed in a fall, a separate task will change that, and the pose looks right either way because it does not show the horizontal speed in the air):
the fall, its landing and the exits are read from the navigation graphs (`smtool graph-dump --falls`, `SmContent.FallAnimations`, `FallLanding`, `FallRules`; tests
`FallAnimationsTests`, `GaitBlendTests` (walk on the spot)), the client drives them (`NetworkView.Fall.cs`, `NetworkView.GaitBlend.cs`) over a **pose layer stack**
(`CharacterViewer.Layers.cs`). Test aids: `--no-fall-pose`, `--no-wos`, `--no-layer-stack` (every layer back into the one action slot), `--log-fall` (the events and the layers' weights),
`--fall-hard-speed <m/s>` (lowers the rifle's hard-landing speed for tests), `--bot-ledge [--ledge-min-drop m]` (with `--bot --bot-gait`: a bot that plans a straight run off a ledge with the
real movement function, runs it and plans again from where it lands), `--wait-fall` / `--wait-fall-land` (screenshot at 0.35 s into a fall / 0.1 s into the landing clip), `--pose-hash <file>`
(a hash of every drawn character's bones per frame, to compare two builds on one demo replay).

### Weapon switch, hit flinch, death hit and the jump pack's upper body (animation pass 2; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the animation audit of 2026-10-28, using the pass-1 layer stack's free slots. Until now a weapon switch showed no body motion (the model changed in the hand half way through the simulation's
switch time), a non-lethal hit showed nothing on the victim, a kill turned the body into a ragdoll in the pose it died in, the jump pack's flight was a single posed clip and the pound's get-up was the
standing one. Now (the same for the own marine and remote ones; the simulation, hit volumes, shots and the protocol are not touched): the clips are read from the base graph `SM_Base_MP` and the jump pack graph
`MP_SM_NAV_JP_Sim` (`smtool graph-dump --upper`, `SmContent.UpperBodyBundle`: `SwitchAnimations`, `FlinchAnimations`, `DeathAnimations`, `JumpPackAnimations`; engine-free rules `FlinchRules`, `DeathRules`; tests
`UpperBodyAnimationsTests`), the client plays them (`NetworkView.UpperBody.cs`, `NetworkView.Jump.cs`, `WeaponRig.Update`) on three more layer slots (`PoseSlots.Switch` 3, `Flinch` 4, `Wobble` 5; a layer laid
over a clip shown by `Pose()` is now applied again, `CharacterViewer._layersDirty`, and a layer can be a whole-pose clip taken as the offset from its own pose at a reference time). Test aids: `--no-switch-anim`,
`--no-flinch`, `--no-death-anim`, `--no-jump-upper` (each restores the pass-1 behaviour; with all four the pass-1 pose stream is reproduced), `--log-upper` (the events; bots print them anyway).

The clip waits up to 0.15 s for the kill's cause (the kill feed may arrive after the death); meanwhile the body keeps its last pose, and the held body slides on with its last horizontal velocity decaying with a 0.2 s time constant (ours; a ray at chest height stops it at a wall), and the ragdoll starts with the decayed velocity. ### Hit reactions: the death clip by the graph's routes, blast deaths, the clip's motion into the ragdoll, flinch sets by the attacker (2026-11-11; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

The two "missing" items of the playtest list (death animations before the ragdoll, flinches) were drawn since animation pass 2 (section above; a headless bot duel on 2026-11-11 showed both working: `P1 dies: SM_REC_MP_BolterDeath_F_01 (DefaultFront) for 0.60 s`, `FLINCH ... Plasma Strong Flinch slot 5`). This pass replaces pass 2's guessed rules with what the base graph says (`smtool graph-dump --upper` prints all of it; engine-free rules `DeathRules`, `FlinchRules`, `WeaponReactions`, `DeathHandover` in `SmContent/UpperBodyAnimations.cs`; tests `HitReactionsTests`, `HitReactionNoBlockTests`; client `NetworkView.UpperBody.cs`, `Ragdoll.Start`). The respawn, the kill credit, the body's collision and every simulated reaction are unchanged: the death clip and the flinches are drawn only. Test aids: `--old-hit-reactions` (pass 2's rules), `--hit-reaction-test --hrt-case <case>` (a stage for clips: deaths and flinches with the same rules and data), `--log-upper`.

### The jump-pack death in mid-air (2026-11-11; client only, both modes' marine view, not simulated, no protocol change)

The owner (2026-11-11), asked whether to play it: "Yes". A marine killed in a jump-pack jump (the graph's `BOOL_JumpIsActive` at its last living frame: flight or dive, not the take-off; ROOT's priority-10 route) plays `SM_Base_MP`'s "Jumppack Death" before the ragdoll instead of going to the ragdoll at once. Read on the install (`smtool graph-dump --upper`, `graph-dump SM_Base_MP`; docs/discovery.md "Hit reactions" and "The jump-pack death in mid-air"). Engine-free rules `JumpDeathRules`, `JumpDeathRun` (`SmContent/JumpDeath.cs`, tests `JumpDeathTests`, 10 cases); client `NetworkView.JumpDeath.cs`, `NetworkView.DeathFx.cs` (`DeathBody`). The respawn, the kill credit, the body's collision and the server's simulation are unchanged: the dead body is placed and posed by each client only. Musou Mode's Ork deaths are not touched. Test aids: `--no-jump-death` (the ragdoll at once, its effects on the ragdoll: before), `--log-upper` (the phases), `--hit-reaction-test --hrt-case death-jump` (the stage, with the effects).

### Transitions, connecting clips, the heavy sprint and the pistol idle (animation pass 3; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the owner's playtest of 2026-10-29: "the falling animation is still not blending smoothly with the charge animation, or others for that matter"; "the assault marine and raptor have a weird idle
animation"; "we're missing 'connecting' animations ... it flicks between animation states in a jarring fashion"; "devastator/havoc needs to have a different sprint animation"; "when hopping and
sprinting a devastator/havok needs to keep his weapon in his hands"; "a 'slowdown' when you stop sprinting ... if movement keys are let go of entirely". The reference videos were not watched
(no video access here): the clips, blends and branches below are the install's behaviour graphs (`smtool graph-dump --sprint-edges`, `--pose-diff A B`; `SmContent.SprintTransitions`, tests
`SprintTransitionsTests`); the client plays them (`client/CharacterViewer.Transitions.cs`, `NetworkView.SprintEdges.cs`, `NetworkView.HeavyHold.cs`). Measured with a new probe (`--transition-probe`,
`client/TransitionProbe.cs`) on four recorded sessions (`--bot-gait --transition-sweep`, a bot that goes through the state switches: sprint and let go, run and let go, sprint then run on, roll, charge,
throw, melee, aim, switch, strafe, hop or jump; and `--bot-ledge --ledge-charge`, charges off ledges; Tactical, Devastator, Assault and a Chaos ledge bot, 150 s each) replayed headless at 60 fps,
`--no-p3` for the before. Test aids: `--no-p3` (every change of this section off), `--no-dead-blend`, `--dead-blend-decay <s>`, `--dead-blend-cap <deg/s>`, `--no-sprint-stop`, `--no-sprint-start`,
`--shared-sprint`, `--log-sprint-edges`, `--transition-probe [--transition-probe-csv <file>] [--transition-probe-trace <bone>]`, `--transition-sweep`, `--ledge-charge`.

### Install transitions the client did not play (polish item 10, 2026-11-12; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

The owner (2026-11-12): "i want to integrate the transition animations that you found before in the original game, that are not currently used in sm-reimpl. they are animations that play between actions or modes or
directions" (his earlier answer 2: "Yes, where the original wires them."). The clips and edges are the install's sprint graphs (`smtool graph-dump MP_SM_Bolter_NuSprint | SM_Heavy_Bolter_NuSprint | SM_Lascannon_Plasma_NuSprint |
SM_TH_NuSprint`, `--root-motion <clip>` now with the root's turn); the reading is `SmContent.SprintTransitions` (its `Interrupt`, `Turn`, `StartWindow` and the hammer's map), the rules are engine-free
(`SprintInterruptRules`, `SprintTurnTracker`, `SprintEdgeClip.TurnProgress`; tests `InstallTransitionsTests`), the client is `NetworkView.SprintEdges.cs` (Classic and Musou alike: Musou's own marines use the same
placement; its MW5 stance cross-fades are unchanged). Everything is decided from state the client already has (the predicted state for the own marine, the snapshot's for others: the simulation's sprint-stop flag, the
body's yaw against the aim, the speed), so nothing changes on a correction. `--no-extra-transitions` switches the section off; `--log-sprint-edges` prints each edge; `--transition-sweep` has three new legs.
Wired: the half-speed stop, the 180-degree turn into a sprint (rifle, pistol, heavy bolter and thunder hammer graphs; the cannons have none), the thunder hammer's sprint stop. Not wired, and why: see the last rows and
`docs/changes-from-original.md` section 3.

### Install transitions, pass 2 batch 1 (2026-11-12; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

The owner (2026-11-12): "start the work to add the transition animations that the original game had but we haven't deployed to sm-reimpl yet" (standing: "where the original wires them"). The full inventory of the
multiplayer content's transition clips, with the graph state, the condition and whether the client plays each, is `docs/transitions-inventory.md`. This batch wires three that the sim's state already triggers: the thunder
hammer's and the chainsword's drop and landing and the hammer's jump-pack landings (this is batch 1 of the second transitions pass; the hammer's air dash etc. are batch 2). `--no-extra-transitions` (the item 10 switch) restores the rifle's fall and the plain landings.

From the owner's requests of 2026-10-29: "Assault Hammer running animation missing"; the power sword and chainsword slash "feels quite janky ... copy the animation from sm1 better"; "add a tiny bit of screen shake to all stun strike moves"; the charge
landing off a ledge; "run a pass where the animations transition much more smoothly ... for all animations". The clips, blends and branches are the install's behaviour graphs (`smtool graph-dump --melee-flow`,
`--locomotion`; `SmContent.MeleeFlowBlends`, `LocomotionAnimations.Hammer`, tests `MeleeFlowTests`); the rules are engine-free (`SmNet.ClipFootLockRules`, `SlashPose`; tests `ClipFootLockRulesTests`); the client is

carried by the strike); no number was taken from it. Measured with `--anim-probe` and `--transition-probe` (new: `--transition-probe-clips` labels the melee and charge clips by name, so a combo's step to step
counts as a switch) on three recorded sessions replayed headless at 60 fps, `--no-melee-flow` for the before: `melee2` (six melee bots, chainsword, power sword and hammer on both sides, 150 s, bot views turning at

### The hammer's swings and air slash (anim/hammer-swing; the step is simulated, the legs and the air slash clip are client presentation)

From the owner's requests of 2026-11-01 (his knowledge of the original outranks our reading): "for Thunderhammer on Assault Marine and Raptor. The step forward distance for the standard melee swings needs to be reduced slightly,
maybe by 1 to 2 meters. You can also judge it. Also, the legs are doing really crazy things when you are doing the regular swings, in particular, continuing the combo. ... Your legs are still mostly rooted to the ground, so we need to do a animation and transition
blending pass"; "there needs to be a separate air slash landing for hammer ... the same move in terms of damage, stagger, visual effects, it just has a different player model animation". Measured with new test aids on a local server
(`--swing-test stand` with `--log-lunge --anim-probe --transition-probe --transition-probe-clips`: a bot swings X, X, X as each combo window opens, nobody in reach; `smtool melee-steps auto thunder_hammer`; `--slash-test`), a thunder hammer Assault, Manufactorum.
Code: `MeleeStep.LungeFactor`, `MeleeTuning.HammerLightLungeFactor`, `MeleeLock.LungeStep`; `CharacterViewer.ClipFootLock.cs` (`ClipStrideScale`), `NetworkView.HammerSwing.cs`; `SmNet.HammerSlashPose`; tests `HammerSwingTests`.

### Light-combo legs of the swords, axe and knife (night batch 2026-11-06, anim/sword-legs; client presentation)

The owner, 2026-11-06: "the 2nd attack in the power sword and likely chainsword light attack combo has weird leg movement. increase the stability of all the leg animations ... the hammer animations look great ... a good reference for how the legs should actually move".

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cause | The hammer's and the swords' legs take the same path (the clip's whole body, then the hand-over to the gait). The difference is the stride stretch (`CharacterViewer.ClipStrideScale`, anim/hammer-swing): the clip's feet are stretched along the heading by the body's travel over the clip's root motion. The hammer's is 1.12 (`smtool melee-steps`: "clip's motion x1.119"); the sword combos' is 2.925 (lunge scale 1.625 x the instant-step boost). At 2.9 the clip's swing leg is flung to the 0.95 reach cap: in the power sword's second swing (`SM_MEL_PA_XATK_Combo2MsA`) the left foot hung 45 to 63 cm above the ground, 1.1 m behind the body, for about 0.3 s, then went 1.5 m forward in five frames (`--leg-trace`, before) | x | per strike | `NetworkView.HammerStrideScale` | measured (`--leg-probe --leg-trace`) | measured | high |
| Fix | A light strike's stride factor exceeds 1 by at most **0.2** (`ClipFootLockRules.LightStrideExcessCap`, `StrideFactor`; `--stride-cap f`). The hammer (1.12) is untouched by construction; heavy and stun strikes keep their stretch; `--old-sword-legs` = before. The same legs path serves the chainsword, power sword, power axe, combat knife and the Chaos twins (all one-handed melee through `HammerStrideScale`) | factor - 1 | per light strike | `NetworkView.HammerSwing.cs` | ours | estimate (the hammer's own excess rounded up) | medium |
| Result | `--leg-probe` (below), medians over 4 to 5 strikes per cell, before -> after: leg-bone turn per 1/60 s, strike by strike: power sword 36 / 45 / 56 -> 34 / 27 / 42 deg; chainsword 47 / 59 / 49 -> 35 / 38 / 34; power axe 50 / 65 / 63 -> 37 / 35 / 38; knife 53 / 63 / 68 -> 33 / 31 / 49. Ankle jitter p99: power sword strike 2 33.7 -> 18.4; chainsword 32.0 / 35.7 / 24.5 -> 26.9 / 21.8 / 21.0. Planted-foot slide rose (power sword 21 -> 70 cm, chainsword 147 -> 239 cm in strike 2): the feet now glide with the body as the hammer's do (the hammer's slide is 530 to 640 cm) instead of being held and flung | cm, deg | per strike | `client/LegProbe.cs` | measured | measured | medium (a loaded machine, 30 to 60 frames per strike resampled to 60 Hz) |

Measurement aid `--leg-probe` (`client/LegProbe.cs`, headless; `--leg-trace` prints each frame of the first two strikes of each kind): per strike of every drawn character, resamples the skeleton's feet to 60 Hz and reports the planted-foot slide (toe within 3 cm and ankle within 24 cm of the ground), the largest planted step, the ankle's jitter (second difference in the body frame) and the largest leg-bone turn. Run: `godot.cmd --max-fps 60 -- --connect 127.0.0.1:<p> --bot --class assault --melee <weapon> --swing-test stand --leg-probe`. Not verified by a human: the look.

is inert (`stun_threshold` 1e6; M28). Hit reactions and heavy strikes: section "Hit reactions" (M28).

Notes (from the extraction report; **interpretations** are marked):
- Each `do_damage` also has `damage_armourshield` (extra damage to the regenerating armour shield, **interpretation**),
  per-material multiplier tables (e.g. bolter head ×2.55, heavy armour ×0.5) and piecewise range fall-off.
- Perk files grant only an upgrade name; the weapon file holds alternative entries keyed to it. **Interpretation**: the
  most specific satisfied entry replaces the default (e.g. thunder hammer 200 → 2000 with its AoE perk; knife 40 → 65).
- Spread comes from `climb_sway_scatter` sets per stance (standing / aiming / crouching) and movement (idle / walking /
  running); bolter hip fire: scatter 0.25 initial, +0.35 per shot, max 1.5, recovery 2.4 per second after 0.1 s (applied since
  weapons/spread, the owner's decision of 2026-10-28; see "Weapon spread").
- Only one weapon-driven movement change was found: plasma cannon charging, `speed_maximum` ×0.5.
- Bolter as used (M6, `GameplayTuning.WithWeapon`, default entries): `damage_general` 22; health multipliers
  `damage_material_multipliers/default_body` 1 and `default_head` 2.55; shield multipliers
  `armourshield_damage_material_multipliers/default_body` 0.505 and `default_head` 0.5; `damage_fall_off` points
  (0, ×1), (45, ×1), (70, ×0.8). Hit-zone names (head, body, arms, legs) map hitbox bodies; the shapes are Havok data not
  decoded yet.
- Melee combo windows and hit frames: decoded for the combat knife (table above, M9), the chainsword (M28) and the power sword, power axe, thunder hammer and the heavy classes' kick and stomp (Weapons C, section below).
- Open: how unconditional and per-upgrade damage combine in
  Exterminatus, the meaning of `shot_cooldown` vs `time_between_shots`, and whether `_old` abilities are dead.

### Melee target lock, alignment and lunge (feel/melee-lock; used by the simulation; protocol 32)

From the owner (2026-10-29, the owner's knowledge of SM1): "target locking for melee attacks. when initiating a melee attack or charge or f stun strike,
if the character model is moving in the general direction of an enemy player model they 'stick' to it and line up to keep delivering more melee
attacks. also in general there should be a bit of 'stickiness' to the gameplay ... also, you should step forward when swinging your melee weapon or
combat knife". The data has the parts: the global `directional_targeting_ext` (the targeting cone and reach), each attack sequencer's
`AttackAlignment` window and its clips blended on `FLT_MeleeTargetDistance` at child weights 1, 3.5 and 7 (`…_1m`, `…_3.5m`, `…_7m`) with their
extracted root motion (`smtool graph-dump --melee`). How the engine combined them is not in the data: those rules are ours or interpretations. Code:
`SmSim/MeleeLock.cs` (lock, alignment, lunge; `Combat.StepPlayer` applies them; `World` passes the rewound players), `SmContent/MeleeMotion.cs`
(reach reader), `SmContent/MeleeLockTuning.cs` (global values), `SmNet/GameClient.cs` (`MeleeLockTarget`, `ViewAt`), `SmNet/MeleePresentation.cs`
and `client/NetworkView.MeleeLock.cs` (presentation). Tests: `MeleeLockTests`, `MeleePresentationTests`, `MeleeLockInstallTests` (install only).

Measured with headless bots (four Tacticals with the knife, 2 v 2, `--bot-melee --anim-probe`, Manufactorum, 150 s a run on a local server). The bots
aim exactly at their target every tick and stand and tap melee within 3 m, so before protocol 32 their freely turning attack already tracked the target
perfectly; both sides interrupt each other often (a swing the client predicted to its hit but the server interrupted does not land). A swing "landed" when
the server's melee hit report arrives within 0.6 s of its predicted hit. Foot slide: the anim probe's planted-foot speed (flat foot) and planted-stretch
slide under whole-body melee clips, every drawn marine, whatever the body's speed (the four bots' figures).

| Build | Swings | Reached their hit | Landed (of reached / of all swings) | Planted-foot speed median, p90 (m/s) | Planted-stretch slide median (cm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main 4095ae4 (no lock, no lunge; two runs) | 100 | 86 | 49 (0.57 / 0.49) | 2.88 to 3.21, 7.8 to 8.9 | 60 to 86 |
| this build, `--no-melee-lock` (lunge and held heading, no lock) | 171 | 145 | 74 (0.51 / 0.43) | — | — |
| this build (lock) | 99 | 77 | 59 (0.77 / 0.60) | 2.12 to 2.32, 8.6 to 8.8 | 48 to 52 |
| this build (lock), hit-stop off (`--no-hit-stop`, then the default) | 105 | 90 | 58 (0.64 / 0.55) | 1.87 to 2.03, 8.6 to 9.0 | 50 to 55 |

The lock lands 0.55 to 0.60 of all swings against 0.49 before (run-to-run spread about 0.05) and against 0.43 for the held heading alone; the lunge's foot
slide falls by about a third (median 3.0 to 2.0 m/s, stretch 60 to 86 cm to 48 to 55 cm; the hit-stop adds about 0.2 m/s, by design). The p90 near
8.5 m/s is unchanged in every build: not the lunge (open: the entry cross-fades from a sprint, the remote players' interpolation).

Not done: the `AttackDistanceValidation` window (read, not used), the 180° attacks, player-to-player collision (the lunge stops 1 m short of the locked
target only; it passes through others), the Ork's presentation of its distance clips (its attacks lunge in the simulation; the Ork view still poses its
chosen clip).

### Quick throw and quickdraw switch (feel/grenades-quickdraw; config hash, no protocol change, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner's requests of 2026-11-06 (verbatim): "make the frag and blind grenades match the original game's models, make them more responsive to throw (less delay
between pressing the keybind and the grenade releasing), and you're free to act immediately and start a new action once the grenade leaves the hand. add a visual effect to
the grenade explosion -" (the last sentence was cut off); "there is currently a slight delay when switching weapons and firing the next one. it's a bit too significant.
make the player point his gun at the crosshair faster (bring it up faster), so shooting any weapon after swapping feels more responsive. it should be near instant, like a
quickdraw." All modes (classic PvP and Musou Mode). Both timings are **deliberate changes from the original** and **estimates (owner's request)** to review in a playtest;
`GameplayTuning.Load(ownerFeel: false)` keeps the data's. Code: `GameplayTuning.OwnerThrowReleaseScale` / `OwnerQuickdrawTime`, `SimConfig.QuickdrawSwitch`, `Combat.StepPlayer`
(the raise), `ActionHandoff.TossClipTime`, client `NetworkView.Quickdraw.cs`, `NetworkView.Grenades.cs`. Tests: `GrenadesQuickdrawTests`.

`SoundTriggers.MeleeHitSound` and `NetworkView.Sound.cs` (`SoundHits`). Tests: `MeleeCharge2Tests` (with the install's numbers, printed), `JumpPackAttackTests` (the

### Dedicated server hardening (server/hardening; server only, no protocol change)

For a public tester demo of the dedicated server. The original was peer-hosted, so none of this has an original counterpart: every
value is ours, chosen for abuse resistance, and configurable (`server.cmd --help`; operator notes in docs/dedicated-server.md).
The per-address rules apply only where the transport knows the sender's address (UDP; in-process loopback endpoints without an
address are exempt). Protocol 23 unchanged: refusals reuse `Reject` (`ServerFull` with a detail text), deferrals send nothing.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loopback exemption | loopback addresses (127.0.0.0/8, ::1) are exempt from the per-address cap, the join rate, the per-address respawn hold and the idle kick, so the owner's playtests can run up to 12 bot clients on one machine; `--limit-loopback` applies them to loopback too (tests); bans and the re-join rule on a dead player's own connection apply either way | - | per join | `ServerOptions.LimitLoopback`, `--limit-loopback` | ours (maintainer's request, 2026-10-28) | ours | none |
| Players per address | at most 4 players from one IP address (IPv4-mapped IPv6 counts as IPv4); more are refused with `ServerFull` "at most 4 players from one address"; 0 = no cap | players | per join | `ServerOptions.MaxPlayersPerAddress`, `--max-per-ip` | ours (one household or LAN party behind one NAT) | ours | none |
| Join rate per address | at most one accepted new join per IP address every 5 s; a Hello inside the window gets no answer, so the client's own resend (every 250 ms) gets in once the window has passed; a new client replacing a player on the same address counts as a join; 0 = no limit | s | wall clock (server) | `ServerOptions.JoinInterval`, `--join-interval` | ours | ours | none |
| Idle kick | a player with no real input (any movement or any button; turning alone does not count) and no customizer use (a Setup from the class creator or appearance editor, an emblem upload chunk; appearance queries and blob requests are automatic and do not count) for 300 s while the match is being played is dropped, with no reason shown (the protocol has no kick message: the client shows a lost connection after its server timeout); warm-up and the end of a round reset the clock; only connections with an address are watched (in-process endpoints without one are not); 0 = never | s | wall clock (server) | `ServerOptions.IdleKick`, `--idle-kick`, `GameServer.IsRealInput` | ours | ours | none |
| Repeated Hello of a joined client | answered with the same Welcome but no longer counts as being heard from: a client that only resends its Hello times out after the 5 s peer timeout | - | per packet | `GameServer.OnHello` | ours (before: it refreshed the timeout, so Hellos alone could hold a slot) | ours | none |
| Re-join while dead | a new client on the connection of a dead player, or from the address of a dead player that left, gets no answer until that player's respawn time has run out (5 s placeholder respawn), so a re-join is never a faster respawn or loadout swap; a re-join while alive is a fresh spawn and the death is not scored (open: the original's rule for leavers is unknown) | s | wall clock (server) | `GameServer.AdmitJoin`, `NoteLeave` | ours | ours | none |
| Tick catch-up | at most 5 ticks per server update; after a longer stall the due ticks are skipped (tick phase kept), snapshot and scoreboard times move up to now, and the skip is logged (throttled to one line per 10 s) | ticks | per update | `ServerOptions.MaxCatchUpTicks` | ours (before: unbounded, so a long stall ran every missed tick at once) | ours | none |
| Crash isolation | a packet handler that throws is logged and drops only that sender's player; a recipient whose snapshot fails is dropped alone (the others still get theirs, and the tick's shot records are always cleared); a tick, scoreboard or pickup step that throws is logged and the server goes on; the first 20 faults are logged (the first 5 with stack traces), then one line per 10 s with a count | - | per packet / per tick | `GameServer.Update`, `Dispatch`, `Guard`, `SendSnapshots` | ours | ours | none |
| Failing simulation | after 60 ticks in a row have failed (2 s at 30 Hz) the server logs `FATAL` and exits with code 4 so a supervisor restarts it; a single good tick resets the count; 0 = never | ticks | per tick | `ServerOptions.MaxConsecutiveTickFaults`, `GameServer.FatalError`, Program.cs | ours | ours | none |
| Bans | `--ban-file`: one IP address or CIDR range per line (the address needs a dot or a colon: a bare number is ignored), `#` comments; checked every 2 s and read again when its time or size changes (a file written in the last 2 s is read once more); banned sources get no reply at all and connected banned players are dropped; a missing file bans no one | s | wall clock (server) | `ServerOptions.BanFile`, `BanList`, `BanFile` | ours | ours | none |
| Refusal detail | a content mismatch names the server's Steam build (from `appmanifest_55150.acf` two folders above the install, read-only, when present) and content fingerprint; the server logs every refusal with the client's protocol, content, config or map hash (throttled per address) | - | per refusal | `GameServer.ContentMismatchDetail`, `NoteRefusal` | ours | ours | none |
| UDP receive | read until the socket reports nothing (`Poll`, then `ReceiveFrom` until would-block), not while `Available` > 0 (on Linux 0 for an empty datagram, which then blocked every packet behind it); at most 256 empty, oversized or failed datagrams skipped per call; the server socket is bound with exclusive address use on Windows, and a port in use stops the server with exit code 3 | datagrams | per call | `DatagramReceive.Next`, `UdpServerTransport` | ours | ours | none |

Open (not done): a `BlobChunk` (an emblem upload chunk, protocol 22) carries no session; the server takes it only from a connection
with a player and only for an upload it asked that connection for, and checks the whole emblem's hash before use, but a sender that
can spoof that player's address could disturb its upload (worst case: the upload fails verification and is retried later).

Open (not done, S2 of the hardening review): lag compensation trusts the client's acknowledged snapshot within the 15-tick (500 ms) rewind
cap, so a client can fake up to 500 ms of lag; bounding the rewind by a server-measured round trip is planned (docs/changes-from-original.md).

## Unknown, needs evidence

How the extracted speeds and acceleration values combine in the original controller, how the original combines the jump pack's values (M14 model is an interpretation), camera blending, pitch relaxing and collision (offsets and FOV are read since M20; whether FOV is vertical is not stated); whether aim assist applied to the PC mouse;
whether shots leave from the camera, the muzzle or the eye, and whether the original tests shots against the ragdoll bodies (used as hit volumes since M20) or other shapes, posed or at rest; how the extracted weapon values combine (upgrades, shield, Exterminatus); melee timing of weapons other than the knife, melee targeting and lunge; execution trigger rules and
invulnerability (the evade's property windows are hyper armour against stuns, not invulnerability, M21); which reaction state a
reaction type enters (the reaction graph's state machine transitions are not decoded; M28 maps kinds to clip sets by name); how the
player triggers the heavy classes' displace kick; the original PC binding of the heavy strike; root motion vs code-driven movement (the evade
follows its clips' extracted motion since M21; walking and the jump pack do not); how long code keeps the ready posture after a shot (blend times are read since M27; other animation blend times are not); network tick rates of the original.

### Network responsiveness (net/responsive, 2026-11-09; client and server; protocol 65: the snapshot carries the input slack; no gameplay rule changed)

The owner (2026-11-09) on Classic PvP and the networking in general: "delayed, not responsive, slow. its smooth, but we're missing something". Measured first with an
opt-in readout (`SM_NET_LATENCY=<s>` / client `--net-latency [s]`: `NETLAT` lines; engine-free probe `tests/SmNet.Tests/NetLatencyProbe.cs`, `SM_NET_PROBE=1`), then four
changes, each with a switch back (client `--old-input-lead`, `--old-own-draw`, `--interp-delay <ms>`, `--no-predicted-hits`, all four `--old-net-feel`; server
`--snapshot-rate 20`). Before/after: see docs/milestones.md, "Network responsiveness".

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Input lead: target (protocol 65) | the server's input slack (ms from an input's arrival to the run of its tick, the least a snapshot covers) aimed at **1** tick (one lost input batch survived; `LeadLossTicks`), more on a lossy link (the smallest count of ticks whose run of lost batches is rarer than **3 in 10,000** a tick, at most **4**, from the snapshot loss over **3 s**: 1 % keeps 2, 5 % keeps 3; `LossTicks`; a target 2 ticks or more above the slack runs the missing ticks at once) plus the jitter guard's ticks plus the measured jitter (the slack's median less its 2nd percentile over **2 s**) plus **5 ms**: about 40 to 55 ms on a clean link; with `--lead-ticks` the whole-tick lead report at **2** instead | ms | per snapshot | `ClientOptions.PreciseLead`, `LeadLossTicks`, `LeadMarginMs`, `GameClient.TargetInputSlack` | ours (net/responsive; the owner 2026-11-09: "buffering as low as it can go while still playing well"; before, the steering only acted on whole ticks below 1 and above 5, so the lead sat at 3 to 5) | ours | medium |
| Input lead: slew | precise: the client's ticks run **1 %** slower for every **10 ms** the filtered slack (time constant **0.25 s**) is above its target past a **2 ms** dead band (as much faster below), at most **4 %**; integer (`--lead-ticks`): 4 % while the filtered lead is **0.75** ticks or more off 2, until within 0.25; the drawn fraction runs over the length each tick was scheduled with | %, ms, ticks, s | per snapshot | `GameClient.SlackGainMs`, `SlackDeadbandMs`, `ClientOptions.LeadSlew`, `LeadBand`, `LeadFilterSeconds` | ours (net/responsive) | ours | medium |
| Input lead: jumps | a report below 0 (the server repeated an input) runs ticks at once up to a lead of 1 (at most **10**); a filtered lead at or above target + 3 pauses toward the target, at most **2** ticks a time; after a jump the steering waits the echo round trip + 0.25 s + 2 ticks | ticks | per snapshot | `GameClient.SteerLead`, `MaxLeadJump`, `MaxLeadPause` | ours (before: one tick per handshake round trip) | ours | medium |
| Input lead: jitter guard | a snapshot whose tick ran without this client's input (`LastInputTick` older, or a negative slack; integer steering also a lead report of 0 or less) raises the target by a tick (at most one a second, **2** in all; not within a feedback wait after this client's own stall, an update gap over **100 ms**); each **10 s** without one lowers it a tick. After such a stall no late catch-up runs, and the ticks a snapshot finds the client behind on move its schedule too (before, its tick loop ran them all on top: each hitch added its length to the lead, 10 ticks after a 400 ms one) | ticks, s | per snapshot | `GameClient.JitterGuard`, `JitterGuardTicks`, `JitterGuardSeconds`, `StallGap`, `StallSkips` | ours (net/responsive) | ours | medium |
| Echo round trip | the time from sending the input a snapshot names as the server's newest (its tick plus the lead) to the snapshot's arrival, smoothed (1/8 gain); an upper bound (it includes the server's wait for its snapshot send and the client's frame); replaces the handshake's round trip (inflated by a map load: 425 ms seen) for the lead's waits | ms | per snapshot | `GameClient.EchoRoundTripMs` | ours (net/responsive) | ours | medium |
| Own marine drawn ahead | the own model and camera are drawn from the newest predicted tick toward a speculative next tick (the newest input stepped once more, held buttons, same collision; presentation only), a tick sooner than before; after an early tick the tick before it toward it; own clips (attack, throw, brace) a tick ahead with it | ticks | per frame | `ClientOptions.DrawOwnAhead`, `GameClient.Ahead`, `ClipLead` | ours (net/responsive; before: between the previous tick and the newest) | ours | medium |
| Own marine: tick step blend | the step a tick or a lead jump makes in that drawing (a new input against the speculative one, ticks run or paused at once) is blended out linearly over **3** ticks; a reconciliation keeps its own 0.1 s fade | ticks | per frame | `GameClient.DrawBlendTicks`, `DrawBlendOffset` | ours (net/responsive) | ours | medium |
| Adaptive interpolation delay | the larger of **1.5** snapshot intervals and the 95th-percentile snapshot gap plus the arrival jitter (98th percentile of the arrival offset less its median) plus **5 ms**, over the last **2 s** of snapshots; floor **50 ms**, ceiling **100 ms** (the server's lag-compensation bound, `ServerOptions.MaxInterpolationDelay`, unchanged); rises at once, falls with a **2 s** time constant; 100 ms until 8 snapshots have arrived (at 20 Hz the gaps alternate 1 and 2 ticks: about 89 ms) | ms | per snapshot | `InterpolationDelayEstimator.BaseIntervals`, `ClientOptions.MinInterpolationDelay`, `MaxInterpolationDelay` | ours (net/responsive) | ours | medium |
| Remote extrapolation | when the render tick passes the newest snapshot (a late one), other players are carried on along their last two snapshots' motion for at most **1** tick past it, then held; a respawn's jump or a dead player is not carried | ticks | per frame | `ClientOptions.MaxExtrapolationTicks`, `GameClient.ExtrapolatedTicks` | ours (net/responsive; `--no-extrapolation`: held at the newest, as before) | ours | medium |
| Own cosmetics on the click's frame | measured, unchanged: a press of Fire, melee or roll runs the next tick in the frame its event arrives (feel/controls' early tick), so the muzzle flash, the shot's sound and the clip show 0.3 to 0.4 ms into that frame (Godot `--latency-probe`, 10 trials each, 60 fps); the tick still decides the shot | ms | per press | `EarlyTick` | ours (feel/controls) | ours | high |
| Musou Mode interpolation floor | **100 ms** (its crowd is drawn at the same render tick and its far records come every 5th tick) | ms | per snapshot | `GameClient.InterpolationFloor` (set in `client/Extras/Musou/NetworkView.Musou.cs`) | ours (net/responsive) | ours | medium |
| Predicted ranged hit feedback | an own hit-scan shot whose traced ray (the tracer's) strikes an enemy as drawn shows the hit marker and plays the hit confirmation on the shot's frame; the server's report then shows its marker again only for hits no prediction showed, a kill (the kill marker) or an unpredicted headshot, and plays its confirmation only for hits no prediction showed (the data's kill layer belongs to the same event, so a predicted kill plays no kill layer); the predictions are forgotten on a respawn or a new connection; a prediction waits **0.75 s** for its report; the server still decides every hit and its damage; not for bots, allies, cones, projectiles or melee | s | per shot | `PredictedHitLedger`, `client/NetworkView.Responsive.cs` | ours (net/responsive; before: the marker waited for the report, 100 to 230 ms) | ours | medium |
| Latency readout | `SM_NET_LATENCY=<s>` (client environment) or `--net-latency [s]`: a `NETLAT` line every s seconds: edge-draw, edge-draw-5cm, lead, lead-ms, rtt, press-apply, shot-hit, marker, interp, snap-gap, remote (count, mean, p50, p90, max) | — | per line | `NetLatencyReadout` | ours | test aid | high |

### Stomp impacts, the power sword and the jump-pack thrust (fx/impact-pass; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

The owner's requests of 2026-10-29: stomps with "ground breaking/shockwaves/etc. to give the stomps impact and weight" (no smoke or dust), a power sword that "should glow blue and flare
up when hitting an enemy", and jump-pack thrusters whose trail starts at the exhaust and is much shorter ("reference the video": the reference flights show bright blue-white glows at the
nozzles and flames of about 1 to 3 m). Content: `SmContent.MeleeEffects` (the melee wargear's blast-strike and deployed effects), `SmContent.NozzleExit`; client: `NetworkView.MeleeFx.cs`,
`StompFx.cs`, `PowerBlade.cs`, `NetworkView.JumpFx.cs`, `FxPlayer` (`TrailScale`, `BeamScale`, `TrailByDistance`), `WeaponRig` (`TryMeleeMarker`, `MeleeMeshInHand`, the exhaust form of
`TryWornMarker`). Tools: `smtool fx-dump <game-dir|auto> <name|word>... [--list] [--fields]`, `smtool fx-dump auto --map <map> [--where]`, `smtool weapon-parts <wargear> --markers
--profile <locator,locator> --exhaust <word>`.

### Ground pound impact and landing effects (M41; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the owner's playtest (2026-10-28; user's knowledge of the original): a ground pound should leave a large impact on the ground with a small crater, a larger thin dark ring
where the pound's hit detection reached (natural, not bright), dust going up around the impact, the original sound, and perhaps physics chunks of the ground thrown about.

### Test bots: aim error, engagement range, spawn-door wait, launcher and side requests (M44a; client and server option, test aids, not simulated, no protocol change)

From the owner's playtest (2026-10-28): bots should move better, wait outside an enemy spawn room instead of hugging its door, miss most of their shots (recorded footage), shoot
from across the map when they see the target, and be startable in numbers (up to 6 per side). **All of it is ours: test aids, not the original AI.** Human clients are untouched
(every rule below runs only under `--bot`; the server option is off by default). Code: `src/SmNet/BotAimModel.cs`, `client/NetworkView.BotAim.cs`, `NetworkView.BotSpawn.cs`,
`NetworkView.Bot.cs`, `NetworkView.Nav.cs`, `src/SmSim/NavAgent.cs`, `tools/bots.ps1` (`bots.cmd`), `MatchRules.HonorSideRequests` (`--honor-side-requests`).

| Parameter (M44a) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bot aim error | a bot that is shooting a ranged weapon at an enemy has its view (yaw, pitch) drifted off the line to the target by a slow **wander** (Ornstein-Uhlenbeck, time constant 1.5 s: a smooth move, no 30 Hz shake), and every tick the trigger is held its **shot** is turned by a fresh Gaussian **scatter through the protocol's shot offsets** (`PlayerInput.ShotYawOffset`/`ShotPitchOffset`, protocol 12; the body does not shake); per axis total σ = wander (0.8 σ) and scatter (0.6 σ) added in quadrature. Melee, grenade throws and every non-shooting tick keep the exact aim (the wander only drifts); the move stick is turned back so the body goes the same way. Seeded by player id (the same seed gives the same error sequence; a run as a whole does not repeat exactly) | radians | per input tick | `BotAimModel`, `NetworkView.BotApplyAim` | ours | test aid | none |

### Classic PvP bots: centre hold, roaming, spread routes, fixed loadouts and the melee push (2026-11-07, push, cover and posts 2026-11-08; client test aid, no protocol change)

The owner, verbatim: "when there are no enemies left on the map (outside of the enemy spawn zone) - or after wiping the enemy team, the bots should default to holding
defensive positions around the center of the map. the bots should generally take different routes out around the map as well and spread out more on annihilation game
mode in particular." and "the bot should never wait directly outside the spawn area of the enemy. they will simply roam around the map until the enemy has spread out and
pressured the center of the map after respawning and returning." Plus a fixed list of loadouts per class. **All of it is ours: test bots, not the original AI.** Every rule
runs only under `--bot`; Musou Mode is untouched (the loadouts apply only on `mp_*` maps, the movement only in the Classic bot paths). Code: `src/SmSim/BotMapPlan.cs`
(`BotMapPlan`, `BotRoamer`), `src/SmSim/BotLoadouts.cs`, `client/NetworkView.BotRoam.cs`, `client/NetworkView.BotLoadout.cs`; `smtool bot-loadouts auto` prints the
loadouts resolved against the install.

### Classic PvP bots: grenade safety (bot-grenade-safety, owner 2026-11-11; client test aid, no protocol or config-hash change)

The owner, verbatim: "change bot behavior in classic pvp mode - i want to set a rule that includes a minimum distance at which they will throw grenades. they should also not (as a
raptor/assault marine) jump in near where the grenade landed until it has exploded." and "currently the assault/raptor bots but bots in general suicide by throwing grenades at enemies
who are on top of them." and "the end result is no more or very few bot suicides to their own grenades." **Every rule and number here is ours (test bots are not the original's AI)**;
the blast radii are the data's. Classic PvP bots only (Annihilation and Seize Ground, faithful or extended content; Musou Mode's co-op bots return their own input first and the hold
skips that tick). Code: `src/SmNet/BotGrenadeSafety.cs` (engine-free rules), `client/NetworkView.BotGrenades.cs`, the callers in `NetworkView.BotInput`, `BotThrow`,
`BotWeaponButtons`, `BotWantsDetonation` and `BotJumpInput`, `NavAgent.CancelTakeOff`; tests `BotGrenadeSafetyTests`, `NavJumpTests`. `--old-bot-throws` restores the old script.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| What the bots did (measured) | headless matches on Manufactorum (127.0.0.1, Annihilation, 8 bots: per side 2 jump-pack, 1 Tactical, 1 heavy, all with frag presets), 3 x 5 min with the old script: **15 of 184 deaths were a bot's own frag** (8 %; 103 throws; 19 enemies killed by frags, 7 of them together with the thrower). 11 of the 15 were Assault or Raptor bots. Every one was thrown at a target 6 to 17 m away (8 under 9 m, 5 at 9 to 13 m, 2 beyond); the old aim went to the ground **8 m short of the target** (at least 2 m in front), a rule from before the owner's 2026-10-29 bounce change, so the grenade came to rest 2 to 6 m from the thrower; within its 1 s ground fuse the thrower then charged (7), jumped or pounded (4) or swung in melee (3) at the target beside it (some did two of these), or did nothing else or walked on (3). None by the plasma weapons' splash (plasma cannon, gun and pistol were in the same matches) | deaths | per match | the server's kill, throw and detonation lines and the bots' logs | measured 2026-11-11 | test aid, measured | medium |
| Safety distance | the item's own largest **damaging** blast radius from the data x the blast reach scale (`SimConfig.ThrownBlastScale`, 1 in Classic PvP) + **1.5 m**: the frag 10 + 1.5 = **11.5 m** (Master-Crafted Wargear's 15 m: 16.5 m); 0 (the old rule) for stims, the blind grenade (its blasts only blind) and anything without a damaging blast | m | per throw | `BotGrenadeSafety.SafetyDistance`, `Margin` | owner 2026-11-11 (a minimum throw distance); radius data; margin ours | test aid, estimate | estimate |
| Throw rule (damaging items) | a throw only when the target's chest **and** the predicted landing point are both at least the safety distance from the bot's chest, in **3D** (a target 9 m out and 7 m up is 11.4 m: refused; one 3 m out and 14 m below: thrown), the target within 20 m horizontally (`--bot-throw-max`, unchanged) and neither the target nor the bot **in the air** (a jump-pack jump or pound in any phase but the landing, or a vertical speed above **3 m/s**; the bot also when not grounded: a flier is not where the grenade lands, and a bot in the air moves on before the release; in the first after-run a frag thrown at a jump-pack target, whose predicted landing had come to 8.6 m by the release, flew on and went off 2.8 s later 5.7 m from the thrower, who lived). The landing point: the target's feet moved by its **horizontal** velocity over the release delay left (0.2 s from the press) plus the flight (distance / 47.5 m/s), or the first level contact on the straight line from the eye to it (a ledge's edge below a target above, a rail). The other gates stay (4 s between presses, nothing else under way) | m, s | per bot tick | `BotGrenadeSafety.CheckThrow`, `PredictLanding`, `NetworkView.BotThrowCheck` | owner 2026-11-11; the rule ours | test aid, estimate | estimate |
| Throw aim | at that landing point (yaw and pitch from the eye, recomputed every tick until the release; under way the **farther** from the bot's chest of the point checked at the press and the one now, so a target that comes on after the press does not pull the aim in under the safety distance): the frag flies straight for its first 10 m and, with the 2026-10-29 bounce, stops within about a metre of its first ground contact, so it goes off at the target or a little beyond (`BotGrenadeSafetyTests`, the simulation with that bounce: aimed at the feet of a target 14 m out it goes off beyond 11.5 m and does not touch the thrower; the old aim at a target 8 m out put 100 or more damage on the thrower). The old aim (8 m short, at least 2 m) stays for the blind grenade and with `--old-bot-throws` | rad | per tick of the throw | `NetworkView.BotAimThrow`, `BotThrowAimPoint`, `BotGrenadeSafety.FartherLanding` | ours | test aid, estimate | estimate |
| Stims and the blind grenade | the old rule: **6 m** horizontally and more (stims at any distance), up to 20 m | m | per bot tick | `BotGrenadeSafety.OldThrowAllowed` | the old test script | test aid | none |
| The own grenade | snapshots carry no owner: after the bot's own predicted release, the first new thrown projectile of the newest snapshot (not there at the release, not held by another own grenade, within **1 s** of the release and no farther from the release point than the throw's speed times the time since plus **3 m**, the nearest such; without that limit a run took an enemy's frag landing 16 m away at the release for the own one) is its own, followed until it is gone (detonated). While it flies (a frag's fuse starts on the ground) the throw's predicted landing point stands for it, and once it has been outside the bot's reach since the release its own place too (a bounce back off a wall comes back at the bot); once it is down (resting or stuck to a player in the snapshot, or moved less than **1.5 m in 0.15 s**, under about 10 m/s: past its bounce or dropped off a wall) its own place; unseen, the landing point at most **2.1 s**; a grenade is a hazard at most **6 s** from its release. With launcher rounds waiting (`ProjectilesOut`) every round of the remote-detonated weapon it carries is one too (reach: the round's blast radius + 1.5 m), and so is a resting or stuck sticky round of its own weapons, each at most **6 s** from when the bot first sees it waiting (a round never set off stops holding the bot). With nothing out (no own grenade, no remote round, no carried weapon that can leave a waiting round) the snapshot is not scanned | s, m | per bot tick | `NetworkView.BotHazards`, `BotGrenadeSafety.TrackOwn`, `IsDown`, `RoundIsHazard`, `LeavesWaitingRounds`, `UnseenSeconds`, `MaxHazardSeconds` | ours | test aid, estimate | estimate |
| The hold (on the ground) | while a hazard is out, a move whose straight path over the next **0.6 s** (6 m/s for a full stick, x 1.5 sprinting or jumping; a jump or charge without a stick goes where the bot faces) passes within a hazard's reach (from the chest, 3D) is **held**: the stick centred, Jump (jump, dash, hop, evade roll), Sprint and the charge's F dropped, the view and fire kept; a bot already inside a reach **backs straight out** (away from the nearest hazard on the ground, at the stick's full length, the view and fire kept, no jump, sprint, melee or charge). Not in a jump, a charge or added content's own bot | s, m/s | per bot tick | `BotGrenadeSafety.Hold`, `LookAhead`, `MoveSpeed`, `NetworkView.BotGrenadeHold` | owner 2026-11-11 ("not jump in near where the grenade landed until it has exploded"); numbers ours | test aid, estimate | estimate |
| Back-out give-up (no deadlock; review 2026-11-11) | the back-out is straight away from the blast on the ground, with no sense of walls: a back-out that gets no **0.25 m** farther (3D, chest to the blast's centre) than its farthest so far for **1.5 s** (a wall or a corner behind the bot) gives up: from that tick the bot's own input goes through, and the blasts whose reach holds its chest are left out of every rule (move, jump, pound, charge, melee) until its chest is out of all of them; the other hazards still count, and once out the holds apply again. Remote detonation still waits until the chest is out of the rounds' reach | s, m | per bot tick | `BotGrenadeSafety.StepBackOut`, `GiveUpSeconds`, `ProgressMetres`, `StillGivenUp`, `NetworkView.BotGrenadeHold`, `BotHazards` | ours | test aid, estimate | estimate |

| Jump pack, charge and melee | no jump at a target whose feet or chest is inside a hazard's reach; in the air no pound onto such a target and no stick toward it, and over its own grenade (its ground point inside a reach) the bot steers straight out; no charge when the target is inside or the run passes through a reach; no melee swing (or its lunge) at a target inside, or while the bot is inside | m | per bot tick | `NetworkView.BotJumpIntoOwnBlast`, `BotPoundIntoOwnBlast`, `BotAirStick`, `BotChargeIntoOwnBlast`, `BotMeleeIntoOwnBlast` | owner 2026-11-11; the rule ours | test aid, estimate | estimate |
| Remote detonation | never while the bot's chest is within a waiting round's blast radius + 1.5 m (the grenade launcher; the fallback detonation after 1.2 s waits too), also after a back-out given up or a round past its 6 s as a hazard; the bot backs out first | m | per press | `BotGrenadeSafety.MayDetonate`, `InReach`, `NetworkView.BotDetonationHeld` | ours | test aid, estimate | estimate |

Now a shot whose projectile has a damaging blast (the plasma cannon, the plasma gun's and pistol's charged balls, the grenade launcher) is not pressed when it would burst within its blast radius + **1.5 m** of the bot's chest: it bursts at the first level contact on the line from the eye to the target's chest, else at the target, or, when nearer, where the shot meets a target coming on (the target's chest moved by its velocity, 3D, over the interpolation delay it is drawn late plus the shot's flight to it; a focused review run had a Raptor flying at a Devastator meet a basic ball 6.5 m from the heavy's chest and kill it) (the plasma cannon's basic ball r 7: 8.5 m; its charged ball r 15: 16.5 m). A charge whose charged shot would is not started (the tap's basic shot instead); a charge already held is held on while its release would (an overheat ends it unfired). | The pistol for a splash weapon at close range (review 2026-11-11: the plasma cannon heavy held its fire from point blank to 8.5 m with nothing else to do) | a run of held splash shots of the primary in hand (no gap over **0.25 s**) that lasts **1 s** switches to the pistol when its clip has a round (a holstered weapon does not reload) and the toggle goes to it (not overheated: the heat rule keeps its own switch); on that pistol the bot stays (an empty clip reloads itself) until the primary's burst point at the target is **2 m** beyond its safety distance (the plasma cannon's basic ball: 10.5 m), then switches back, as the old switch rule does once the pistol is out of ammunition | s, m | per bot tick | `BotGrenadeSafety.NoteHeld`, `HeldFor`, `TakePistol`, `BackToSplash`, `PistolAfterSeconds`, `PistolBackMargin`, `HeldGapSeconds`, `NetworkView.BotSplashSwitch` | ours | test aid, estimate | estimate |

The bots threw 45 % less (57 against 103); refused: 69 targets too close, 23 in the air, 22 landings too close (the level on the line, or a target coming on), 6 from the air; held: 60 charges, 15 jumps, 3 pounds, 1 melee swing, 14 moves, 5 back-outs, 44 splash shots. ### The Ork Boy in the simulation (Ork O4; used by the simulation; no protocol change)

The Ork Boy is a deliberate addition (docs/ork-faction-design.md; owner's decisions 2026-10-28). Off by default: `GameplayTuning.Load(gameDir, OrkBalanceMode.Parity | Data)`
adds it (since O5 the server and the networked client always do, in Parity: section "The Ork Boy on the wire and in the server (Ork O5)"); without it every config hashes exactly as before (pinned by
`OrkSimTests.ConfigsWithoutClassBodiesHashAsBefore`; the install's config hash is unchanged, `BD42193EA8C48334`). `smtool ork-balance <game-dir|auto> [--mode parity|data|both]`
prints every row below with the install's numbers. Code: `SmContent/OrkClass.cs`, `SmContent/OrkBalance.cs`, `SmSim/Bodies.cs`; tests `OrkBalanceTests`, `OrkSimTests`.

| Parameter (O4) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |

### Connect timeout, hosting checks and hosted bots (fix/connect-timeout; client, front end and release launcher; no protocol change)

From the owner's report of the tester release (build 4fa4d46): an old server still held UDP 27015, the front end's hosted server could not bind it and exited (code 3), JOIN then
reached the old server, which dropped this version's Hello unread (servers from before 2026-10-28 had no refusal for another version's Hello), and the client showed
"Connecting" forever. Then the owner's requests of 2026-10-29: a STOP SERVER button, bots in a hosted match ("no bots are joining after successfully hosting", "add 7 bots on local
pc only server hosting initiation"), and + BOT / − BOT. fix/hosting-bots-logs (the owner's decisions of 2026-10-29, after a tester's 8 GB laptop ran out of memory
with the 7 default bots and the bots' logs pushed the player's own log out): no bots by default, one BOTS stepper (0 to 15) applied at the start, no + BOT / − BOT, and
every bot writes its own log file. **All values here are ours.** Code: `SmNet.ConnectFailure`, `GameClient` (`ClientStatus.NoAnswer`), `SmNet.MatchFlowGate`,
`SmContent.HostStart`, `SmContent.HostBots`, `client/FrontEnd/HostPanel.cs`, `HostedServer.cs`, `HostedBots.cs`, `tools/release/package/Host.cmd`, `Launcher.ps1 -StartBots`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### Performance pass 1 (perf/pass-1; build, client and release launcher; no protocol change)

The owner's report on the e792504 tester build hosted "This PC only" (the server, 7 headless bots and the owner's client on one PC). Measured on one PC
(a current desktop CPU and a current high-end GPU) by replaying one recorded 8-player Manufactorum demo (`--play-demo`, windowed off-screen, `--frame-profile`, the new
`--perf-probe`), the e792504 playtest zip against an export of this branch; other Godot runs shared the PC, so single runs vary by about 1.5 ms
(interleaved repeats). Before / after with 7 bots on the same PC: mean frame **12.0 → 6.4 ms**, p99 20.2 → 12.9 ms, p99.9 37.9 → 17.5 ms, frames over
33 ms 24 → 1 in 90 s; with no bots 7.5 → 5.3 ms, 4 → 0. Causes and fixes:
the exported game compiled SmSim, SmNet, SmContent and SmFormats without JIT optimisation (Godot's `ExportRelease` configuration is not one
Microsoft.NET.Sdk optimises; `Directory.Build.props` now does: collision rays 6 to 8.6 times faster, the follow camera 1.8 → 0.2 ms a frame);
`HitVolumes.Bounds` took a hull's margin again for every corner (20 to 45 ms on the crosshair ray while a jump-pack player flew, Debug; same result now);
the first ammunition drop's model was read on the main thread (100 to 140 ms, about 20 s into every match; now during the map load); a blocking full
collection of the .NET GC (88 ms once). Code: `client/BotLean.cs`, `client/PerfProbe.cs`, `NetworkView.Pickups.cs` (`PrewarmPickups`), `SmNet.LeanBot`.
Merged with perf/lean-bots (integrate/2026-10-29): perf/pass-1's `--bot-lean` flag is gone; its frame cap, physics rate and `--no-fx` apply to every lean bot
(`LeanBot.Decide`: a headless `--bot` without `--bot-full-load` or a presentation aid), whose skipped loads (map visuals included) are perf/lean-bots'.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lean bot frame cap | a lean bot (`LeanBot.Decide`: the hosted match's bots, `bots.cmd`, `Launcher.ps1 -StartBots`) runs at most **30** frames a second (`--bot-fps n` overrides, 0 = no cap; Godot's own `--max-fps` before `--` wins); before, a headless bot ran uncapped at about 134 | frames/s | per frame | `LeanBot.FrameCap`, `LeanBot.FrameCapFor`, `BotLean.Apply` | ours (the server's 30 Hz tick: one input a tick) | ours | none |
| Lean bot physics steps | **30** a second (a lean bot builds no ragdolls or physics props; Godot's default 60) | steps/s | engine physics | `LeanBot.PhysicsTicks` | ours | ours | none |
| Lean bot content | no effects (`--no-fx`); everything else perf/lean-bots skips (row "Lean headless bot": the map's visuals, sound, looks, weapons, ragdolls, poses, ...); collision, navigation, characters and everything the bot decides from are loaded | — | per bot | `BotLean`, `NetworkView.Lean.cs` | ours | ours | none |
| Human client GC mode | `GCLatencyMode.SustainedLowLatency` for a client that is not a bot (no blocking full collection unless memory runs low); `--gc-default` keeps the runtime's default | — | per process | `ModelViewer.StartNetwork` | ours | ours | none |
| Probe (`--perf-probe`) | every 5 s and at the end: frame times, the renderer's CPU and GPU time, draw calls, objects, primitives, physics step, video memory, node, light (with shadows), decal, particle and mesh counts, managed heap, bytes allocated per frame, collections, working set | ms, counts, MB | per 5 s | `client/PerfProbe.cs` | test aid | - | - |

### The networked Ork: model and locomotion (Ork O7a; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

A player whose class has the Ork race (`Races.Of(config, class, team) == Race.Orks`) is drawn as an Ork: the boy's original skinned meshes on the boy's own rig
(`OrkAssets`, a rig of 51 bones, so a character is replaced, not re-skinned, when its player changes race), its weapons on the boy's prop bones (`WeaponRig`, O6) and
its movement from the boy's own clips. Code: `client/NetworkView.Ork.cs` (hooks in `NetworkView.cs` `Place` / `Spawn`, `NetworkView.Appearance.cs` `EnsureModel`,
`NetworkView.Weapons.cs`, `NetworkView.Death.cs`, `NetworkView.Prewarm.cs`, `CharacterViewer.LegIk.cs`, `WeaponAssets.FromCatalogue`), engine-free rules in
`SmContent/OrkLocomotion.cs` (`OrkLookRules`, `OrkLocomotionPlan`, `OrkPitchClip`; tests `OrkLocomotionTests`). `smtool graph-dump --gaits --rig ork` prints the plan and the
measured gaits, `--bones --rig ork` the skeleton. `--no-ork-model` (test aid) draws Orks as the default marine, as before O7a. **Not done here** (done in O7b / O7c, next section):
hit reactions, the charge clip, melee swings, the dodge hop, the death clips, the shot recoil, the reload clip, the throw's release mapping; still absent: the body-turn / run-start
/ foot-pin rules of the marines (the boy's graphs have none), Ork sounds (O8).

### The networked Ork: actions and reactions (Ork O7b / O7c; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

The boy's own clips for what an Ork does and what happens to it, laid over the times the simulation already runs (the marine's timings for reactions and the throw, the Ork's own
from O4 for the choppa, the charge and the hop). Code: `client/NetworkView.OrkActions.cs` (`OrkActionPose`, in the marines' order: reaction, charge, melee, hop, throw, then
locomotion with the recoil and the reload over it; hooks in `NetworkView.cs` `Place` / `SetUpClasses`, `NetworkView.ClipSmoothing.cs`, `NetworkView.Reload.cs`,
`NetworkView.Reactions.cs`, `NetworkView.Death.cs`, `NetworkView.Weapons.cs`); engine-free reader and rules in `SmContent/OrkActions.cs` (`OrkActions`, `OrkActionPlan`,
`OrkActionRules`; tests `OrkActionsTests`), read with the locomotion on one worker (`OrkLocomotionBundle.Actions`; the action clips are decoded there too). `smtool ork-actions
<game-dir|auto>` prints every clip, its timing and the rate it plays at. Test aids: `--no-ork-actions` (the O7a movement pose only), `--ork-capture <dir>` (windowed client:
screenshots of each action half way, inside the private data folder). The marine and Chaos paths are unchanged (`Place` hands a character on the Ork rig to `PlaceOrk` first; the
marine hooks only skip the Ork class's clips, which are not marine-rig clips). Labels: *original asset loaded* for every clip; the stretching of a clip to the simulation's time is
**ours** (design section 5: "stretched to the sim's marine timings"; parity: the Ork keeps the Tactical's reaction, throw and hop timings), the choices of clip where the boy has no
exact one are **interpretation**.

### Ork sounds and barks (Ork O8; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

What the data binds for the Ork Boy and what the client plays for it. Read with `smtool ork-sounds <game-dir|auto>` (each sound and speech command of the boy's blueprint
`ork_coop_boy` and the Ork wargear resolved against the banks: voices per post, the speech bank's line for his voice; then the behaviour tags of the boy rig's clips and what binds
them). Code: `SmContent/OrkSounds.cs` (names, rules, tested in `OrkSoundTests`), `SoundTriggers` (the Ork blueprint joins `PlayerBlueprints`; the boy rig's clip tags join the marine
rig's table; the Ork class's speech character is the blueprint's), `client/NetworkView.Sound.Ork.cs`, hooks in `NetworkView.Sound.cs` (`BlueprintName`, `SoundOrk`), `NetworkView.Match.cs`
(`OrkKillSound`) and `SoundSystem.StopSpeech`. A player of the Ork race sounds as an Ork whether or not the Ork model is drawn; before O8 it played the marine blueprint's spawn and death
sounds and nothing else. `--log-sound ork` prints every Ork post with the voices it resolved to; `--no-ork-silly` switches off the roar and taunt (ours).

### Added content: Musou Mode (TF0 contracts, TF1 map, TF3 Guardsmen and leashed defenders; no protocol change)

The owner's decision (2026-11-01): Musou Mode is this war. `--content musou` runs the war on the composed map `tfw_war`; the 5-wave run stays only as a test aid
(`--map mp_tdm_09`). Since pass 2's M1 the map is Manufactorum from the player's install and a closed Stormbird room (placeholder demonstration); the war's own numbers join this table with
their milestones. Contract and code: `docs/added-content.md` section 8.

### Added content: Musou Mode: the war between the battles (TF2: `WarSim`, not yet driven by a match)

`WarSim` and `WarRules` (pure, deterministic, stepped at 1 Hz in war seconds: real seconds × the time scale; TF4 connects them to the run). Every number is a proposal to check in a playtest. Calibration, with these values (`WarSimTests`, scripted runs, no playtest): an unattended war first besieges an HQ at 33.1 min and loses one at 47.2 min; in the hub 188.7 min (× 4.00); three wins on lane B (8 min battle, 1 min hub, 5 s travel, 20 s pickup) open the final assault at 28.2 min with no siege; with an assumed 8 min final assault a run takes 37.3 min.

| Parameter (the war) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| War time scale | 0.25 in the hub; 1.0 in travel, battle and pickup; 0 in the final assault and after the end; the battle's own lane is frozen in the Battle phase only (so it runs during a pickup); the wound timers run on the war clock even there | × real time | per step | `WarRules.TimeScale`, `WarSim.Step` | the design's calibrated proposal (section C), unchanged by TF2's tuning; the pickup and the wound timer our reading | ours | low |
| War start | Imperial 100, Ork 110; fronts A 1, B 0, C 1; progress 0 | strength, front | at start | `WarRules` | the design's calibrated proposal (section C), unchanged by TF2's tuning | estimate | low |
| War front step | m = (lord present 1.25) × (front -1: 1.5); a = (m·I − O)/(m·I + O), 0 when both are 0; progress += a·dt/30, within -1 to 1 | — | per war second | `WarRules`, `WarSim` | the design's calibrated proposal (section C), unchanged by TF2's tuning | estimate | low |
| War strengths | I −= 0.0002·O·dt, O −= 0.0002·I·dt; I += 0.03·dt, cap 200; O += 0.035·(1 + clock/1800)·dt, cap 250; both from the step's starting values, floor 0 | strength | per war second | `WarRules`, `WarSim` | the design's calibrated proposal (section C), unchanged by TF2's tuning; the floor ours | estimate | low |

### Added content: Musou Mode: gore (Musou pass 2 M10, owner items 8, 22 and 23; client only, no protocol change)

The owner (2026-11-01, verbatim): "add excessive gore to this gamemode. i'm talking Project Brutality DOOM mod levels of gore. [...] don't add the blood on screen effects, just the blood spatters/gore objects flying through the air, spilling to the ground, signficant gore. only player character and retainer allies and space marines's attacks should produce gore though." Item 23: "Make enemies are killed by explosions or frag Grenades or shot by lascannon explode in a bloody explosion." Item 22: "Include a visual "cleave" effect that denotes who got hit with a slashing bloody visual." Everything here is client presentation in `client/Extras/Musou/Gore/` (the engine-free rules and field in `src/SmNet/Extras/Musou/Gore/`); nothing reaches the simulation or the wire. Not for PvP: it runs only under `--content musou` (`MusouActive`), never headless, and not with `--no-musou-gore`. Every value is ours (inspired by the Project Brutality mod; no asset of it is used: shapes, shaders and colours are generated).

The line is a level circle segment round the swinger's feet, as wide as the cleave (`MusouCleaveShape`, the server's own volume: in the war **240 degrees** (120 to each side) for every melee weapon, reach the cleave range x 1.3; in the 5-wave run the core cone x 1.5; the power spear's sweep its own in both, **15 m** and **150 degrees** to each side (300), through `SpearRules.Sweep`, the one function the server's `World.ArsenalCleave` reads too), centred on the heading, **through the enemies struck**: at their mean flat distance from the swinger, at least **1.5 m**, at most the cleave's reach, and at their mean chest height (1.1 m when none is known). It faces the camera along the curve and, like the strokes, has no depth test and draws over every model but the striker's own (Forward+ and Mobile: the stencil twins). The Compatibility renderer has no stencil: no twins are made there, another player's arc also draws over his own model, and the own player's arcs are depth tested with every vertex pulled **1 m** toward the eye along its sight line (its place on the screen unchanged): the own model in front of the line hides it, the Orks it runs through do not, a wall or model more than 1 m in front of the line does (ours, low). The own swing's arc comes at the predicted strike (every melee weapon) through the enemies the client sees in the cleave (picked with `MusouCleaveShape`: reach, cone and count, the spear's too), otherwise with the server's report of that swing, from the strike's pose; a report is the swing's only within 0.6 s of the strike, while a melee step is still in progress and no charge is. Another player's (an AI Marine's too) comes once a frame's reported hits are in (one arc per player and server tick; the same step reported again within 0.25 s is the same swing; an arc still waiting from an earlier tick when a later tick's hit comes, a backlog after a hitch, is drawn first). A melee hit with no swing behind it (a charge's contact, the spear's impale, the air slash's landing, anyone the client has no state for) keeps the old stroke. Colours and the 30 m limit (from the swinger) are the strokes'. `--musou-old-slashes` restores the strokes on every enemy; test aids `--musou-slash-arc-radius f` (the line at f times the reach; 1: the hitbox's edge), `--log-musou-arcs` | m, degrees | per swing | `MusouSlashArcRules`, `MusouCleaveShape`, `MusouSlashArcView`, `NetworkView.MusouSlashArc.cs` | the owner (one line along the swing's cleave, overlapping its targets); the width is the cleave's rules (`MusouSlashArcTests` pins it to the server's cleave in a real World: war and 5-wave run, plain and track-to-hit steps, no weapon, the hammer, the spear); the radius through the targets (not the reach: at the reach, 8.8 to 10.7 m, the line ran far past the Orks struck), the floor, height and timing ours | owner's decision / ours | low |
| Melee slash arc: sweep, fade, thickness | the line sweeps from one end of the arc to the other in **0.12 s** in the swing's direction (the light chain alternates, its first step from the swinger's right to the left; a heavy strike from the right; no swing direction is known per step), holds **0.05 s**, fades over **0.22 s** (0.39 s in all; a 0.03 s rise, eased, no pop); thickness **0.16 m** for a light step, **+8 %** for each later step of the chain (at most +32 %), **0.26 m** for a heavy strike; pointed at both ends, brightest at the sweep's head; the power sword's brightness x1.35 (its stroke style) | s, m | per swing | `MusouSlashArcRules.SweepSeconds`, `HoldSeconds`, `FadeSeconds`, `Width`, `Direction` | ours | ours | low |

The path is sampled from the swing's own animation clip: the melee weapon's tip (the far end of its mesh's longest axis from the grip, an estimate: the models have no tip locator) through **28 samples from 0.30 s before to 0.12 s after the strike's hit time**, in the swinger's frame, once per clip and weapon (cached). Only the fast part is kept (the tip's steps at least **35 %** of its fastest) and only the part inside the cleave's cone (half angle of `MusouCleaveShape`); the directions seen from the chest are held to **-60 .. +75 degrees** of elevation, smoothed once and resampled evenly (36 segments), stretched about its middle (azimuth and elevation together, so its tilt and curve stay) over the cleave's span when it sweeps under it (at most 2.5 times; none for a chop that sweeps under 15 degrees), and put out at the cleave radius with no point lower than 0.1 m above the swinger's feet level (the line has no depth test). A path is cached per clip, weapon, cleave half angle and body; when the swinger's posed clip is none of the swing's own clips (and there is more than one) the level arc is drawn, `--log-musou-arcs` says why. A path with under 4 usable samples or under **30 degrees** of travel, or a swing with no model or weapon in hand, draws today's level arc instead. Colours, sweep, fade, thickness, stencil, no-depth and the Compatibility path are the arc's. ### Added content: Gore: the dark blood (second pass, 2026-11-01; client only, no protocol change; `ContentExtras.Gore` and Musou Mode)

The owner (2026-11-01, verbatim): "use the gore in the video reference as inspiration for the gore system in musou mode. i want the blood to be dark, shaped the way it is there [...] the new gore effects should be implemented only into musou mode and classic pvp mode with the 'extended' toggle on. no extra gore should be in the 'faithful' version." Then, after playing it: "currently the blood clouds don't appear consistently. ensure they always appear when damaging an ork with either melee or ranged attacks, or explosives [...] essentially, turn up the gore 200%. make the clouds bigger, make the blood textures bigger, make there be more of it all. i like the way it looks though, keep that. make the clouds much much bigger." The look follows the game's own trailer (a reference; nothing of it is stored). This section replaces the look and the amounts of the Musou gore rows above where they differ; the rules of who makes gore and the death queue's budgets are kept.

### Added content: Musou Mode: the original blood (gore-original, 2026-11-07; client only, no protocol change)

The owner (2026-11-07, verbatim): "use this video from the original game as a reference for the gore effects of all melee and ranged weapons. make the gore and blood splatters and clouds look and behave just like this reference and the original game." His answer to the scope question (choice 1): "choice 1, but since it is musou mode multiply the volume and magnitude of the blood effects by 1.5x". In Musou Mode the original's own Ork blood replaces the dark trailer gore of the section "Gore: the dark blood" (`--old-musou-gore` brings that back, `--no-musou-gore` shows none); classic PvP is unchanged. The reference is his 1.8 s recording of an Exterminatus match (a Raptor's hammer kill on an Ork; frames in the private cache `previews\gore-reference`): an impact glow at 0.24 to 0.34 s, at 0.37 s a red flash and dark red ink streaks thrown 1 to 2 m, a dark crimson see-through cloud 2 to 3 m wide that fades by about 1.2 s, dark red splats left on the floor. `smtool ork-blood auto` prints the data below.

### Added content: Musou Mode: melee and firepower (pass 2, M5, owner items 7, 21, 22, 24; `TfwRules.Version` 13, no protocol change)

The owner (2026-11-01, verbatim): item 7 "if a marine runs through or charges through or otherwise forcibly connects with a marine, they should forcefully be pushed out of the way (ragdoll). they get back up after, most of the time (sometimes they die). the small ork fodder should act the same way as guardsmen when they are melee attacked or charged into, but run or walked into into should move them out of the way the same way as guardsmen"; item 21 "Make frag grenades explosions much bigger and make the player character throw three grenades in a spread"; item 22 "Make cleave even more, up to 20 enemies hit in one swing"; item 24 "Allow all ranges weapons to penetrate more enemies". All of it is `TfwCombatRules`, read only through `MusouSim.War`, which only `World.StartTfw` sets: no core file changed, Annihilation, Seize Ground and the 5-wave aid never see it (`PvpCombatIsolationTests`, `MusouIsolationTests`, `MusouSkirmishPinTests`).

### Added content: Musou Mode: retainer paint, the class change in the Stormbird and the elites' bars (pass 2, M7 and M11; no protocol change, `TfwRules.Version` 15)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-01 (verbatim). Item 1: "in musou mode your retainer allies should have the same armor color scheme as the player's selected custom loadout." Item 2: "in the stormbird, when the player selects 'deploy as selected custom class' in the customizer UI, he should instantly switch classes on the fly instead of needing to die and respawn to switch. make the player model be completely covered in a cloud of smoke that fades away after 2 seconds (to transition the class change)." Item 14: "add a health bar above elite's heads. it's always visible." Code: `GameServer.TfwLook.cs`, `TfwRun.Class.cs`, `GameServer.TfwClass.cs`, `TfwBars.cs`, `GameServer.TfwBars.cs`, `client/Extras/Musou/Tfw/` (`NetworkView.TfwClass.cs`, `TfwSmoke.cs`, `TfwBarsView.cs`). Tests: `TfwClassBarsTests`. Every number below is an estimate for a playtest to refine.

The retainer's class stays the Tactical, only the paint, pieces and badges follow; the owner's emblem needs nothing (the owner shows it, so the blob is served and kept already).
