### Added content: Musou Mode: fire support (M8, M9: `TfwFire`, `World.TfwFire.cs`, `TfwFireView.cs`; no protocol change, `TfwRules.Version` 15)

The owner's items 10, 12 and 13, then his change of 2026-11-01: "make the artillery strikes be 'orbital support' that i can aim at a point on the ground with my crosshair. give me a keybind for activating it. the barrage should start instantly." So no barrage falls at random. The Thunderhawk runs of item 13 are paused by the owner: `TfwFireRules.RunsEnabled` is false, so the rows on them describe code that never runs in a match. The same day he removed the strike's cooldown and the flyby from the war's sounds (`TfwRules.Version` 16). Only in a battle of Musou Mode. The reference for the look is Post Scriptum's artillery; the sounds are the install's, and the banks name no artillery, whistle or war bed (docs/discovery.md, S0), so those are stand-ins. Heard by nobody yet: every level below is the mixer's arithmetic.

| Parameter (fire support) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Orbital strike | B calls one on the point under the crosshair (the key given up by any action for the match, restored on exit; keyboard and mouse only). The server decides: a battle on, the caller in it and alive, the point on the battlefield. No barrage at random | | on the call | `World.TfwOrbital`, `TfwOrders.cs` | the owner (2026-11-01) | owner's knowledge | high |
| Strike cooldown | **60** s per player after each strike in a battle (since 2026-11-06, `TfwRules.Version` 25): a call within it is refused by the server and not sent by the client; the HUD's line reads "B ORBITAL STRIKE IN n S" in grey (n whole seconds rounded up, own block byte 14), then "READY" in gold. **At the Firing Range none**: every press calls one and starts no cooldown (a cooldown from a battle does not apply there). ### Added content: Musou Mode: drop pod assault (`docs/drop-pod-assault.md`, `TfwDropPod.cs`, `World.TfwDropPod.cs`, `NetworkView.TfwDropPod.cs`; `TfwRules.Version` 75, `MusouSim.Version` and `Protocol.Version` unchanged)
The owner's words (2026-11-12): the second support ability, chosen per loadout in the customizer's SUPPORT ABILITIES step (the first is the artillery strike); B marks a point as the artillery strike does; a few seconds later a drop pod falls from the sky with a streak of fire and smoke, the screen shakes hard, the doors drop open and 4 tactical marines fight for 30 seconds, retreat to the Imperial HQ and vanish. Musou Mode only; Classic PvP has no support call. The owner gave only the numbers marked "owner"; every other value is ours.

### Death effects (F-D1; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

The effects the original multiplayer data itself binds to a marine's or Chaos marine's death (faithful content, not the gore extras of `docs/gore-design.md`). Read at run time from the install by `SmContent/DeathEffects.cs`
(`DeathEffects`, `DeathAction`, `DeathEffectRules`; tested in `DeathEffectsTests`), played by `client/NetworkView.DeathFx.cs` when the ragdoll starts. Evidence, with the `smtool baf-dump` calls that found it: `docs/discovery.md` "Death effects (F-D1)".
Nothing is severed or removed: the marine armour has no stump or wound geometry, and the effects are particles at bones. Open question for the owner: did a plasma or melta kill visibly remove a limb or the body in multiplayer? (The data names the effects "limb vanish" and "vaporize limb", and a `remove_wargear` step makes the corpse's ranged weapon disappear 1.2 s after a plasma death; no mesh element is in any of them.)

### Flying hitboxes, the view fraction, the grenade bounce and the bots' damage scale (fix/hitboxes-grenades-bots; protocol 37)

From the owner's playtest (2026-10-29, verbatim): "it feels difficult to shoot enemy assault marines or raptors while they're flying. check on their hitboxes. also they're
absolutely murdering me quickly with their bolt pistols. reduce all bot damage by 66% temporarily for testing purposes." and "grenades shouldn't bounce so far when thrown."
Code: `src/SmSim/FlightHitVolumes.cs` (`FlightVolumes`, `SimConfig.HitBody`), `src/SmContent/PosedHitVolumes.cs`, `src/SmContent/FlightHitVolumes.cs`, `src/SmSim/RewindFraction.cs`
(`World.SeenAt`, `World.Between`), `GameClient.ViewOf`, `RigidSpec.Bounce` / `GroundMaterial`, `OwnerBalance.WithGrenadeBounce`, `src/SmSim/DamageScale.cs`, `--bot-damage-scale`.
Probes: `smtool hitbox-probe <game-dir|auto>`, `FlyingHitboxProbe` and `GrenadeBounceProbe` (install tests, skipped without the install); synthetic tests `FlyingHitboxTests`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Shots from 20 m (8 directions x 3 elevations) at the centre of each drawn volume, every flight clip at fractions 0 to 1 by 0.1: **the rest volumes took 73.6 % of the shots aimed at the drawn torso (head, chest, pelvis) and 70.8 % of those at any drawn volume** | m, % | per shot | `smtool hitbox-probe auto` | install (rig, ragdoll, clips; read-only), 2026-10-29 | measured | high |

Shots, cones, projectiles' direct hits and pierce exits use them; blasts, melee and the charge still measure to the rest chest height. Posed by every client and the server from its own install; the config hash covers the clip names, keys and counts, not the posed values (platform maths may differ in the last bits; the server alone hits with them). Measured by `smtool hitbox-probe` (geometry: 99.9 % of the shots at the drawn torso hit when the set is the drawn one) and `FlyingHitboxProbe` (below) | m | per shot | `SimConfig.FlightHitVolumes`, `FlightVolumes`, `SmContent.FlightHitVolumes`, `PosedHitVolumes`, `SimConfig.HitBody` | clips, bones, mapper and shapes extracted; that the original's hit test followed the animated pose is an **interpretation** (the hit test is in the executable); the 9 steps are ours | interpretation | medium |

### Display names: the bots' names (names/bot-lore; protocol 41)

The owner's request (2026-10-29, verbatim): "give the bots lore accurate names instead of the current P1, P2, etc." SM1 multiplayer showed each player's own
account name and had no bots; **every name and rule here is ours**. Code: `src/SmNet/PlayerNames.cs` (the pools, the choice, the sanitiser), `src/SmServer/GameServer.Names.cs`
(naming on the server), `ScoreEntry.Name` (the wire), `GameClient.NameOf` (the client's names), `NetworkView.HudName` (every place a name is drawn). Tests: `PlayerNameTests`.

### Player collision (sim/player-collision; protocol 43, used by the simulation)

From the owner's request (2026-10-29, verbatim): "improve player model collision. the models shouldn't get stuck inside each other." Before this branch players did not
collide with each other at all in the simulation: every player's movement step saw only the level, the props and the other side's spawn-room blockers, so two players
walked, charged, were knocked and landed straight through each other; only the cameras were pushed out of bodies (M40-T6) and the charge's contact test measured
distances. The original's Havok character proxies block each other (players cannot stand inside each other in SM1), but how its controller resolves them is not decoded:
every rule below is ours. Code: `src/SmSim/PlayerCollision.cs` (`PlayerCollision`, `BodyView`, `PlayerBody`), `src/SmSim/WorldBodies.cs` (`World.RecordBodies`,
`BodiesFor`, `LeastCrowded`), `Movement.Step` / `Glide` / `Fly`, `src/SmNet/GameClient.Bodies.cs`, `GameServer.WithBoundedBody`, `src/SmNet/DrawnBodies.cs`,
`client/NetworkView.Bodies.cs`, `src/SmSim/OverlapProbe.cs`. Tests: `PlayerCollisionTests`. Test aids: server `--no-player-collision` (with the same switch on every client:
config hash) and `--log-overlaps`; client `--no-player-collision`, `--no-body-separation`; a bot logs drawn overlaps and prediction corrections every 10 s.

| Parameter (sim/player-collision) | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Who collides | every living player with every other living player, allies and enemies alike, in every way of moving (walk, sprint, sprint stop, evades, knockback, the charge and the dash attack, melee lunges and the lock's root motion, jump-pack flight, the pound and slash dives, falls); the dead (ragdolls), pickups and projectiles do not; `SimConfig.PlayerBodies` (on; off only with the test switch, hashed only when off) | — | per tick | `Movement.Step` / `Glide` / `Fly`, `PlayerCollision` | the owner's request; the scope ours | ours | medium |
| Body shape | the character capsule already used against the level: radius 0.45 m, 1.9 m tall, upright, the same for every class (the Ork too); two players touch when their axes are 0.9 m apart and their heights overlap | m | per tick | `SimConfig.CapsuleRadius`, `CapsuleHeight` | the existing placeholder capsule (the ragdoll's hit volumes stick out further at the pads and the backpack) | ours | low |
| What a step collides with (prediction-exact) | the others as the stepping player's client last knew them: each input names the newest snapshot its client held when it was sampled (`PlayerInput.BodyTick`, one byte on the wire: ticks back from the input, 1 to 24; 0 = none); the server keeps every tick's end state for 64 ticks (`World.RecordBodies`, the same floats the snapshot after it carries) and both sides take that tick's living players. The client's prediction, its replays and the server therefore step with the same bodies (measured with a temporary trace over 16,300 ticks of an 8-bot run: no tick where client and server stepped the same input from the same state with different bodies); a step depends only on past ticks, so the server's player order changes nothing | ticks | per input | `World.BodiesFor`, `GameClient.BodyTickFor` / `BodiesFor`, `PlayerCollision.See` | ours (standard client prediction; the original was peer-hosted) | ours | medium |
| Others carried on to now | each body is moved on from the snapshot by its velocity there for the ticks up to the input's tick, at most 10 ticks (0.33 s, about the lag at 150 ms RTT) and 3 m, horizontally only; the carry stops where the body would touch the stepping player (it could not have walked through it) and is dropped when the two already overlapped in the snapshot and the body was coming closer. Without the carry two sprinters meet a round trip too late and run through each other; without the stop a runner who stopped against the player is carried on past it | ticks, m | per input | `PlayerCollision.See`, `Where`, `MaxExtrapolationTicks`, `MaxExtrapolation` | ours | ours | low |
| Blocking and sliding | the part of a move going into a body the player touches or overlaps is removed; the rest sweeps the two capsules' circles (0.9 m) and slides along the first one met (up to 4 slides a tick, no tunnelling at any speed); the velocity loses what went into the body, as against a wall (a blocked charge or lunge stops at contact range, 0.9 m between axes) | m | per tick | `PlayerCollision.Resolve` | ours | ours | medium |
| Push apart | two capsules that overlapped sideways in the snapshot are pushed apart along the line between their axes there (a tie on one spot: one of 8 fixed directions from the two ids, opposite for each): each player moves out **half** the overlap (the other half is the other's own step), less what it has already moved out along that line since the snapshot, at most **3 m/s**; the push is not velocity. Measuring from the snapshot keeps a crowd from rocking (pushing on the stale picture of now overshot by a round trip's worth). Two players on one spot are 0.9 m apart after 5 ticks | m/s | per tick | `PlayerCollision.Push`, `SeparationSpeed` | ours | ours | low |
| On a head | feet within 0.3 m below another capsule's top and at most 0.05 m above it are on its head: not blocked sideways, they slide off at **6 m/s** (the whole overlap); a body coming down onto a head (a fall, a jump-pack landing) is held at the head's top, not grounded and not falling, until it has slid off (2 to 5 ticks); a ground pound's or slash's dive lands on the head in the tick it touches it (review fix: its impact then, at the head's height, not 0.1 to 0.3 s later beside the victim), then slides off in its recovery; bodies above a player's head band are the upper player's to resolve | m, m/s | per tick | `PlayerCollision.Relate`, `Finish`, `OnTopBand`, `HeadReach`, `SlideOffSpeed` | ours | ours | low |
| The charge and the dash attack | a body stops the charge's motion but is not a wall: the wall test (the collision stop) is the level's move alone; meeting a player is the contact's business (`World.ResolveRush`: an enemy is hit, an ally stops it), now at most at contact range | — | per tick | `Rush.Move` | ours | ours | low |
| Charge against a target that brakes (playtest item) | the charge is stopped 0.9 m from the target as the charger's client carried it on (its velocity at the snapshot); a target that braked or turned since is really farther, so the charge can stop short and its contact (2 x 0.45 + 0.3 m, on the rewound target) whiff where it hit before player collision. To check in a playtest: charges at targets that stop or dodge late | m | per charge | `PlayerCollision.See`, `Rush.Contact` | ours | ours | low |
| Evades | a roll, hop or dash met by a body within the wall-hit angle ends as at a wall; the push apart is left out of that test (review fix: being pushed by a stale overlap is not being stopped, so a roll started while overlapping does not end at once) | ° | per tick | `Evade.Step`, `PlayerCollision.LastPush` | ours | ours | low |
| Spawns | as before every spawn skips spots within 2 m of a living player when a free one exists; when none is free it now takes the spot whose nearest living player is farthest (before: the rotation's next, possibly on top of someone); placeholder spawns (no map) move out to a wider circle when within 1 m of a living player | m | per spawn | `World.ChooseSpawn`, `TryStartAreaSpawn`, `LeastCrowded`, `PlaceholderSpawn` | ours | ours | low |
| Server bound (review fix) | the world itself never collides with a picture older than **24 ticks** (0.8 s: the shot rewind's 15 ticks plus the view slack): an older body tick is raised to 24 ticks back, and on the server (`World.BoundBodies`) so is none (lag byte 0, or a lag beyond 24, which the wire drops to 0), whatever the client acknowledges, so a client cannot shed the bodies and walk through players; tools and tests without the bound keep 0 = no bodies. On top, a body tick older than the snapshot the input's batch acknowledged, less the view slack (the longest interpolation delay + 4 ticks), is raised to that bound. An honest client names its newest snapshot and predicts exactly; one whose newest snapshot is more than 24 ticks old (over about 450 ms RTT, or a stall) or a join's first ticks before its first snapshot predict without bodies while the server has them. A repeated input (lost packets) keeps its body tick relative to its own tick | ticks | per input | `World.BodiesFor`, `World.BoundBodies`, `PlayerCollision.MaxBodyLagTicks`, `GameServer.WithBoundedBody`, `BodySlack` | ours | ours | medium |
| Drawn remote players (client only) | remote players are drawn between snapshots in the past and the own player in the present, so bodies the simulation keeps apart can still be drawn inside each other: each overlapping pair of drawn living players (heights overlapping) is moved apart along the line between their axes, half each, all of it on the remote when the other is the own player (never moved), 3 passes, each body at most **0.45 m** from its interpolated place; positions of the drawing only, visual only (the simulation, the server's hit tests and the shots are untouched; buffers reused, no per-frame allocation); `--no-body-separation` draws them as interpolated | m | per frame | `DrawnBodies.Separate`, `NetworkView.DrawnRemotes` | ours | ours | low |
| Measured: synthetic world (no network) | sprinting head-on (9 m/s each) with a view lag of 1 / 4 / 9 ticks: worst overlap 1 / 17 / 17 cm, face to face at the end (before: straight through); 0.2 m off head-on: they slide past each other, worst 2 cm / none / none; a locked melee combo, a 3 m knockback toward a bystander, a charge into an ally, a jump-pack landing on a head: never inside (before: 69 cm into the bystander, 41 cm into the ally); 8 players pushing into one point for 4 s at lag 3, then standing still for 1 s: apart (clearance 0.000 m) and the same result whatever the server's player order | m | per run | `PlayerCollisionTests` | measured | measured | high |
| Measured: prediction in a crowd (150 ms RTT, 10 ms jitter, 5 % loss, 8 clients pushing into the middle for 17 s, then standing 3 s) | position mismatches between each client's prediction and the server: **8 and 0 with collision, 8 and 0 without** (two seeds; the 8 are the loss's); correction p99 0 m both; closest-pair overlap while pushing 0.18 / 0.27 m mean (without: 0.76 / 0.73 m); after standing still 3 s: apart (0.05 / 0.00 m; without: −0.66 / −0.67 m) | m | per run | `PlayerCollisionTests.Prediction_matches_the_server_in_a_crowd_at_150ms_rtt_and_5pct_loss` | measured | measured | high |
| Measured: 8 melee bots on Manufactorum (headless, 127.0.0.1, 4 v 4 Tacticals with `--bot-melee`, 120 s, before = `--no-player-collision`) | server, ticks with a pair overlapping (of ticks with a pair): > 1 cm 27.2 % → **5.9 %**, > 5 cm 26.8 % → 4.3 %, > 20 cm 22.2 % → **2.0 %**; closest −0.87 → −0.81 m (a transient in a brawl). Drawn by the bots (frames): > 5 cm 27 to 33 % → 0 to 2.4 % (median 0.06 %), > 20 cm 22 to 28 % → 0 to 0.5 %. Prediction corrections above 1 mm per bot: 4 to 13 before, 4 to 13 after (deaths and unpredicted hits; p99 0 m both). A first run after the build (both runs on one loaded PC) showed 70 to 164 above 1 mm with collision; a traced rerun found no disagreement between the client's and the server's bodies, and the repeat above showed the same counts as without: logged as a load outlier | %, m | per run | server `--log-overlaps`, the bots' "bodies:" lines | measured | measured | medium |
| Protocol 43 | inputs 40 bytes (39 + the body lag byte); snapshots unchanged (worst case 1200); the config hash unchanged unless collision is switched off | bytes | per message | `Protocol` | ours | engineering | high |
| Armour flashes on character models (fx/character-visuals) | **owner's decision (2026-10-30):** armour damage while armour remains: a subtle yellow flash on the model; the armour breaks: a subtle red flash; the armour starts recharging: a yellowish glow with a strong outline (his reference). Seen by everyone. Own model: exact from the predicted shield. Others: derived (no wire change: slim records carry no shield): a hit with the shot record's armour bit up flashes yellow; the first hit that finds it down flashes red (one hit late); the glow starts the class's regeneration delay after the last damage seen (melee and splash out of view are not seen). Flash lengths 0.22 s (hit), 0.4 s (break), glow 1.1 s; strengths 0.2 / 0.2 / 0.4 additive (rim-weighted) and the outline 2.8 cm thick; colours (1, 0.82, 0.15) / (1, 0.12, 0.08) / (1, 0.78, 0.22), outline (1, 0.86, 0.35) | s / colour | per frame | `ArmourFlashTracker`, `CharacterViewer.SetArmourFlash`, `NetworkView.CharacterFlash.cs` | the owner's words and reference image; every number ours | owner's decision; estimate (values) | low |

### Combat pass: the charge key, holstered reloads, headshots, directional melee, the ledge charge's fall (sim/combat-pass; protocol 45, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-30, items 8, 10, 12, 19, 21 (his decisions and recollections; the headshot values are the install's). Code: `Combat.StepPlayerCore`
(the charge key, the holstered reloads, the melee direction), `Rush.WHeld`, `Rush.DashOffset`, `PlayerState.OtherReloadLeft` / `ThirdReloadLeft` / `MeleeDirection`, `FallRules.ChargeShowsFall`
(client). Tests: `CombatPassTests`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| The charge is purely W + F | an F (heavy) press with W held (the stick's forward part at least 0.7) is the charge or nothing: when the charge cannot start because its spacing since the last one (`min_time_between_activations`, 1 s) is not over, or the body is in the air, the press is never a stun strike (struck or queued mid-combo) and is **buffered**: kept for the input buffer's window (0.3 s, an estimate) and replayed, so the charge starts on the first tick it is allowed (`InputBuffer.Locked`: a heavy press during the spacing or in the air is kept); F without W is the stun strike as before | - | per press edge | `Combat.StepPlayerCore` | the owner's decision (2026-10-30): "W held when F is pressed = charge, never a stun strike (purely W + F)" | owner's decision | high; the 0.3 s window is an estimate (the owner's follow-up decision: buffer the press); the buffer's hold rule keeps it while F stays down; the press remembers that W was held (`PlayerState.BufferedCharge`, bit 7 of the own record's slot byte) and is dropped, not struck, if W is let go before it replays |
| Reloads continue while the weapon is not equipped | a switch no longer cancels the reload in progress: the weapon keeps its own remaining time (`PlayerState.ReloadLeft` for the one in hand, `OtherReloadLeft` for the first holstered weapon, `ThirdReloadLeft` for the second one with Weapon Versatility), and a holstered weapon's reload runs down every tick and moves its rounds from the reserve into the clip when done, on its own timer (e.g. the bolter's 1.3 s); a weapon taken back in hand has what is left; a recharging weapon (plasma) holstered goes on round by round; death and respawn clear them; since protocol 56 (sim/reload-keeps; the owner 2026-11-03: "reloads should not be cancelled by anything other than switching weapons") a melee attack, a throw, a ground pound, a hit reaction or a charge no longer cancels the in-hand reload either: it runs on through them | s | per tick | `Combat.StepPlayerCore` | the owner's recollection (2026-10-30): "reloads continue while the weapon is not equipped (all weapons)"; the timers are the data's `reload_time` | owner's recollection | medium (the data says nothing about holstered weapons; the rule is his) |
| Reload while holstered: timing | the reload times are the weapons' own (data): bolt pistol 0.75 s, bolter 1.3 s, sniper 2.5 s, plasma gun 1.5 s, melta 2.5 s, heavy bolter 1.5 s, lascannon 2.25 s (the server's start-up listing) | s | per reload | `WeaponSpec.ReloadTime` | wargear `reload_time` | extracted | high |
| Headshot bonus: implemented | a hit on the head body takes the weapon's head multiplier on health and its shield-head multiplier on the armour (`WeaponSpec.HeadMultiplier` / `ShieldHeadMultiplier`, from `damage_material_multipliers/default_head` and `armourshield_damage_material_multipliers/default_head`); armour first, then the rest on health at the head multiplier; shots, charged shots and the piercing exits use them (`Combat.ApplyDamage`); nothing was missing | x | per hit | `Combat.ApplyDamage`, `Combat.HitShapes` | the install (the server's start-up listing, `smtool weapon-dps`) | extracted | high |
| Head multipliers per weapon (health x, armour x) | bolt pistol (SM, CSM, Devastator) **2.5** (armour 1); bolter, stalker bolter and the bolter pistols **2.55** (armour 0.5); sniper rifle 2 (armour 2.5); lascannon 2.25 (armour 2.25); plasma gun, plasma pistol, melta, storm bolter, grenade launcher, heavy bolter, plasma cannon 1 (the plasma weapons' armour 2) | x | per hit | `WeaponSpec` | same | extracted | high |
| The bolt pistol's headshot | 40 x 2.5 = **100** = a full marine's health: with the armour gone one headshot kills (the owner's example holds with the data's numbers); with the armour up the first headshot only takes 40 of its 100; at 40 m the fall-off (x0.78) leaves 78, not a kill | health | per hit | `Combat.ApplyDamage` | the data; the owner's example (2026-10-30) | extracted | high |
| Directional melee | the stick's way of eight (`Evade.DirectionOf`, dead zone 0.1: W, W + D, D, S + D, S, S + A, A, W + A; no stick = forward) at the tick a melee attack begins sets the facing it is struck in, relative to the view: forward 0, A / D 90 degrees, S 180, the diagonals 45 / 135 (`Rush.DashOffset`, as the dash attack's lunge); the body turns at once and the hit cone follows it, so S turns round and strikes the one behind; latched for the attack (it follows the view's turns), re-read by each combo attack and by the heavy strike; the facing is kept through the hit even when the hit comes after the move-on time (some weapons); from the move-on time the walk's frame is the view again | degrees | per attack | `Combat.StepPlayerCore`, `PlayerState.MeleeDirection` | the owner's decision (2026-10-30): "the WASD direction held at the melee press sets the attack direction relative to the camera; S = turn and strike backwards; all 8 directions incl. diagonals; no keys = forward" | owner's decision | high (the eight directions); the instant turn (no ease) is our smallest choice, an estimate |
| Directional melee: with a lock | the lock search already went along the stick (`MeleeLock.SearchDirection`); a lock the start's cone accepts still turns the body to the stick's continuous direction and then eases to the target | - | per attack | `Combat.StepPlayerCore` | unchanged (feel/melee-lock) | ours | medium |

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### Light melee flinches, nothing else (sim/light-melee-flinch; protocol 52, used by the simulation)

The owner, 2026-11-01: "combat knife should not stagger or stun an enemy, nor any light melee attack. only stun strikes, charges, stomps, and kicks should heavy stagger/stun. any light melee attack should 'flinch' ranged attacks by players shooting ranged weapons ... a melee attack landing on a player shouldn't interrupt a melee attack, hop, charge, or any other action animation. it should only 'throw off the aim'." A **deliberate change** to the data's reaction tables (`reaction_mp_melee`), in classic PvP between players, Faithful and Extended alike. Musou Mode's enemy hits on players (`MusouHit`, `TfwCombatRules`) are unchanged. Code: `World.ResolveMelee(light)`, `Spread.Flinch`, `Spread.After`, `PlayerState.FlinchTicks`. Tests: `LightMeleeFlinchTests`, `ReactionTests`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Which hits are light | every attack of the normal melee combo of every weapon (the knife's CK 1..3 and any later step, the chainsword, power sword, axe, hammer, the Ork's choppa) and the jump-pack sword slash; a light hit starts **no** interrupt, stun or stagger and no knockback, whatever the data's table says. Heavy strikes (Y, the stun strike), the charge, the stomps and the ground pound's blast, and the heavy classes' kick (their light attack, `MeleeStep.Kick`, `ability_displace_kick`) keep their reactions, as do grenades and blasts | — | per hit | `World.ResolveMelee`, `MeleeStep.Kick` | owner's decision | owner's decision | — |
| Reach of the stun-type reactions | `TryReact` is reached from: `ResolveMelee` (heavy list, the kick), `ApplyBlast` (stomps, ground pound, grenades), `ResolveRush` (the charge). A light hit goes to `Flinch` instead | — | — | `ReactionWorld.cs`, `RushWorld.cs` | code | — | — |
| The flinch's size | **6** degrees added to both scatter half-widths (past the set's maximum; a weapon without a scatter set too) of every shot fired while the flinch lasts; it falls linearly to 0 over the flinch | degrees | per shot | `SimConfig.MeleeFlinchDegrees`, `Spread.After` | owner's wish ("throw off the aim"); the number is ours | ours (estimate) | low |
| The flinch's length | **0.5** s (15 ticks at 30 Hz), restarted (never shortened) by each light hit; no stacking; on the wire in the own record (protocol 52, one byte) so the client's own shots predict exactly | s | per light hit | `SimConfig.MeleeFlinchSeconds`, `PlayerState.FlinchTicks` | ours | ours (estimate) | low |
| What a flinch is not | not a reaction: hyper armour and reaction immunity do not matter (a light hit flinches through them); a player who is not shooting loses nothing: only the client's additive hit flinch plays (presentation, `--no-hit-flinch`), which stops no action; no view kick is added | — | — | `Spread.Flinch` | owner's wish | owner's decision | — |

### The feel pass: the roll's blending for every action (anim/feel-pass; client only, not simulated, no protocol change)

Sources: the owner's playtest notes of 2026-10-30, item 15 and its interview ("the tactical roll is PERFECT ... make the rest of the animations/actions blend and transition that well and in the
same style"; most wrong: movement weight, melee impact, transitions; worst: move ↔ shoot / aim, into / out of melee, combo chains, the air slash's landing). The base graph's transitions were
read with `smtool graph-dump SM_Base_MP --no-tree` and `MP_SM_NAV_JP_Sim`. Code: `client/NetworkView.Feel.cs` (the pattern in its class comment), `NetworkView.SprintEdges.cs` (`ExitBlendOf`),
`NetworkView.Jump.cs`, `CharacterViewer.cs` (the layer fold, the clip restart), `SmNet.SlashPose.SmoothDiveTime` (test `SlashPoseTests`). Measured with `--transition-probe --transition-probe-clips`
and `--anim-probe` on one recorded session (`feel/sweep1`, 165 s, protocol 45: a Tactical with `--transition-sweep` recording, an Assault with `--slash-test`, a Raptor and a Devastator with
`--transition-sweep`, a Chaos Tactical with `--bot-melee`), replayed headless at 60 fps, `--no-feel` for the before. Test aids: `--no-feel` (every change of this section off), the probe's new
`bob` lines (the pelvis's height and sideways range over 48-frame windows of one state, by speed band), its aim / ready labels, and a replay's connect timeout of 10 minutes (a demo recorded beside
other loading clients waited more than the live 10 s for its Welcome and replayed as "no answer").

### Controller (gamepad; client only, no protocol change)

Sources: the owner's request of 2026-10-30 ("make the game controller compatible. match exactly the bindings to the original sm1. autodetect when a controller is connected and switch to that as the primary
way to control the game. when the controller is disconnected swap back to keyboard/mouse controls"); the owner's screenshot of the original's Xbox 360 binding screen (2026-10-30; kept outside the repository);
the install's locale strings (`smtool locale`: 110651-110693 the control screen's labels, 120988/120989 Sprint / Zoom Cycle, 122097 and 122101 the stick-press labels, 121466 / 121467 / 121511 / 121520 /
119788 the options for gamepad on/off, button layout, stick layout, targeting assistance and vibration, 119789-119792 the stick layouts AUTO CENTER / SOUTHPAW / LEGACY / LEGACY SOUTHPAW, 120990 the four weapon
slots), the install's `camera_input_tuning.oppc` (the look stick's speeds, mapping and damping; read by `CameraTuning`, `InputTuning.StickMapping` / `StickDamping`) and the owner's recollection (Start, Back and the
sprint click, 2026-10-30). The button-to-action assignment is in the engine, not in the data read (the `ControlMap.gfx` movie fills its labels from native code); the owner's screenshot is the authority for it.

`client/NetworkView.GamepadTest.cs` (`--pad-test`). The sampled input is the same `PlayerInput` the keyboard makes (analog stick magnitude included: the simulation scales speed by the stick's length), so the
server and the protocol are unchanged. Kind column: owner screenshot (the original's own binding screen, Xbox 360), owner recollection, data, estimate (ours).

### Sticky launcher grenades (sim/sticky-launcher; protocol 48, used by the simulation)

Source: the owner (2026-10-31): "vengeance launcher grenades should not bounce. they should instantly stick to whatever they strike. they can also stick to players." The data agrees in part: `grenade_launcher_grenade_multiplayer` has `sticky` true and `detonate_on_collision` false (row "Projectile `grenade_launcher_grenade_multiplayer`"); its `max_bounce_count` 1 is what made the old rule bounce once off the level before sticking. Code: `World.Fly`, `World.Dropped`. Tests: `ProjectileTests`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sticky shots never bounce off the level | a projectile with `sticky` stops at the first contact with world geometry (wall, floor, ceiling) at the hit point, 2 cm off the surface along its normal, and rests there until detonated; `max_bounce_count` is ignored for sticky non-rigid projectiles (the grenade launcher; the plasma pistol's sticky shot has no bounce anyway). Thrown rigid-body grenades (frag, krak) are unchanged (1 bounce, ground fuse) | — | per tick | `World.Fly` | owner's recollection; data `sticky` | owner recollection | medium |
| Stuck to a player | unchanged (protocol 7): on striking a player the grenade takes the shot's direct damage (10) and attaches at the point struck, following the player's position (walking, rolling, jump-pack, any move); detonation (R, delays 0 / 0.25 / 0.32 s, at most 3, 4th detonates the oldest) is unchanged and its blast is centred on the host's current position with the existing explosion rules: the host takes the blast's `do_damage` (75) as body, plus splash like any player in range (no direct-hit multiplier change) | — | per tick | `World.StepProjectiles`, `World.Detonate` | owner's recollection; existing rules | owner recollection | medium |
| Host dies or leaves | the grenade comes off, rests in the air for the tick and falls with full gravity (it never strikes that player again); it sticks to whatever it meets next (a floor, wall, or another player) and stays until detonated or its owner leaves. Before: it hung in the air where the host died. Round end/reset clears all projectiles (unchanged) | — | per tick | `World.Dropped` | ours | interpretation | low |
| Wire | unchanged: flags stuck / attached already exist in the 14-byte projectile record; snapshot worst case stays 1194 bytes; protocol 48 because the rules differ | bytes | — | `Protocol` | ours | — | — |

### Switch cancel (sim/switch-cancel; protocol 48: no wire change, bumped so a client of 47 cannot mispredict switches against this server; used by the simulation and the client's prediction)

Source: the owner, 2026-10-31. Code: `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (the switch branch no longer waits for the running switch), `InputBuffer.Locked` (a Switch press is not held by a switch under way), the client's `NetworkView.UpperBody` (`SwitchWeight`). Tests: `CombatPassTests`, `FivePerksTests`, `SlotTests`, `LoadoutTests`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A switch can be cancelled by a new switch | while a switch (the old weapon lowering, the new one raising) is playing, a switch request (keys 1/2/3, the cycle, the wheel, the D-pad) takes effect at once: the requested weapon is put in hand and the full switch time starts over, so firing and reloading still wait the whole switch time of the last request; naming the weapon just lowered brings it back (its own ammunition, heat and reload progress follow it as in any switch); no ammunition is lost or duplicated and holstered weapons keep reloading. The original's exact blend or time saved on a switch back is not known: the full time is the safe reading | s (the switch time, placeholder × 0.8) | per tick | `Combat.StepPlayerCore`, `InputBuffer.Locked` | the owner's recollection, 2026-10-31: "while the switching weapon animation is playing you should be able to switch weapons again instantly and cancel the existing switch animation and start equipping a new weapon" | owner recollection | medium |
| The switch animation restarts without a pop | the client starts the new switch clip pieces from the layer weight the cancelled one had reached (fading in from there over the same 0.1 s smooth curve) | s | per frame | `NetworkView.UpperBody.SwitchWeight` | ours | ours | low |

### Melee interaction pass: the charge connect locked, its impact, reactions turned to the attacker (anim/melee-interaction; protocol 48, no wire change)

Source: the owner, 2026-10-31 ("still very floaty and disconnected ... the target is stunned and plays the stun animation. the player delivering the charge ... should play the recoil
animation like he charged into a wall ... much weightier/meatier/crunchier ... charges don't consistently lock the target and charge deliverer together ... some interaction between melee
participants"). Data used: the sprint graph's `Knocked Back` state (`SM_NAV_Bullrush2Idle_F_Collision_01`, entered on `BOOL_Bullrush_Hit`: already the charger's stop on a player since
M29, now reached on every connect and on the contact tick in the own view), the stun's four `SM_MP_REC_Grenade_*` clips (unchanged), the bull rush's `body_smash` material container (effects
and `play_sm_bull_rush_smash`), the effects package's `body_smash` and `body_smash_directional`. Code: `SmSim.ChargeLock` (hooked in `World.ResolveRush` / `StopRushes`), `GameClient.ChargeLock.cs`
(prediction), `SmNet.MeleeInteraction` (presentation rules), `client/NetworkView.MeleeInteraction.cs`. Tests: `ChargeLockTests`, `MeleeInteractionTests`. Test aids: `--no-charge-lock` (server and
every client; config hash), `--no-charge-impact`, `--no-reaction-facing`, `--no-hit-flinch`, `--no-lock-draw`, `--log-charge-impact`, `--charge-shots <dir>` (capture).

Why the connect was inconsistent (measured in `ChargeLockTests` with the lock off): a player running at the charger was never met (the move was blocked by the newer body picture, 0.9 m,
while the contact tested only the rewound picture, up to 2.2 m farther at a 0.33 s view lag); a met victim stood 1.1 to 1.2 m away at up to 49 degrees off the charger's heading; the own
client's prediction never stopped at the contact (0 of 20 contact ticks predicted; with the lock 20 of 20).

### The weight pass: landing, recoil, flinch, strike entries, camera impulses (feel/weight-impact; client only, not simulated, no protocol or config-hash change)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-01: "a lot of actions and animations feel very floaty. send a pass of weight/impact to pretty much all animations/actions that i haven't specifically said feel very good". ### Movement fixes: the heavy hop down stairs and off ledges, the pound in a full jump, the short hop while falling, steering a ledge charge (sim/movement-fixes; protocol 51, no wire change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-01 (verbatim): A "devastator/havoc hop you should go down while still going foward if you go down stairs or off a ledge. currently you maintain
horizontal momentum and don't move down at all - which is pretty janky."; B "with daemon maul and thunder hammer, when full height jumping, there is a delay in which a ground pound
will trigger/work."; C "when falling as assault marine/raptor, if i am falling out of a ledge or out of a jump, i am not able to short hop (space bar tap). i should be able to perform a
short hop at any moment while falling." Code: `Evade.Step` (`HopFall`), `Evade.Begin` (`FallingBelowCurve`, the air dash's start), `Evade.CanDashInAir`, `JumpPack.Begin` (the air
tap), `InputBuffer.AirTapPending`; client `NetworkView.Fall.cs` (`EvadeFallingInAir`), `NetworkView.Jump.cs`, `NetworkView.Sound.cs`. Tests: `MovementFixesTests` (and the updated
evade, jump-pack and buffer tests). Measured with a scratch probe on the install's config (buildid 7412325, not committed).

### Stall keep-alive and freeze diagnostics (fix/stall-keepalive; client and a log filter, no protocol change)

Source: a playtester on the Compatibility renderer (AMD integrated GPU) was dropped each time his thunder hammer landed a hit; a rendered bot on that renderer with a cold shader cache froze its main thread for 13.5 s in a first draw and was dropped by the server ("timed out"). Any long freeze of the client's main thread dropped a player, because the client sent its inputs only from its frame. Code: `GameClient.KeepAlive.cs` (`KeepAliveStep`), `ClientOptions.StallKeepAlive`, `UdpClientTransport.Send` (locked), `IClientTransport.ThreadSafeSend`, `NetworkView.Stall.cs`, `ConnectionLost`, `HostedServerLog`, `FrameWatchdog`. Tests: `StallKeepAliveTests`, `ConnectionLostTests`, `HostedServerLogTests`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stall keep-alive: start | when no `GameClient.Update` has begun for **1 s**, a background thread (checks every 100 ms) re-sends the newest input batch | s | client clock | `ClientOptions.KeepAliveAfter` | ours (the server's own silence rule is 0.5 s neutral, 5 s timeout) | ours | none |
| Stall keep-alive: interval | one keep-alive every **0.5 s** while stalled (ten times inside the server's 5 s timeout) | s | client clock | `ClientOptions.KeepAliveInterval` | ours | ours | none |
| Stall keep-alive: bound | none after **30 s** of stall, so a client that is truly hung still times out | s | client clock | `ClientOptions.KeepAliveBound` | ours | ours | none |
| Stall keep-alive: content | the newest batch with every input made neutral (no movement, no buttons, no melee target; ticks, heading, pitch and view fields kept); a spectator's batch (its camera) as it is. A server of the same protocol takes it as a batch that sets `LastHeard`; its ticks are long simulated and skipped (an input at or before the server's tick is ignored), its snapshot acknowledgement is not newer (no ping sample), and the idle kick does not count it as play. The frozen player stands still, as after 500 ms of silence | - | - | `GameClient.KeepAliveStep`, `GameServer.OnInputs` | ours | ours | none |
| Stall keep-alive: scope | runs only for a live UDP connection (`IClientTransport.ThreadSafeSend`); never on a replayed demo, a recording client, or the in-process test transports; ends with the connection, on `Leave` and when the scene exits. `--no-stall-keepalive` turns it off (test aid) | - | - | `NetworkView.Stall.cs` | ours | test aid | none |
| Watchdog for human players | the frame watchdog now also runs for a human's client, reporting a frame that has not finished for **3 s** (bots and `--frame-profile`: 2 s, unchanged) in the client log | s | wall clock | `FrameWatchdog.HumanStallSeconds` | ours | ours | none |
| Slow-frame line | a frame that took **1 s** or more while connected is written to the log with the keep-alive packets sent meanwhile | s | wall clock | `NetworkView.SlowFrameLogSeconds` | ours | ours | none |
| "Connection is gone" line | names the cause: a freeze of this client (a frame of at least server timeout minus 1 s since the last snapshot), a freeze earlier in the session, or a server or network that went silent while frames ran normally; with the worst frame, the time since the last snapshot and the keep-alive count | - | - | `ConnectionLost.Text` | ours | ours | none |
| Hosted server lines in the client log | every join, every leave with its reason, every refusal, every fault note (" failed: ", "dropped after", "FATAL") with up to **14** stack lines after it, as "hosted server: ..."; the server's own throttle (the first 20 faults in full, then one in 10 s; stacks for the first 5) is the only limit | lines | per line | `HostedServerLog` | ours | ours | none |
| Test aids | `--test-freeze-at <s> --test-freeze-seconds <n>` (the main thread sleeps n s once the client has been connected s seconds), `--no-stall-keepalive` | - | - | `NetworkView.Stall.cs` | - | test aid | - |

### Added content: Musou Ork hit reactions (musou/ork-flinch; 2026-11-13; client drawing only, Musou Mode only, no protocol or hash change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-13: "use this proxy as a reference to add back in hit reactions to orks in musou mode. we previously disabled hit reactions due to the 180 degree turn on hit bug that was happening with the original animations." The reference is his motion-study preview (12 s, 24 fps; standing, running, attacking Orks). Decision file: decisions/2026-11-13-musou-ork-hit-reactions.md in the coordination repository.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hit reaction, what it is | A procedural additive flinch over the Ork's own clip: the torso tips back, the pelvis shifts away from the hit and drops, the knees bend (two-bone IK keeps the feet where the clip put them); facing, path, speed and attack phase never change. Drawn only: no simulation, wire, protocol or hash change. Every shot, blow or blast of any player that lands makes it (hit events: attacker, enemy, marker; detonations the view already plays); not the Weirdboy's shield hits, not a dying or knocked Ork | - | per hit | `MusouOrkFlinchRules`, `MusouCrowd.Hit/Blast`, `MusouOrkFlinchPose`, `NetworkView.MusouOrkFlinch.cs` | owner 2026-11-13 (hit reactions identical to the reference, translated onto the Ork animations); the lead's reading of the preview | interpretation | medium |
| Hit reaction, timing | rise **0.04** s (one frame at 24 fps), hold **0.04** s, fall **0.27** s with (1 - u)^1.5, over at **0.35** s. Measured from the reference's standing sequence (frames 25 to 49, 24 fps): the excess over the idle sway read 8.4, 8.4, 7.5, 6.0, 4.5, 3.1, 2.2, 1.5, 1.2 at 0 to 333 ms | s | per hit | `MusouOrkFlinchRules.Rise/Hold/Fall/FallPower` | owner 2026-11-13 reference v3 (measured) | estimate | medium |
| Hit reaction, pose at strength 1 | torso tipped back **38** degrees (spine 10 + 9 + 9, neck 4, head 6), pelvis and torso **0.14** m along the hit, pelvis **0.09** m down, the shift cut back for any leg the clip left too straight to follow with the foot kept. History: 11 degrees first, 19 after a pixel check against the reference (summed pixel change per figure area 9 against 15 to 26), then doubled to 38 at the owner's word of 2026-11-13 ("increase the magnitude of all ork reactions by 2x of current - keep the scaling stagger strength"); the pelvis moved in the wrong frame in the first two versions (35 to 125 mm of foot drift), fixed with the doubling | degrees, m | per hit | `MusouOrkFlinchRules.Spine1..Head, PelvisBack, PelvisDrop` | owner 2026-11-13 reference v3 (V2 reaction +30%) | ours | low |
| Hit reaction, repeated hits | each hit re-kicks to the same size (the displacement goes from where it is to the full size over the rise): no growth under automatic fire; the size is capped at **2.5** base sizes (the deepest tip 85 degrees: spine 70, the neck and head held at 15 because past that the face pointed at the sky and the head sank into the shoulders; the owner, 2026-11-13: "Let them go harder"; it was 3 while the base was half its size and 2 for a day), so heavy (2) stays below charge and a hammer or axe heavy strike (2.5), and a close blast reaches 2.5; only a hammer's charge (3.1) is clipped. | Hit reaction, explosives | an Ork inside a detonation's splash radius takes **2.5x** beside the centre fading linearly to **1x** at the edge, away from the centre; the server's hit reports of the same blast within 0.6 s add no second kick. Frags, launcher and plasma-cannon rounds arrive as detonations the view plays; the artillery and the drop pod's blast only if the view plays them as detonations (otherwise their hits read as shots: no blast event on the wire). The plasma cannon's shot as a blast is the lead's assumption | x, m | per blast | `MusouOrkFlinchRules.BlastStrength`, `MusouCrowd.Blast`, `NetworkView.MusouOrkFlinchBlast` | owner 2026-11-13; plasma cannon: lead's assumption | ours | medium |

| Hit reaction, crowd tiers | a skeletal (near) Ork poses the full flinch; a baked (far) Ork leans its whole instance about its feet by **14** degrees and shifts **0.12** m per base size; none past **70** m. At 1,000 Orks (40 skinned, 960 baked) under 1,200 hits a second the crowd's Frame() mean cost, re-measured at the doubled magnitude with the reach limit (stage aid, no render): 5.2 and 5.6 ms with the flinch against 4.4 and 4.5 ms without, so about 1 ms; one earlier run read 11.2 against 4.1 ms (worst frame 117 ms) while the machine was busy. ### Added content: Musou audio pass (musou/audio-pass; 2026-11-09; client only, Musou Mode only, no protocol, wire or hash change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-09, Musou Mode only: "ensure ork ambient voices sound like they are from far away. make the player's character barks sound full volume all the time - no muffling from explosions or persistent loud fire."; "make all 'bolter' rifle weapons have deeper, punchier, more satisfying sounds. i want to hear wet smacks and followed by explosion sounds when they impact their first target. the piercing and explosions still happen as they did before."; "the melee on hit sound effect should play longer than they currently do - they sound cut off. ensure the beginning of the sound and later end of the sound fully play - make the sound have a longer playtime". Every number is ours, to refine by ear. Gate: `MusouAudioRules.Applies` and `NetworkView.MusouAudioOn` (the Musou content flag); Classic PvP posts nothing of this and routes no voice differently (`SoundEmitter.ProtectSpeech` / `Tail` default false). Test aid `--no-musou-audio-pass` restores the 2026-11-08 sound.

Measured with `smtool audio-mix <event> --distance d --loudness`: `play_or_bo_1_growls` / `play_or_bo_2_roar`: -17.2 dB at 1 to 3 m, -21.0 at 10 m, -31.2 dB from 30 m on (the curve's floor), distance LPF 4.7 at 30 m, 9.4 at 60 m, 15 at 100 m, 18.8 at 130 m; the speech lines (`ork_boy:celebration` ...) use the speech events' curves with the loudness rule (range x2.5, floor 20 %). | Own barks | the own player's character speech (the Titus battle barks and the class exertion/action lines) is exempt from the data's Set/Reset actions (an explosion such as `play_big_damage_med_explosion` carries 11: the low-pass and volume cuts that muffled them), from instance limits and from voice stealing (it takes a player whatever the priority, and nothing steals its) and plays on `SmVoice`, straight into Master (no reverb send, no SmSfx limiter). **Falloff (fifth follow-up): none of ours.** The original plays the own character's speech as a 3D voice (its speech events carry an attenuation, `smtool audio-mix --speech titus/roar`: 3D), and the engine's own-emitter rule keeps the player's own 3D sounds at least `OwnMinDistance` = 1.5 m close; the earlier "read at 0 m" override is removed, so the voice reads its original curve at 1.5 m | - | per voice | `SoundEmitter.ProtectSpeech`, `SoundSystem.Shielded/FullVoice/BusOf` | owner 2026-11-09 | ours | medium (the master bus limiter still acts on a clipping mix: not removable) |

### Added content: the client's own volleys (musou-net-budget; client only, no protocol change)

The owner (2026-11-09): "maximize client sided rendering/drawing effects to make the battlefield feel real and intense and alive". The simulation lets few Orks shoot at a target at once (8 a player, 10 a Guard squad); every other standing gun Ork the client draws in range of a target fires bursts of its own on that client alone, drawn and heard like the server's rounds. No damage, no bytes, no server time; two clients see different volleys. `--no-musou-volleys` turns them off.

| Target | the nearest player or Guardsman **8-30** m away (flat), at most **4** m higher or lower, within **50** degrees of the Ork's facing, with a clear line from his muzzle (1.4 m up) to the target's chest (1.2 m up) at the burst's start | m, degrees | per burst | `MusouVolleyPlanner` | ours | ours | estimate |

### Added content: gore by source (musou-net-budget; client budgets and the server's event order, no protocol or wire change)

The owner (2026-11-09): "i'm not consistently seeing gore effects from both ranged and melee attacks ... ensure that all player attacks in particular - then allied space marine attacks have high priority for generating gore effects during heavy fighting." Measured with a fighting co-op bot (3 AI Marines, up to 2,200 Orks shown): one shared hit-effect bucket refused 30 % of the own near hits, 40 % of the own hits fell beyond the 30 m reach, and the full effect player (160) refused new blood 1,361 times because the crowd's tracers held a higher priority. `--musou-old-gore-budget` (client) and `SM_MUSOU_OLD_HIT_RANK=1` (server) restore the old behaviour.

### Melee cancels of hops and charges, the jump pack from a fall or a charge (feel/melee-cancels; protocol 54)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-02 ("end assault marine/raptor charges and hops with a melee attack ... the same strict cooldown based on the intended timing of the end of the animation ... tactical marine rolls should not be cancellable, and don't touch the devastator/havoc hop ... in both musou mode and classic pvp mode"; "jump with space bar hold when falling, or charging at any time no restrictions", Assault and Raptor only). Which values are the original's is not known; every row is ours or the owner's rule applied.
Code: `MeleeCancel` (new), `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (`cancelStart`, `cancelLock`, the melee lock now kept in Musou too), `JumpPack.Begin` (`airLong`, `airStart`), `PlayerState.MeleeLock` (already on the wire since protocol 53). Tests: `MeleeCancelTests`; four older tests changed (`JumpPackAttackTests`, `JumpTierTests`, `MovementFixesTests`) because their rules are superseded.

The swing the cancel started and its combo go on as usual; the lock is `PlayerState.MeleeLock` (also kept in Musou Mode, which has no other lock) and the longer of it and the combo-window lock holds. ### Charge cancel: S, not the grenade; the ally bump (charge-cancel, charge-ally-bump; protocol 66, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-11: "New way to dash cancel has emerged and it's extremely fun and easy ... Dash, then press grenade with no grenade left, to cancel a dash. In general, while smooth this isn't a good input to have do this maneuver because you have to use your grenade to do the maneuver"; "the expected behavior after your work is done is that throwing a grenade no longer cancels a bull rush/charge animation. what should cancel a charge animation is tapping or holding the S key (backpedal)"; "in classic pvp, teammates currently have collision with each other and the player. today, if you bull rush or charge and hit a friendly, your player character will play the 'recoil' or stun animation. no animation should play when hitting an ally. that animation should only play when charging or clashing with an enemy."
Code: `ChargeCancel` (new: `BackHeld`, `EndsAtBranch`, `AllyBumps`, `Bumped`), `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (the charge's other input), `World.ResolveRush` / `StopRushes` (the bump), `ChargeLock.Predict` (the own prediction), `GameClient.PredictChargeContact` (a bump is no connect: no impact presentation). Tests: `ChargeCancelTests` (30); older tests changed because their rules are superseded: `ChargeDirectionsTests` (three), `NoFireInChargeTests` (two), `ChargeLockTests` (the ally), `MeleeCooldownTests` (S, now under the restore switch).

The press is input-buffered (0.3 s), so one up to 0.3 s before the branch counted too. The S cancel and the dropped grenade cancel are the shared step's. Synthetic run: three marines of one side, 150 ms RTT, 5 % loss, 40 s, every charge cancelled with S held or tapped, mashed with Grenade (one frag, then none) or left to its end: 25 ally bumps, 4 S cancels, 1110 ticks compared per client, 0 mismatches, nothing excluded (seeds 391, 392) | - | per tick | `GameClient.PredictChargeContact`, `ChargeCancelTests` | measured | observed | high |
| Switches | `--old-charge-cancel` (a Grenade press ends every charge phase from its stick branch, S does not: protocol 65) and `--old-ally-bump` (the collision stop on an ally: protocol 65), each on the server and every client (config hash, written only when on) | - | - | `SimConfig.ChargeBackCancel`, `SimConfig.ChargeAllyBump` | restore switches | test aid | decided |
| Protocol 66 | no layout change; the rules change the simulation, so client and server must agree (renumbered at integration if another branch takes 66) | - | - | `Protocol.Version` | ours | - | - |
| Protocol 67 | no layout change; the ally slide changes the simulation (section "Charge ally slide"), so client and server must agree (renumbered at integration if another branch takes 67) | - | - | `Protocol.Version` | ours | - | - |

### Charge ally slide (charge-ally-slide; protocol 67, used by the simulation)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-11: "when a charge hits an ally it should slide past." and "early s tap should not be remembered" (answering the open questions of protocol 66's ally bump and S cancel).
Code: `ChargeCancel.AllyPasses`, `ChargeLock.Find` (`passAllies`) and `ChargeLock.Predict`, `World.ResolveRush` (`AllyPasses`), `GameClient.PredictChargeContact`. Tests: `ChargeCancelTests`, `ChargeLockTests`, `RushTests`, `MusouCombatTests`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Allies are no contact | a charge (the bull rush, the dash attack's lunge) passes a player of its own side that it cannot harm (match rules without friendly fire, or none): `ChargeLock.Find` leaves that player out of the contact test, so there is no hit, no collision stop (the recoil), no turn to him, no velocity change from the charge and no impact presentation (hit-stop, effects, camera kick); the clip plays to its own end (or the charger's other early ends). The ally takes nothing: no damage, reaction, pull to a lock spot or shove by the charge | - | per tick | `ChargeCancel.AllyPasses`, `ChargeLock.Find` | owner 2026-11-11 ("when a charge hits an ally it should slide past") | owner's decision | high |
| The slide | what slides the charger past is the shared player collision (sim/player-collision, unchanged): the capsules block each other and the charger's move slides along the ally's capsule (up to four slides; the velocity loses what went into the body), with the push apart at 3 m/s each side; the speed and heading are kept except for that deflection, and a body dead ahead is rounded or the charger is held at its capsule. The slide is the capsules' own rule and is not tuned for the charge (ours) | m | per tick | `PlayerCollision.Resolve` | the collision rules: ours; the charge's slide: owner 2026-11-11 | ours | medium |
| Where it applies | every mode: Classic PvP and Musou Mode alike (Musou has no rule of its own for it: its players are allies and passed each other's charge); protocol 66 limited the bump to Classic PvP and kept the recoil on an ally in Musou, which the slide replaces. Musou enemies' contact is Musou's own and unchanged | - | - | `ChargeCancel.AllyPasses` | owner 2026-11-11 | owner's decision | medium |
| Not passed | an enemy (hit, stun, recoil and clash exactly as before, also with an ally in front of it: the nearest enemy in reach is met); an ally with friendly fire on (hit, stunned, the recoil, as before); a charge that meets a wall (the wall's recoil) | - | per tick | `World.ResolveRush` | unchanged | - | - |
| Prediction | the own client predicts it exactly: `ChargeLock.Predict` passes allies by the same rule (friendly fire read from the server's scoreboard, taken as on until the first arrives, as the server has no rules then); synthetic run: three marines of one side, 150 ms RTT, 5 % loss, 40 s, every charge cancelled with S held or tapped, mashed with Grenade or left to its end, allies in the way with the bodies on: 0 mismatches per client, no contact ever predicted or resolved (seeds 391, 392) | - | per tick | `GameClient.PredictChargeContact`, `ChargeCancelTests` | measured | observed | high |
| An S tap before the branch is not remembered | an S press made before the rush's stick branch (0.467 s) and let go does nothing when the branch comes, with or without the input buffer: the stick is tested on the branch tick only and the buffer keeps button presses, not the stick (checked for every tap tick 1 to 17 with the buffer window 0 and 0.3 s) | - | per tick | `ChargeCancel.EndsAtBranch`, `ChargeCancelTests` | owner 2026-11-11 ("early s tap should not be remembered"); already how protocol 66 behaved, now pinned | owner's decision | high |
| Switch | `--old-ally-bump` (server and every client; config hash, written only when on) now restores the protocol 65 collision stop on an ally (the slide and the bump are gone either way) | - | - | `SimConfig.ChargeAllyBump` | restore switch | test aid | decided |


### Musou Mode: random swings, thrown bodies, thinner clouds (musou/melee-ragdoll-clouds; Musou Mode only, no protocol change, `TfwRules.Version` 23)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-02: "randomize what animation each attack is. its currently playing the first light swing attack in each weapon's combo chain"; "stop making ork bodies disappear instantly when killed by artillery, frag grenades, grenade launcher explosions, and plasma cannon explosions. the bodies should ragdoll and be explosively knocked away as well as up into the air (random, some go up some go sideways, some both) ... don't remove the gore that happens or bloody explosions"; "make the gore clouds slightly more see through. not completely transparent". Cause of the vanishing: a blast or artillery death was gibbed (no corpse) and only thrown within 40 m under a cap of 16 flung bodies that also counted those lying, so most of a big blast's dead simply went. ### Solid bodies: no passing through, the charge meets what it runs into (fix/charge-player-collision; protocol 57, no wire change)

Source: the owner's playtest, 2026-11-06: "Sometimes you can charge through an enemy instead of impacting on them and their body stopping your movement. It happens a lot. I think this is
because the collision of the models works from a center point rather than an outer hitbox ... ensure that players never pass directly through other players ... Ensure the charge clash and
stun and recoil animations play more reliably as well." His reference clip (original footage) shows the impact where the charger's shoulder meets the target's body. Cause (measured in
`SolidBodiesTests`): every move collided only with the others as its own client last saw them (sim/player-collision), so a target that stepped into the line within a round trip was run
through (24 of 48 step-in runs at 0.17 to 0.5 s of lag; an eight-player crowd at 150 ms came to -0.88 m, axes all but together); the charge's 45 degree cone was measured from wherever the
tick's move began, so a body 0.85 to 1.2 m off the line was met or missed by the tick's phase (20 of 189 standing-target runs at 35 m/s passed without a contact); a charger that met a body
kept its whole tick's move (up to 1.14 m beyond the point met). Code: `SmSim.SolidBodies`, `Rush.Contact`, `ChargeLock.Find` / `Predict`, `World.GuardBodies` (`World.SolidGuard`, set by the server).
Opponents only: allies keep the protocol 56 bodies and contact (so the co-op of the added content is unchanged).

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Charge contact: the sweep | an opponent already within reach (2 × 0.45 + 0.3 m) when the tick's move starts is met at once when within 45 degrees of the heading from there (as before); any other is met at the **first touch** of the swept reach along the move, when it lies anywhere **in front** of the charger at that point (the front half: a shoulder clipping a shoulder at the side of the reach counts); the earliest touch along the move is the one met. Predicted by the own client | m, degrees | per tick | `Rush.Contact` (`SweptContact`), `ChargeLock.Find` | ours (the original's contact is engine code; the owner's "outer hitbox") | ours | low |
| Charge stop at the contact | a charger that meets an opponent stops at the point of its tick's move where it met it, swept through the level from where it began the tick (not a tick's move beyond, up to 1.17 m at the bull rush's burst); the lock then pulls the stunned victim to 0.9 m in front as before. Predicted by the own client | m | the contact tick | `SolidBodies.AtContact`, `World.ResolveRush`, `ChargeLock.Predict` | ours | ours | low |
| The guard (server) | after every player moved, each pair of living opponents is swept against the other as they really moved this tick: a relative path that would bring the axes closer than **0.45 m** (one capsule radius: never more than half into the other, never through), or **0.75 m** (the capsules' edge less 0.15 m) when either is charging (the bull rush or the dash attack's lunge), or closer than they already were, is cut where it reaches that distance, for each one moving toward the other; its velocity into the other is lost. Up to 3 passes over the pairs in id order. Not predicted: a client whose picture of the others was wrong is corrected to the stop | m | per tick, after every player's move, before shots, melee and charges | `SolidBodies.Guard`, `World.GuardBodies` | ours | ours | low (the 0.45 m walkers' limit: a 0.75 m limit corrected 27 % of ticks in an eight-player crowd at 150 ms, 0.45 m 5 %, p99 3.5 to 8.9 cm; playtest) |
| The charge meets the bodies as they are (server) | a charge also tests every opponent's move this tick as it really happened (after the guard): the relative sweep, its first touch, the same reach, front half and line of sight; the earliest of this, the charger's rewound picture and its blocking body is met. Not predicted (the own recoil then starts with the correction, from the contact tick's clip time) | m | per tick | `ChargeLock.Find` (`now`) | ours | ours | low |
| Clash, stun and recoil states | every harmful connect on a victim that may react ends its tick with the charger in the collision stop (its first tick) and the victim in the stun; the snapshots carry both (state-driven clips); checked for every connect seen by the charger's own client, the victim's own client and each one's view of the other at 150 ms with 5 % loss | - | the contact tick | `World.ResolveRush` / `StopRushes`; `SolidBodiesTests` | ours (test) | ours | medium |
| Switch | `--old-body-contact` on the server and every client (config hash): the protocol 56 contact, stop and no guard; `ServerOptions.BodyGuard` false (tests): the guard and the real-move contact off, the predicted rules kept | - | - | `SimConfig.SolidBodies`, `ServerOptions.BodyGuard` | test aid | test aid | decided |

### Swing step, the lock-on's lunge and the air jump by mode (sim/swing-step, sim/lock-reach, sim/air-jumps; protocol 59, no wire change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-06: "for all melee weapons except thunder hammer/daemon maul: increase the distance of the step-forward during a melee swing by 50%. for the thunder hammer reduce that step-forward during the swing by 30%. for all melee weapons reduce the lunge distance of the lock on by 30%. only in musou mode should the assault marine/raptor have extra/infinite jumps. in classic pvp mode the assault marine/raptor class should not be able to jump full height during an existing jump. they should only be able to hop with space bar + WASD." Interpretations (ours, to confirm with the owner): a "swing" is a light strike (the X chain; the heavy list is the stun attacks and finishers, unchanged); the daemon maul takes the hammer's 0.7 (the owner named only the hammer); the "lock-on lunge" is a locked attack's approach to its target; "during an existing jump" covers every airborne state (falling off a ledge, after an apex, after an air hop, a charge held in the air), so no air start of a full jump is left as a loophole.
Code: `MeleeTuning.WeaponMap.SwingStepFactor`, `MeleeTuning.OwnerSwingStep` / `OwnerHammerSwingStep` (multiplied into `MeleeStep.LungeFactor`), `MeleeLockSpec.LungeReach`, `GameplayTuning.OwnerLockLungeReach`, `MeleeLock.LungeStep`; `SimConfig.JumpPackAirJumps` (hook `ExtrasAirJumps`, set by Musou Mode in `Extras/SimConfig.Extras.cs`), `JumpPack.Begin` (`airLong`). Tests: `SwingStepLockReachTests`, `MeleeCancelTests` (Classic), `Extras/Musou/MusouAirJumpTests`. Measured on the install with `smtool melee-steps` (whole clip, 30 Hz ticks).

### Musou Mode: packs and twice the Orks again (musou/ork-swarm-2x, 2026-11-06; `TfwRules.Version` 25, `MusouSim.Version` 8; Musou Mode only)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-06: "make the orks stop running in straight lines in musou mode. they should pool up at their spawn point before fanning out, swarming their target in a rough blobby formation. double the amount of orks on the map again. also remove the small red attack incoming indicators that appear under them when they are melee attacking." Supersedes the counts of "Musou Mode: twice the Orks again" above. Every value is ours (an estimate for the playtest). Everything here runs only in a war (`MusouSim.Swarm` set by `World.StartTfw`); the 5-wave run and classic PvP are unchanged. Cause of the lines: each Ork followed the flow field from its own walking-graph cell to the next cell's centre, so the cells' shortest ways merged into files, worst round every corner (a test pack of 120 became a file 0.7 m wide and 18.8 m long round a wall's end).

Measured on a real local server (`--tfw-test-fight`, `SM_TICK_STATS`, `SM_TFW_KEEP_HUMAN=1`, one client, this PC) while other sessions' test hosts held the CPU at 100 % (an empty server skipped ticks too), so means and p99 are stall-bound and only the medians compare: before (896 Orks) server tick p50 3.9 to 5.2 ms, about 62 KB/s, headless client 82 to 94 fps; after (1610 to 1790 Orks) server tick p50 4.3 to 5.3 ms of the 33 ms budget, 38 to 63 KB/s (the per-client budget holds it; far Orks update less often), the Musou step 3 to 9 ms between stalls; windowed client, the player held at the landing with 1360 to 1630 drawn by the vertex-animation tier: 105 to 121 fps, p50 6.7 to 7.6 ms; the player walked into the swarm with 1700 drawn (40 skinned): 41 to 48 fps, p50 15 to 19 ms, against 52 to 59 fps with `--musou-visible 900` in the same scenario and load. Not measured: a quiet PC, older GPUs, several clients. No exception in any run. Overhead screenshots (`--tfw-swarm-shots`): `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\musou-swarm\`.

### Musou Mode: patrols, hunters and no Ork stuns (musou/ork-patrols-nostun, 2026-11-06; `TfwRules.Version` 28, `MusouSim.Version` unchanged, no protocol or wire change; Musou Mode only)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-06: "there should be large formations of orks all around the map at all time ... include patrols that both patrol on set routes and also hunt down the players no matter where they are", then the same day (through the lead): keep the number of Orks exactly as it is (no 20x, no impostor crowds), the patrols and hunters come from the existing Orks; and, verbatim: "remove all stun effects by orks in musou mode. they should never impede player movement or action". Every value is ours (an estimate for the playtest). Everything here runs only in a war (`TfwBattle`, `MusouSim.War`); the 5-wave test aid (`MusouSkirmishPinTests`) and classic PvP (`MusouIsolationTests`, `PvpCombatIsolationTests`, `TfwNoStunTests`) are unchanged. Tests: `TfwPatrolTests`, `TfwNoStunTests`.

Measured on a real local server (`server.cmd`-equivalent `dotnet run -c Release`, `--content musou --bind 127.0.0.1`, `SM_TICK_STATS=10`, `SM_TFW_FIGHT_LOG=10`, `SM_TFW_KEEP_HUMAN=1`, one headless `--tfw-test-fight` client, the same build with and without `SM_TFW_NO_PATROLS=1`) while other sessions held the CPU (p99 70 to 230 ms and skipped ticks in every run, so only medians compare): without columns server tick p50 4.8 to 5.6 ms and the Musou step 2.6 to 4.1 ms at 900 to 1640 Orks (later windows of that run 19 to 37 ms under heavier foreign load); with columns p50 3.7 to 6.2 ms and the step 2.6 to 4.5 ms at 770 to 1790 Orks, the same Ork counts (pool and caps unchanged). All 6 columns formed on the real map with 12 route searches, the longest 224 ms: hence the searches run off the tick and are taken 3 s after the start. The client draws the same Orks (no client change); its fps was not measured separately.

### Musou Mode: Boss Ork facing and wall room, patrol waits bounded (night/ork-movement, 2026-11-06; `TfwRules.Version` and `MusouSim.Version` unchanged, no protocol or wire change; Musou Mode only)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-06: "currently elite 3x scaled up orks in musou mode walk against walls looking the wrong direction while running forward. ensure that they face the direction they are moving when running forward"; and a live report of patrol columns stalling for rear ranks. Cause found: a running enemy's facing was set to its *desired* direction (the flow field's next node) each tick, not the way it actually moved, so a body pressed on a wall faced the wall; and the walking graph keeps only a normal Ork's 0.4 m off the walls, so a Boss Ork (3x the body, radius 1.8 m for the Nob) ground along them.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Musou: Boss Ork facing while it runs | a Boss Ork in the Seek state faces its smoothed actual velocity (**0.1** of each tick's velocity blended in, about 0.3 s), turning at most **6** rad/s; slower than **0.8** m/s (pressed on a wall, shuffling, stopped) it keeps its facing; every other enemy keeps facing its desired way | rad/s, m/s | per tick | `MusouSim.BossTurnRate`, `BossFaceSpeed`, `BossHeadingBlend`, `TurnToVelocity` | owner request 2026-11-06; the rates ours | ours | estimate |
| Musou: Boss Ork wall room | a Boss Ork leans away from any wall nearer than its radius minus the graph's 0.4 m margin (Nob 1.4 m, Boy 0.8 m), by up to **0.9** of its speed at the wall itself, along the gradient of the distance to the nearest closed cell (`MusouNav.EdgeDistance`, `EdgeGradient`) | m, share of speed | per tick | `MusouSim.BossWallRoom`, `BossWallPush` | ours | ours | estimate |
| Musou: Boss Ork straight-line check | a Boss Ork near its target (within the slot distance) only closes in on its slot round the target when the straight line to it is walkable on the graph (`NavGraph.StraightWalk`); when a wall is in the line it keeps to the flow field for **1.5** s (about 6 m, past the corner). Found by tracing: the length test alone flipped between "straight" and "round" on neighbouring nodes at a wall's corner, so the enemy (any Ork; a Boss Ork was the one we fixed) stepped to and fro there for good, facing both ways; the crowd keeps the old length test, untouched | s | per tick | `MusouSim.WayIsStraight`, `BossNotStraightSeconds` | ours | ours | estimate |
| Musou: a column's wait is bounded | the head waits (stops) while its middle Ork is **4** m behind, at most **2.5** s at a time; then Orks more than **9** m behind their places are let go alone and the head creeps on at **0.6** of its pace until the ranks are up (**4** m), then walks at full pace | s, m, share | per tick | `TfwPatrolRules.MaxWaitSeconds`, `LateBehind`, `CreepFraction` | ours | ours | estimate |

Measured before the facing change: a floor with a wall and a gap, a Boss Nob or Boss Boy running round the wall's end to a player: facing against its velocity was already exact (the wrong facing shows only when it shuffles or presses on a wall); with the player 16 m away straight through the wall, the old code never arrived (40 s, shuffling at the corner, facing flipping each tick, also a plain Boy); after, it arrives in about 11.5 s and its facing is within 6 degrees (p95) of its net movement over 0.5 s.

Measured (test arena and an open floor with a wall, 180 s, no player near, columns formed: stopped seconds of the wait, per column): before, a 24 m gap 0.0 to 0.1 s, a 2.5 m gap 0.0 to 0.5 s, the test arena's real graph 0.0 to 0.3 s of 15 to 177 s formed; the live stalls were not reproduced in these layouts (the rule is a bound now, not a fix of a measured stall).

### Musou Mode: expansion S2, the Bomb Squig and the Rokkit Boy (musou/exp-s2, 2026-11-07; `MusouSim.Version` 14, `TfwRules.Version` 34, no core protocol bump: `Protocol.Version` stays 63)

Source: the owner's brief of 2026-11-07 (`docs/musou-expansion.md`, stage S2, rules "Bomb Squig", "Rokkit Boy", "Ork blast"). Every value is ours (owner brief 2026-11-07) unless marked; the Squig's burst is the original frag's data. Musou Mode battles only (the skirmish and the 5-wave run never spawn either; Classic PvP untouched). Tests `MusouExpansionS2Tests`.

### Musou Mode: expansion S6, the battle flow (musou/exp-s6, 2026-11-08; `MusouSim.Version` 18, `TfwRules.Version` 36, no core protocol bump: `Protocol.Version` stays 63)

Source: the owner's brief of 2026-11-07 (`docs/musou-expansion.md`, stage S6, "Battle flow", and its "S6 design"). Values marked brief are the owner's; every other value is ours (an estimate). Musou Mode battles only (`TfwBattle`, the war): the skirmish, the 5-wave run and Classic PvP are untouched.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Levels (near / far) | an army is real within **90** m of any human (the distance to its footprint: centre less its slots' radius), aggregate again past **120** m (hysteresis; **300** / **330** m since 2026-11-09, spec "Musou Mode: Ork movement feel"); every co-op human counts, an AI Marine never | m | per tick | `TfwArmyRules.NearMetres`, `FarMetres`, `TfwBattle.StepLevels` | brief | ours | hi |
| Promotion and demotion caps | at most **16** Orks and **1** Guard squad made real a tick over all armies, at most **32** Orks and **2** squads folded back a tick; at most **480** real army Orks and **28** army squads at once (superseded 2026-11-09: spec "Musou Mode: no Ork formations, 80 % of the Orks") | units | per tick | `TfwArmyRules` | ours | ours | estimate |
| Pools | the Ork pool **2560** (was 2048); every spawner but the armies keeps **2048** (`TfwBattleRules.CrowdPool`, less the 80 reserve), the armies' real Orks count outside the crowds' cap; GuardSim **40** squads (was 24), wire Guardsman ids up to **448** | slots | - | `MusouSim.Capacity`, `TfwBattleRules.CrowdPool`, `GuardSim.MaxSquads`, `TfwWire.GuardCapacity` | ours (brief: lift only where needed) | ours | hi |
| Slots | one layout shared by server and client: the anchor is the front rank's middle; Orks in rows of round(1.2 x sqrt(planned)) files clamped **6 to 36**, **1.4** m apart, ranks **1.6** m; Guardsmen in squad blocks of two rows of five, **1.5** m (as `GuardSim` lays out a squad), width a multiple of 5, **5 to 30**; the width is fixed for the army's life; real members fill slots from the front, the aggregate stands in the slots after the highest real one | m, files | fixed | `TfwArmyLayout` | ours | ours | hi |
| Far clash | twice a second (**0.5** s) at each position and at the base: Lanchester's square law in strength (men x worth) between the aggregates there and the real units within its radius + **10** m; a side's strength lost a step = the other side's strength x **0.011** a second x (0.3 + 0.7 x cohesion) x (1 ± **0.3** roll), shared by strength and paid in each army's own men; cohesion falls by **1.5** x the share of the start lost and by **0.05** a second per unit of the enemy's strength edge, recovers **0.02** a second out of a fight; an army routs at cohesion **0.2** or **65 %** losses; elites die at **0.5** of their share.
