### Musou Mode: Guardsmen as defenders, the capture under fire, the Boss Ork cleave (musou/guard-formations, 2026-11-06; `TfwRules.Version` 28, no protocol or wire change)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-06: "re add the imperial guardsmen infantry formations to the game. they move and act on their own to defend existing points. only allied space marine lords and players and retainers go capture new territory"; "the boss orks should be able to cleave guardsmen the way that players cleave orks"; "players should be able to make progress capturing a point even if orks are still defending it. only stop capturing if no player remains on the point." Musou Mode only; classic PvP untouched. Tests `TfwGuardFormationTests`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Who captures | a capturer: a living human or AI Marine (a lord or a retainer) on the point; a Guardsman never adds progress, at any rate | - | per tick | `TfwBattle.StepPosition` | the owner (2026-11-06) | owner's decision | high |
| Capture under fire | with a capturer on it a point's progress grows at the full rate (25 s to secure) whatever Orks stand on it: Clearing (capturers and Orks) and Securing (capturers alone) both grow it; Held (no capturer) holds none and the progress falls **2 %** a second, as before | s | per tick | `TfwBattle.StepPosition` | the owner (2026-11-06); the decay unchanged (ours) | owner's decision | high |
| Keeping a secured point | any Imperial on it keeps it, a Guardsman included (he defends it); Orks alone on it take it back in 20 s, as before | s | per tick | `TfwBattle.StepPosition` | ours: "defend existing points" | ours | medium |
| HUD: clearing | "CLEARING n%" (was "CLEARING", the progress now grows), then " - n ORKS" as before | - | per frame | `TfwHudModel.ObjectiveState` | ours | ours | medium |
| Defence posts | once a second the squads are posted: with no point secured all hold the landing zone (within **10** m); otherwise each squad in turn goes to the secured point with the highest (threat + **8**) / (squads posted + 1), threat the Orks within **40** m of it (up to 64, in steps of **8**); a squad keeps its post while that post still wants it, the others go to the nearest post short of squads; each stands at its spot within 0.7 of the point's radius and stops to fight an enemy within 8 m (as before). The final assault: the three secured points | m, enemies | per second | `TfwBattle.StepSquads`, `TfwBattleRules.Threat*` | the owner: "they move and act on their own to defend existing points"; every number ours, an estimate to check in a playtest | estimate | low |
| Squads | as before: clamp(round(I / 15), 4, 12), at most 6 in the field, refilled from the landing zone every 15 s and at each secured point; 10 men in two rows of five | squads | at landing | `TfwBattle` | as before | ours | low |
| Boss Ork cleave on Guardsmen | a Boss Ork's melee blow on a squad strikes every living Guardsman, of any squad, within its melee reach + its body radius + 0.4 m (a Guardsman) + 0.5 m (the players' cleave's extra) of its feet, 1.5 m up or down, in the front half (the core's 60 degrees x 1.5, as the players' cleave), at most **20**, nearest first: each takes the blow's damage (Boss Nob 50, Boss 'Ard Boy 20, Boss Boy 16; a Guardsman has 85); one who lives is thrown **2** m and falls (1.8 s down, 0.7 s up) or with **10 %** dies at once; with none in the arc the blow lands on one man as before. The Warboss's and every other Ork's blows land on one man, as before; the Boss Shoota's rounds too | m, men | per blow | `World.TfwGuardCleave`, `GuardSim.Cleave` | the owner (2026-11-06): "the way that players cleave orks": the players' cleave and fall rules (`MusouCombatRules`, `TfwCombatRules`) reused; the reach's body terms ours | ours | medium |

### Musou Mode: the Guardsmen spread out on the way and round a held point (musou/guard-spread, 2026-11-08; `TfwRules.Version` 44, no protocol or wire change)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-08: "guardsmen need to spread out much more when running to a point. after its captured they splinter and spread out around the point to defend it. on the way to the point guardsmen get stuck on corners and walk in straight lines directly next to walls. they need to spread out." The direction is his; every number is ours, to check in a playtest. All in `GuardRules` (server only; the near, simulated Guardsmen: the far clash's numbers and the men's strength are unchanged). `GuardRules.Spread` false restores the old walk (two tight rows on the field's own steps, one block on the point).

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open order on the move | while a squad walks to an order its men take places in two loose ranks of five round the squad's place on its way: **3.5** m abreast, ranks **3** m apart, the second rank half a gap aside, each man shifted up to **0.75** m each way by a fixed roll of his slot (no neat line); over the last **6** m the order closes to the standing spacing's share (1.5 / 3.5). Standing (no order, or arrived without a point to hold): the old two rows of five, 1.5 m | m | per tick | `GuardRules.MoveSpacing`, `MoveRankSpacing`, `MoveJitter`, `MoveTaper`; `GuardSim.MoveOffset` | the owner (2026-11-08): "spread out much more when running to a point"; the numbers ours | estimate | low |
| Squad lanes | squads on the move go in three lanes by their index (mod 3: middle, right, left), **6** m apart across their heading, so squads bound for one point do not walk in one file | m | per tick | `GuardRules.LaneSpacing` | ours, from the same request | estimate | low |
| Places off the walls | a man's place on the move is pulled in towards the squad's place (whole, 3/4, 1/2, 1/4) until it stands at least **1** m from a wall or ledge (the graph's own body margin not counted) and can be walked to in a straight line from the squad's place (checked every **6** ticks a man, staggered) | m, ticks | every 6 ticks | `GuardRules.PlaceClearance`, `DirectCheckTicks`; `GuardSim.FitScale` | the owner: "walk in straight lines directly next to walls"; the numbers ours | estimate | low |
| The way off the walls | the squad's way, and a man's when his straight line to his place is blocked, takes at each node, of the linked neighbours that still get nearer to the goal, the one with the highest directness (metres nearer per metre walked, at most 1) + **1.5** x its wall distance up to **2** m / 2 m; a drop is the field's own step; it always gets nearer, so it never loops | m | per step | `GuardRules.WayClearance`, `WayClearanceWeight`; `GuardSim.WayNext` | ours (an inflated-obstacle walk on the existing field, no new field) | estimate | low |
| Stuck men | a man who moves less than **30 %** of the step he wants for **0.5** s takes a detour for **2** s: by the way from where he stands, or, with no way, sideways (60 degrees off his line, his side by his slot and the detour's half) | s, share | per tick | `GuardRules.StuckSeconds`, `StuckFraction`, `DetourSeconds` | the owner: "get stuck on corners"; the numbers ours | estimate | low |
| Fire teams round a held point | a squad sent to a point (`TfwBattle.Send`: a secured position, or the landing zone with none, each squad to its own spot within 0.7 of the radius) splits on arrival into **3** fire teams (3, 3 and 4 men) spread over an arc of **120** degrees centred on its own bearing from the point's centre, at **0.8** of the point's radius; each team's spot is, of its place and 16 round it (**3** m and 1.5 m out), the walkable one within 0.95 of the radius and in a straight line from the centre whose wall distance is nearest **1** m (beside cover), the nearer on a tie; its men stand **2** m apart across the bearing and face outward when there. A man whose straight line to his post is blocked goes by the point's way, then straight. Set once on arrival | m, degrees | at arrival | `GuardRules.HoldTeams`, `HoldArcDegrees`, `HoldRadiusScale`, `TeamSpacing`, `CoverSearch`, `CoverEdge`; `GuardSim.SetPosts`, `GuardSim.CoverSpot` | the owner (2026-11-08): "after its captured they splinter and spread out around the point to defend it"; the numbers ours | estimate | low |
| Armies' squads | an army's squads (expansion S6) walk in the open order and lanes too; a held army keeps its block layout (`TfwArmyLayout`), no fire teams | - | per tick | `TfwBattle.OrderSquad` | ours (the block layout is the far layer's) | ours | low |

### Musou Mode: Guard vantage teams (musou/guard-vantage, 2026-11-09; `TfwRules.Version` 52, the lead renumbers; no protocol or wire change)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-09: "make small squads of guardsmen position themselves up in buildings randomly at times around the map - they should only position on high ground vantage points with good lines of fire around them within 50m of a friendly captured point. if there is no friendly captured point then they still defend the stronghold/imperial base but also venture out in front of their home base to take up high ground vantage point positions around the imperial base." The 50 m and the direction are his; every other number is ours, to check in a playtest. All in `GuardVantageRules` (server only; `GuardVantage` finds the spots, `TfwBattle.Vantage.cs` sends the teams). `GuardVantageRules.Enabled` false restores the Guardsmen as before. On Ashfall of 2026-11-09 the finder takes 95 spots (4, 7 and 4 within 50 m of points A, B and C; none within 50 m of the base, 8 in front of it within 100 m), heights 3 to 5.6 m (the level's walkable floors reach about 6 m), in about 4 s off the tick (Debug).

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vantage height | a spot stands at least **3** m (a storey) over the median of the lowest floors of the columns sampled in **16** directions at **4, 8, 12 and 16** m (columns with no floor left out, at least **16** samples needed), so a pit's rim or a wide plateau's middle is not high ground | m | once a level | `GuardVantageRules.MinHeight`, `GroundDirections`, `GroundRings`, `MinGroundSamples`; `GuardVantage.Find` | the owner: "high ground vantage points"; the test ours | ours | low |
| Vantage reach | a spot must be walked to from the base (the landing zone's node) and back, over the walking graph's walk and drop links (its real stairs and ramps; no jump packs) | - | once a level | `GuardVantage.Reachable` | ours | ours | medium |
| Candidates | one node per **3** m bin and storey: the highest over its ground, then the one whose wall/ledge distance is nearest **1** m (a roof's or balcony's edge, not its middle) | m | once a level | `GuardVantageRules.BinSize`, `EdgePreference` | ours | ours | low |
| Room | at least **3** posts (of up to **6**) on the spot's own floor (within 0.5 m) at it and 16 places round it (half of and the whole **2.5** m), **1.1** m apart, each walkable in a straight line from the spot | m | once a level | `GuardVantageRules.MinPosts`, `MaxPosts`, `PostRadius`, `PostSpacing`; `GuardVantage.Posts` | ours | ours | low |
| Lines of fire | from a man's eye (**1.5** m) to the chest (**1.2** m) of one standing on the ground in **16** directions at **10, 20 and 30** m, raycast on the weapons mesh (a ray stopped 0.3 m short of its end is blocked; no ground there counts blocked); at least **30 %** clear. The team faces the mean way of the clear lines | m, share | once a level | `GuardVantageRules.Directions`, `SightDistances`, `EyeHeight`, `ChestHeight`, `MinOpen` | the owner: "good lines of fire around them"; the numbers ours | ours | low |
| Score and spacing | score = clear share x (0.5 + 0.5 x min(height, **12** m) / 12 m); the best kept first, each at least **8** m (flat) from those kept | m | once a level | `GuardVantageRules.ScoreHeight`, `Spacing` | ours | ours | low |
| Where a team may go | within **50** m (flat) of a friendly-captured (secured) position; with none secured, within **50** m of the base and in front of it (towards the Ork HQ: at most 90 degrees off the base's line to the HQ), or out to **100** m on a level with no such spot within 50 m (Ashfall now) | m | each second | `GuardVantageRules.PointRadius`, `BaseRadius`, `BaseRadiusFar`, `BaseFrontCos` | the owner's 50 m and "in front of their home base"; the 100 m fallback and the front's angle ours | ours | low |
| How often | a team leaves every **20** to **45** s (a fixed roll each time; the first a whole interval after the landing), at most **4** teams out at once, one team a spot; the spot by a roll weighted by its score among those that may be taken, the field squad nearest it that stands at its post | s | rolled each departure | `GuardVantageRules.IntervalMin`, `IntervalMax`, `MostTeams` | the owner: "randomly at times"; the numbers ours | ours | low |
| Team size | **3** to **6** men (a roll) of one field squad, which keeps at least **4**; armies' squads never send one | men | at departure | `GuardVantageRules.MenMin`, `MenMax`, `ParentKeeps`; `GuardSim.Detach` | the owner: "small squads"; the numbers ours | ours | low |
| The way up and the hold | the team walks the walking graph's way to the spot (the Guardsmen's open order, its men by the way when their straight line is blocked; never put there), takes the spot's posts and faces its open side, fires from there as any squad (range 40 m, line of sight); it holds **60** to **150** s (a roll), then walks back and rejoins its squad within **6** m (its men into the squad's free slots; any left over stay a field squad) | s, m | per tick | `GuardVantageRules.HoldMin`, `HoldMax`, `RejoinDistance`; `GuardSim.OrderPosts`, `GuardSim.Merge` | ours | ours | low |

### Musou Mode: the Guardsmen's strength, endless ammunition, the grenade refill, the AI Marines' damage (night/musou-rules, 2026-11-06; `TfwRules.Version` 30, no protocol or wire change)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-06: "scale up the guardsmen to what you believe will half the time win, half the time lose against ork counterattacks (the purpose of the guardsmen is only to defend captured points)"; "ammo should be infinite in musou mode"; "grenades should refill every 30 seconds automatically"; "bots in musou mode should retain all player attributes and statistics - except make them take 90% reduced damage". Musou Mode only (`World.TfwSupply.cs`, `GuardRules`; the damage hook `ExtrasDamageTaken` returns 1 outside a war); Classic PvP untouched. Tests `GuardHoldTrialTests`, `TfwSupplyTests`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guardsmen's strength | health and shot damage **1.1x** (85 to 93.5 hit points, 5 to 5.5 a shot); fire rate, hit chance, range, speed and the squads unchanged. 4.5x from the night batch of 2026-11-06 (60 held against a full crowd of 400 half the time) until 2026-11-08, when the owner set the near balance to the far clash's, man for man (0.875x); 1.1x since 2026-11-10 (the owner: "Raise the guards to 1.1"), after every Nob coming twice had brought the trial below to 1 of 20 | factor | at spawn, per shot | `GuardRules.Strength` | the owner's request; the factor ours, from the trial below (1.1 the owner's pick from it) | estimate | low |
| The counterattack trial | headless, no player, deterministic: the field's 6 squads (60 men) stand on a secured point (12 m); one spawn point's full crowd (400 Orks, the run's middle elite share 35 %: 140 elites in runs of 20, 75 % 'Ard Boyz and 25 % Nobs, the rest 70 % Boyz and 30 % Shootas, on an 11 m disc) comes from a seeded bearing 35 to 55 m away; held: a Guardsman stands when the last Ork falls or at 300 s; lost: every man down. Measured over seeds 1 to 20: x1 held 0 (the field gone in 36 s on average, 5 Orks killed), x2 0, x3 0, x4 0, x4.25 7, **x4.5 11 (55 %; one at the time limit)**, x4.75 12, x5 20. **Since 2026-11-08 the target is a crowd of the field's own size, 60 Orks** (same mix): x0.5 held 0, x0.75 6, x0.8 6, x0.85 7, **x0.875 10 (50 %)**, x0.9 15, x1 18, x1.25 20 (`SM_GUARD_CROWD=60 SM_GUARD_SWEEP=...`). **Since 2026-11-10 every Nob comes twice** (`TfwBattleRules.BigTwins`): x0.875 held 1, x1 5, **x1.1 10 (50 %)**, x1.25 15, x1.4 19 | seeds | per run | `GuardHoldTrial` (tests) | ours: one crowd is the counterattack the battle sends at a point (`TfwBattleRules.CrowdSize`); no player, lord, retainer, Boss Ork, trickle or reserve squad takes part | estimate | low |
| Endless ammunition | every living player's weapons (humans and AI Marines, every slot) keep a full reserve (the perks' size; more from a box is kept), so a reload always fills the clip; a weapon that cannot reload (a brace weapon, or one with no reserve) gets a full clip back once it is empty. ### The charge clash: charger and victim locked through the shove (feel/charge-clash; protocol 59, no wire change)

Source: the owner (2026-11-06): "use this reference video for how a f charge should work (holding w, shift, and F at the same time). the player should never, ever phase through another
player model. both models 'clash', one delivering the charge one receiving (kind of sticking together like a lock on)." His recording of the original (30 fps, 9.8 s; studied frame by frame,
frames kept outside the repo under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\previews\charge-clash\video\`): a Space Marine with bolt pistol and knife charges a Chaos Marine; the rush (the orange
charge glow) starts at about 5.45 s, homes about 30 to 40 degrees right onto the target over its last 0.3 s, and meets it at 6.07 to 6.10 s (frames 182 to 183: the charger's shoulder at the
victim's chest, the victim's shield flash); for frames 183 to 188 (about 0.18 s) the two travel together, the victim held in front at a fixed distance; at frames 188 to 190 the charger twists
back in its recoil while the victim, stunned, stays about a metre in front; no knockback beyond that. Data (read on the install with our readers, 2026-11-06): the charger's stop
`SM_NAV_Bullrush2Idle_F_Collision_01` moves the body **forward 1.83 m in its first 0.2 s** (0.54, 0.51, 0.39, 0.24, 0.14, 0.02 m a tick) and then **1.11 m back** by 0.7 s, still to its
end at 1.067 s: the shove and the recoil of the recording. The Tactical's bull rush stuns, the Assault's / Raptor's bull rush staggers (`ability_bullrush_01`), their dash attack stuns.
Cause of the phasing: the shove's 1.83 m collided with the victim's body as the charger's client last saw it (often where it stood before the lock's pull), and as a walker after the stop the
server's guard let it come 0.45 m into the victim (`ChargeClashTests`: 150 of 150 lagged control runs overlapped, by up to 0.45 m). Code: `SmSim.ChargeClash`, `World.CarryClashes` /
`HoldClashes` / `OpenClashes`, `GameClient.ClashBodies`, `NetworkView.LockDrawn`, `DrawnBodies`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Clash opens | a bull rush whose hit puts its victim in a reaction (the stun; the Assault's stagger) locks the two (not an ally, not a victim in hyper armour or flight) | - | the contact tick | `World.OpenClashes` | owner's reference video; pairing ours | interpretation | medium |
| The shove (clash duration) | the collision stop's ticks up to its farthest forward point: **0.2 s (6 ticks)**, 1.83 m; the video's travel together: about 0.18 s (frames 183 to 188) | s, m | ticks from the stop | `ChargeClash.CarryTicks` | data (extracted motion); video agrees | data | high |
| The lock | through the shove the charger's step ignores the victim's body (its own client predicts this: 120 of 120 clash ticks exact at 150 ms, 5 % loss) and the world carries the victim by the charger's move, swept through the level (a kill volume stops it); a victim the level stops holds the charger back by the same amount; the guard's cuts against third players hold both | - | each tick of the shove | `ChargeClash.Carrying`, `World.CarryClashes`, `HoldClashes` | owner's reference video ("sticking together like a lock on") | ours | medium |
| Lock distance | **0.9 m** feet to feet (two capsule radii: the capsules touching, the charger's shoulder at the victim's chest), held on every tick of the shove | m | - | `ChargeLock.LockDistance` | video (shoulder to chest); value ours | estimate | medium |
| Recoil | the stop's backward 1.11 m (0.2 to 0.7 s) separates them; the victim stays stunned where the shove left it (no knockback: none in the data); about 2.0 m apart at the end | m | - | `Rush.Move` (data motion) | data; video agrees (victim about a metre in front of the recoiling charger) | data | high |
| Charger meets any body at its edge | the server's guard with a charger, or with a player in a charge's stop (collision stop, dash hit, dash wall stop), is **0.85 m**: the touch (0.9 m) less a **5 cm** slack (`SolidBodies.ClashDepth`; was 0.15 m, 0.75 m) that bodies pressing on each other through the shared collision's lagged picture never reach (they settle up to about 1.5 cm in), so the exact prediction is kept and only a stale picture's real intrusion is cut; walkers keep 0.45 m (their drawn bodies are moved apart, below) | m | each tick | `SolidBodies.GuardDistance`, `World.Charging` | owner ("never, ever phase") | ours | high |

### Musou Mode: a burst of deaths spread over frames, near wind-ups first (night batch 2026-11-06, `night/death-spike`; client drawing and the server's send order, Musou Mode only, no protocol, wire or config-hash change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-06: "currently when a grenade explodes many orks die instantaneously. find a way to optimize that and remove the moment of extreme frame time when many orks are dying at the same instant"; and the open item of musou/far-ork-smooth, whether near Orks' wind-ups come late under a full send budget (row "Musou enemy interest" and "Musou send budget" above carry the send-order values). Code: `MusouDeathRules`, `NetworkView.MusouDeathSpread.cs`, `MusouRagdolls.Prewarm`, `CrowdView.KeepSkinned`, `MusouSendRules.NearChangeFirst` / `TelegraphFirst`. Test aids: client `--musou-old-deaths` (every death handed out in the frame it arrives, no doll dressing ahead, as before), `--musou-death-spike-test [N]` (with `--musou-death-spike-ab`), server `SM_MUSOU_OLD_NEAR_SEND=1`. Tests: `MusouWindUpLatencyTests`.

Measured headless (`--musou-death-spike-test 60`: the scripted feed's 60 Orks 8 m in front of the camera all die by a blast in one tick every 4 s; the crowd, ragdolls, gore and sounds run, nothing is rendered; the main thread's own CPU per frame, so another process's load does not count, though a busy shared PC still moved every figure by up to 2x between runs; `--musou-death-spike-ab` takes turns so both meet the same load). Warm bursts, the worst frame of the second after (medians of 7): 16.5 ms old against 15.8 ms new (quiet frames about 9 ms); with 150 Orks (100 bodies kept) 16.7 against 16.0. The cold one (the first burst of a run): 52 to 63 ms old, 31 to 39 ms new (single samples from separate runs). The per-death work itself is small when warm (1 to 2 ms for 60); the frames after a burst cost more mostly from what then flies (20 ragdolls in the physics, 40 thrown bodies probing the walls, the gore), which the spreading does not change. Not shown headless: the GPU (shader and pipeline compiles on first use, the overdraw of near gore clouds, skinning the dolls), and a real battle's 1800-Ork load.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Deaths handed out a frame (Musou) | the deaths the client is told of wait in a queue and are handed out (body, ragdoll, gore, death yell and fall) the nearest to the camera first, at most **24** a frame, of them at most **5** thrown as ragdolls (only as many as the pool of 20 can take count as dolls; the rest tumble as crowd bodies); one that has waited **0.1 s** goes out whatever the counts. A waiting death is drawn where it fell, playing its death clip from its arrival, under the skeleton that drew the living Ork, which its body then keeps (no blink, no new skeleton). 60 deaths in one tick: out over 3 frames at 60 fps; 150: over 5 | deaths, s | per frame | `MusouDeathRules.PerFrame`, `DollsPerFrame`, `MaxWaitSeconds` | owner 2026-11-06 ("deaths may start up to about 100 ms staggered" is the brief's bound); values ours | ours | low |
| Ragdoll pool dressed ahead (Musou) | once the 20 dolls are made, one doll a frame is given the meshes of one thrown look (Boy, Shoota Boy, 'Ard Boy, Gretchin, Nob), hidden, until every doll has every look, so the first blast of a match builds no nodes | dolls | one a frame after load | `MusouRagdolls.Prewarm` | ours | ours | medium |

### Jump escape, hop-cancel momentum and descent recharge (protocol 62; sim/jump-escape, sim/hop-cancel-momentum, sim/descent-recharge, 2026-11-06)

Source: the owner's batch of 2026-11-06 (late), stream A: (1) "assault and raptor marine in classic pvp mode should be able to jump out of all stuns or loss of control effects or animations" and "assault marine/raptor in all game modes should be able to jump out of any animation. basically, cancel any animation thats currently playing when the assault marine/raptor presses jump"; (2) "when cancelling the hop (short space bar press) of an asasult marine with a melee attack, the character still moves up in the air a bit. he should start moving horizontally only with some momentum carried over, combined with the step forward or lock on lunge of the melee attack"; (3) "ensure that a assault marine/raptor in classic pvp can jump twice before regenerating fuel. he should be able to jump a 3rd time shortly after. it feels that jumping uses more fuel than the original game. make it match the game data of the original game - fuel consumption per jump."
Code: `SmSim.JumpEscape`, `MeleeCancel.HopCarry`, `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (the escape, the air swing), `JumpPack.Begin` (`escape`, the descent recharge), `SimConfig.JumpPackDescentRecharge`. Tests: `JumpEscapeTests`. Shared by the server and the client's prediction.

### Hammer and maul: hop swing, slam recovery and the steered slam (sim/hop-swing, sim/slam-recovery, sim/slam-steer; 2026-11-07, protocol 63 unchanged)

Sources: the owner's report of 2026-11-07 (verbatim): "Cannot swing inside of the second half of a hop (spacebar) on the ground. the player should be able to perform a short hop (space bar) and at any
point in that short hop early, or towards the end of the animation, perform a melee swing with the hammer (right mouse click). Too large of a delay after an FF where you cant swing. ... make the cooldown
after a stun strike combo that must expire before you can melee swing or initiate a follow up stun strike combo f + f shorter - match the cooldown between executing a new light attack combo after a
previous light attack combo ... Be able to rotate the FF stun strike combo animation during the second F stun strike animation, as the hammer is coming down, from a central axis. (like rotating a turret)
... be able to be steered 185 degrees around in a circle from the original point of aim or directly forward." Applies to the Assault's thunder hammer and the Raptor's daemon maul (one map,
`MeleeTuning.ThunderHammer`), Classic PvP and Musou Mode alike. The owner's recording of the original (2026-11-07, 60 fps, 6.7 s, two F,F slams with a thunder hammer Assault; kept outside the repo) was
measured frame by frame. Code: `MeleeCancel`, `Rush.CanDashAttack`, `Combat.StepPlayer` (the string reset, `SteeredHeading`), `MeleeStep.HopSwing` / `SteerFrom` / `SteerTo` / `SteerRate`,
`MeleeSteer.Heading`, `MeleeTuning.Finisher`, client `NetworkView.Turning.cs` (`SteeredStrike`). Tests: `HammerHopSlamTests`. Test aids (server and client alike): `SM_OLD_HOP_SWING=1`,
`SM_OLD_SLAM_RECOVERY=1`, `SM_OLD_SLAM_STEER=1`.

### Musou Mode: Orks face their target (musou/ork-facing, 2026-11-08; `MusouSim.Version` 22, `TfwRules.Version` 44; Musou Mode only)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-08 (verbatim): "orks should try to face the player more in musou mode. notably, shooter orks running from the player or moving around in a different direction still manage to shoot the player, while not facing their target." Cause found: the server snapped a gunner's facing to its target the tick a burst began (a half turn inside one snapshot) and otherwise faced its walking direction, so a backing-off or flow-routed gunner looked away while its tracers flew. The wire is not at fault (yaw is 256 steps a turn, 1.4 degrees; the client interpolates the angle along the shortest way). Residual client note: a far Ork sent every 5th tick is drawn carrying on along its last step (up to one gap) after it stops to fire; with the turn-first rule this is short.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Musou: fire cone | a ranged Ork (Shoota Boy, Rokkit Boy, Big Shoota Nob and any gunner using the burst) fires a round only with its facing within **30** degrees (each side) of its target; outside it, it turns and the burst waits | degrees | each round | `MusouFacingRules.FireConeDegrees` | ours | ours | low |
| Musou: gunner turn rate | **720** degrees a second while aiming (a half turn in 0.25 s) | deg/s | per tick | `MusouFacingRules.ShooterTurnDegrees` | ours | ours | low |
| Musou: engaged turn rate | **480** degrees a second while moving with the body on its target | deg/s | per tick | `MusouFacingRules.EngageTurnDegrees` | ours | ours | low |
| Musou: facing while moving | a ranged Ork within **1.5** times its range of its target, and a melee Ork within **10** m, moves (backing off, closing in, strafing) with its body turned toward the target, not its walking direction; the Big Shoota Nob at his post likewise | m | per tick | `MusouFacingRules.ShooterEngageScale`, `MeleeEngageRange` | ours | ours | low |

Boss Orks keep their velocity-facing; leashed or idle Orks keep their look-round. Tick cost: 600 Orks stepped in the simulation alone, 0.586 to 0.623 ms a tick (best of 5), about 6 percent.

### Musou Mode: Orks at a point spread out and look round (hotfix/ork-capture-spread, 2026-11-08; `MusouSim.Version` 20; Musou Mode only)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-08: "orks pile up all looking at the center of a point when capturing it - they should spread out a bit and look around." Cause: an Ork retaking a secured point walked to its centre and stopped **3** m short (`MusouSwarmRules.GoalStand`), so a band stood in a heap at the centre still facing the way it walked in (at the centre). Capture rules, timing, counts, damage and targeting are unchanged: every spot lies inside the capture ring, and an Ork inside still counts. Classic PvP untouched.

A goal with no ring (0) keeps the old 3 m stand. ### No on-hit effects on shot players in Classic PvP (claude/classic-no-player-hit-fx, 2026-11-11; client only, not simulated, no protocol or config-hash change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-11 (verbatim): "simply remove instances of weapon on hit visual effects like the stalker bolter explosion cloud on the player target you shot and hit - classic pvp only". The cloud, as captured with `--bolt-fx-demo sm_mp_ranged_sniper_rifle --bolt-fx-armour 0`, is pvp-hit-fx's health-hit burst (`HealthHitBurst`: a red-orange fire burst that turns into a grey smoke cloud for about a second), which every gun played on a hit with no armour left; the Stalker's hits nearly always find the armour gone. This supersedes for Classic PvP the player-hit parts of "Hit decals only on the map" (sparks, armour-hit glows, blood) and of pvp-hit-fx (the burst, the break effect after a shot), and the melta's whole-body burn of fix/melta-burn-onhit. `--player-hit-fx` restores them all.

### Musou Mode: smooth crowd motion (crowd-smooth, 2026-11-08; Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 22, no core protocol bump: `Protocol.Version` stays 64)

Measured first with an engine-free metric (`MusouCrowdSmoothnessTests`: probes with a known true path among a filler crowd, through the real `MusouInterest`, `TfwGuardInterest` and event window, a 50 to 66 ms link, the real client states sampled at 60 fps 3 ticks behind). Causes found: (1) a Stormboy in a hop (state Airborne) was neither carried on past his newest record nor glided, and drawn on straight chords between records: held in the air, then a jump of up to 9.6 m under a full budget; (2) the Guardsmen had no carry-on or glide at all and, under a crowd that fills Musou's 55 KB/s, only the 3 KB/s left of the client's 58: a Guardsman 60 m off had a record about every 48 ticks and was drawn still in 97 % of his moving frames, jumping 5 m; (3) under a full budget the overdue far Orks took it all and a Boy fighting 3 m from the player had a record only every 6th tick; (4) facings came in steps, one per record. | Ashfall boundary block variant per face (Musou, client) | the owner, 2026-11-08: the wall bricks flicker with FSR off and with every FSR 2 preset (his recording: whole blocks of the boundary wall switching between the plain and the darker, grittier face each frame; under FSR 2 they turned to a per-pixel speckle). Cause: the masonry shader hashed each 4 m x 1 m block's variant from floor() of the interpolated plane coordinate, and the boundary's faces lie on whole metres (x or y = +-240, +-244), so the value flipped between two neighbours with every sub-pixel camera change or jitter. The face is now a whole number rounded per vertex and passed flat (`plane_id`); the variants and their layout are otherwise as before. Flicker check (gallery, the game's camera, 1600 x 900, whole frame, pixels whose luma changes by more than 8 inside a patch of changed pixels, wall view like the recording): MSAA 4x + SMAA under a +-0.5 px jitter 0.68 -> 0.002 %, AA off 0.63 -> 0.008 %, FSR 2 Quality, Balanced, Performance on a still camera 0.084 / 0.049 / 0.062 -> 0.000 %, FSR 2 Native AA all changed pixels 1.69 -> 0.26 % (the speckle; the rest edge lines), Compatibility renderer 0.42 -> 0.021 %, a slow turn 1.2-1.5 -> 0.000 %. Test aid `--ashfall-old-wall-hash` | per vertex, rounded to the metre | per frame | `AshfallKitView.MasonryShader` (`plane_id`) | measured (ashfall-no-flicker) | ours | high |
| Ashfall grime pass order (Musou, client) | the owner, 2026-11-08: flickering all over the map with FSR off. Cause: the kit models' grime overlay (blend mix) and its multiply pass (its next pass) are two transparent passes of the same instance at the same depth, which the transparent sort left tied: per instance and per frame either drew first, and mix-then-multiply differs from multiply-then-mix by about 12 % where the soot lies, so whole floor slabs and wall feet switched brightness with any camera change; which way a launch started was chance (about half the launches). Now fixed priorities: the overlay **-12**, the multiply **-11**: after the alpha-to-coverage cut-outs (-100), before the gore ground decals (-10), the impact glow (-1) and every effect (0). Not depth precision (the depth pull at 0, 1e-4, 1e-3 or 1e-2 changed nothing). Flicker check (gate view, MSAA, +-0.5 px jitter, patch pixels): old order 2.0-2.8 % in 4 of 6 launches, new order 0.011-0.012 % in 6 of 6 (as with no grime, 0.007 %); plaza single frame pairs up to 17 % -> at most 0.1 %. Under FSR 2 the grime is folded (no passes) and nothing changed. ### Musou Mode: Ork movement feel (musou-ork-movement, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only; `MusouSim.Version` 28, `TfwRules.Version` 52, both to be renumbered at integration; no protocol or wire change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-09: "storm boys do a lot of walking in place while on the ground. reduce their movement floatiness - the same is true for all orks. make them fan out more and move more intentionally and forcefully with full continuity and flow of movement. increase the distance for active ork behavior and rendering - 300m." Measured first with an engine-free metric (`MusouOrkMovementTests`: a pack of 120 Boyz released 175 m from a player beyond a 24 m gap in a wall, and the two Stormboy squads hunting a player on the S3 tests' floor; per Ork tick in Seek: the share standing still far from the player, the facing off the actual move, the move's heading change a tick, the pack's width across its way, as drawn: the share of frames the run clip plays with the Ork slower than 0.3 m/s). Causes: (1) the client played the run clip for every Ork in Seek at the clip's own rate, whatever he did (`MusouCrowd.ClipOf`), so one standing, waiting or pressed in the crowd ran on the spot and one slower or faster than the stride slid his feet; (2) a Stormboy under orders walked at full speed to within 0.8 m of his place and the crowd and the landing shove pushed him straight back out, so he stepped to and fro every tick (heading change 180 degrees a tick), and between hops (1.7 s of every 3) the squad stood on its landing places; a squad with one member fighting sent all the others to that one member's feet; (3) a running Ork faced where he wanted to go at once, so the crowd's push slid him sideways or backwards under that facing; (4) a melee Ork with a token waited only within 0.8 of his reach (1.28 m for a Boy) while the player's ring pushed him to 1.3 m: he stepped in and out every tick between blows. Before / after (switches `SM_MUSOU_OLD_ORK_MOVE=1`, client `--musou-old-gait`): Stormboys standing on the ground 37.7 % / 0.6 %, their mean ground speed 0.19 / 5.02 m/s, facing off the move mean 32 / 2.5 degrees, heading change a tick p99 132 / 11 degrees, the run on the spot as drawn 66.5 % / 1.3 % of their ground frames (the eased speed's stop); the pack: facing off the move mean 9.2 / 2.5 degrees (p90 22 / 3.3), heading change p95 9.5 / 3.7 degrees (p99 25 / 10), across its way 5.0 / 8.0 m, standing 0 / 0.3 %.

### Musou Mode: the corpse floor (musou-ork-movement, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only; client rules only: no simulation, wire or protocol change, so `MusouSim.Version` and `TfwRules.Version` stay)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-09: "ork corpses should never immediately disappear, same as guardsmen and allied space marines. they should always leave a corpse for at least 10 seconds before disappearing." The new floor wins over 2026-11-08's "if a player cannot see it, it doesn't ever get drawn" (the lead's brief). What took a body away early: (1) every crowd body (Orks, Guardsmen, an aggregate's losses) lay **3** s and sank over 1.5 s (gone 4.5 s after the death); (2) the Ork pool kept **100** bodies and the Guard pool **40**, the oldest out first whatever its age (a grenade's 280 deaths dropped 180 at once); (3) the deaths waiting to be handed out were cut to the last 100; (4) a death past 90 m outside the view left nothing, and an aggregate's loss left a body only within 90 m and at most 6 a section, the Guardsmen's none; (5) a gibbed death left no corpse even where its burst was not drawn (past the gore's 60 m, or the original blood's distance or frame budget); (6) a ragdoll lay **3** s after it settled, and a new throw took the longest-lying doll; (7) a Marine's ragdoll went when its player respawned or left the snapshot (a battle's end dismisses its Marines), and a full cap of 16 dropped the oldest. Not a cause: the server's slots (a dead Ork's slot stays taken through its 2 s of dying, freed ids go to the back of a first-in first-out queue of 2,560, and the client's body is its own copy, kept whatever comes next on the id); the death events (they go first in the event window, three copies). Measured (`MusouCorpseFloorTests`, the pools' bookkeeping run engine-free with the same rules): a grenade's 280 deaths and then 30 a second for 40 s, half of them 150 to 300 m away: before, every one of the 1,480 bodies went under 10 s (the shortest at once); now the shortest lies 10.00 s, the Ork pool peaks at 580 bodies, none dropped young. A bounded clash on the synthetic arena (45 s, one thread, a human beside it): 200 v 200 killed 518 Orks and 146 Guardsmen, the pools peaked at 150 and 78 bodies; 1,000 v 1,000 (`SM_ARMY_PROFILE=1`) 652 and 593, peaks 181 and 194; none dropped young. The server's tick and the 55 KB/s send budget are unchanged (nothing sent or simulated changed). The client draws a body with the vertex-animation tier past the members' 1,800 and the look's 1,000 (bodies have a count of their own, up to the ceiling): a peak of 580 bodies is 580 more instances, in their 32 m cells (culled out of the view). Not measured in the rendered client (no human has played it).

### Musou Mode: elite and Boss Orks in the fight (musou-ork-movement, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only, a war's pool; `MusouSim.Version` 29, to be renumbered at integration; no protocol or wire change; a melee Boss Ork faces his target only while his way is within 45 degrees of it, so round a wall he faces where he goes)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-09: "boss and elite orks are having issues that we fixed with regular orks. / not taking visibly doing things when the player or other enemy targets (the ork elite/bosses targets) / boss ork shootas just run away instead of backpedaling and shooting / boss ork boys dont take melee swings, they just kind of run around in melee combat." Kinds looked at: Nob, 'Ard Boy, Big Shoota Nob, the Warboss and the four Boss Orks (Boss Boy, Boss Shoota Boy, Boss 'Ard Boy, Boss Nob); the Weirdboy, Rokkit Boy, Stormboy and Scrap Mek keep their own rules. Measured (`MusouEliteOrkTests`: one Ork 10 m from a standing target, alone and with 12 Boyz round the target; a shooter 22 m from a target walking in at 3 m/s; each against a player and a Guard squad; 12 to 14 s, the fight on). Causes: (1) a Boss Ork turned to his smoothed velocity every tick and skipped the engaged Orks' rule of facing the target while moving: a Boss Shoota backing off turned round and ran (193 of 420 ticks retreating with his back to the target, facing 92 degrees off it on average) and fired 7 rounds to a Shoota Boy's 12; (2) a target's melee tokens (6 a player, 12 a squad) go to the nearest Ork asking, so with Boyz at it a wider body never won one, and the even push apart held a 3x body beyond its reach: a Nob, a Boss Boy, 'Ard Boy or Nob and the Warboss struck **0** blows in 12 s through 12 Boyz, circling the crowd (alone each swung 5 to 7 times). Before / after (server `SM_MUSOU_OLD_ELITES=1`): through the crowd 0 / 5 to 7 blows, the first after 1.6 to 2.8 s, facing off the target within 6 m 0 degrees; the Boss Shoota's back turned 193 / 0 ticks, backing off facing the target 17 / 230 ticks, facing off it 92 / 0 degrees, rounds 7 / 10. Not changed: the client draws a wind-up, strike and recovery with the attack clip and a shooter's burst as before for every kind (the Big Shoota's gun model and tracers are another session's).

### Musou Mode: no Ork formations, 80 % of the Orks (musou-ork-movement, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only; `TfwRules.Version` 53, to be renumbered at integration; no protocol or wire change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-09, with a screenshot: "there are currently on occasion large rectangular formations of orks that move from their points to imperial captured points. they walk through objects, don't interact with the world or fight. completely remove those orks from musou mode. they're depicted in the reference screenshot. reduce the total amount of orks on the map to 80% of current." What they were: the battle flow's Ork armies (expansion S6) kept an **aggregate**, men counted but not simulated, beyond the real cap (480 real army Orks) and past 330 m of every human; the client drew it as up to **900** impostors in the army's formation slots (rows of up to 36 files, 1.6 m by 1.4 m), carried along the army's way and through anything on it, killed only by the far clash's dice. A wave of 1,000 against a near point was 480 real Orks and a rectangle of 520 behind them. Choice: **every Ork that exists is a real crowd Ork** (not: drop the armies), because the armies carry the battle flow itself (waves with committed destinations, retakes of points, retreats, the Guard garrisons' fights, the Waaagh! barks and the map's markers); only their Ork aggregate goes. Dependencies checked: a point's count takes the real Orks on it (`OrksInside`; the aggregate's own count `ArmyOrksOn` is off); the far clash fights the real Orks at a point against the Guard aggregates there (their losses are real deaths, counted by the KO path as every Ork's); the pacing (lulls, peaks, the muster's 30 s, the destinations) is unchanged; the Guard armies keep their aggregates and impostors (not in the request; a follow-up if wanted). Before / after on the synthetic arena (`OrkTotalsProfileTests`, `SM_ARMY_PROFILE=1`; 180 simulated s, one human at the landing zone, patrols and Scrap Meks on, a wave of 1,000 sent at once; this PC, one thread): real Orks alive at most **2109** / **1684** (80 %), the armies' real at most 480 / 384, aggregate Orks **984** / **0** (a queue of spawns the next ticks make, never drawn: at most 368 for the test aid's whole wave at once), all Orks at most **2588** / **1684** (65 %); tick mean **7.07** / **2.88** ms, p99 **39.98** / **4.38** ms, max **80.4** / **20.0** ms (a first after-run: 3.48 / 10.17 / 52.0 ms); Orks killed 2847 / 2175. Not seen by a human.

### Polish pass P3 (claude/polish-p3, 2026-11-11; client only; first frames and loads: no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change)

The plan's items 16 in part and 29 (`docs/polish-pass-plan.md`; 29's stall turned out to be the map's sound file read in the first frame of play, not the stream objects; item 31 was checked and needs no change); of item 2's remainder the ragdoll world's shape stays on the main thread (made on the load's worker it crashed the Compatibility renderer's load in about half of the Musou joins, so that part was taken out again). Nothing here changes what a player does or what the server decides: the same sounds, shapes and pictures, made at another moment or by another thread. ### Polish pass P2 (claude/polish-p2, 2026-11-10; client, content, server; load time only: no simulation, wire, protocol or config-hash change)

The plan's items 1 and 2 (`docs/polish-pass-plan.md`): the Ashfall layout cache and the map load off the main thread. Baseline and after numbers: `docs/milestones.md`, "Polish pass P2".

| Ashfall layout cache (Musou, added content) | the generated level and dressing of a layout are written once to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\sm-reimpl\cache\ashfall\<layout>-v<level version>-g<graybox version>-d<dressing version>-<8 bytes of the simulation assembly's module version id>-<8 bytes of the reader assembly's>-<process>.bin` (a derived file, nothing from the install; never in the repository) and read back by the client at every join and by the server at every start; a new build of the generator or the reader has a new key, so neither ever serves a stale layout; the client's and the server's files are kept apart by the process name and each kind keeps its newest **2**; after each write the layout's files without a process ending (the first format's `<layout>-v<level version>-g<graybox version>-d<dressing version>-<8 bytes>.bin`) and write temporaries older than **10 min** (a crash's leftovers) are deleted too, never the other kind's files nor any other file; the level's own hash is in the file and in the map hash the server and client compare. Format (version **2**): magic, format version, key, layout, hash, parts (kind, corners), points, areas, spawns, the dressing's version, items, hidden parts, structures, item parts, flags, then an FNV-1a 64 checksum over all of that and an end mark; the end mark and the checksum are checked before anything is parsed; a cut, damaged or longer file, or one that fails to parse, is refused, the layout generated and written again (through a per-process temporary name). `SM_NO_ASHFALL_CACHE=1` (both) and the client's `--no-ashfall-cache` generate as before | — | per join, per server start | `SmContent.Extras.Musou.AshfallLayoutCache`, `TfwAshfallContent`, `TfwWorld.Load` | the lead's decision (2026-11-10, the plan's question 6) | ours | high |

### Musou Mode: the big Orks' deaths and gait (musou-big-ork-deaths, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode only; the deaths and gait client presentation; the bodies against the map in the simulation, `MusouSim.Version` 34, to be renumbered at integration; no protocol change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-09 (relayed by the lead): "the elite and boss orks and the warboss need to have death animations. they also look like they move in slow motion because of the way they're scaled up. resolve these issues." Found with the client's new stage, `--musou-crowd-test` (the real `MusouLooks` and `MusouCrowd`, scripted Orks that run and die): the crowd plays the Nob's and the Boss Orks' death clip (`BOY_1HM_DIE_Basic_02`, the gun kinds `BOY_2HR_DIE_Fall_Forward_01`) and lays them down in both the skinned and the vertex-animation tiers whenever a body is handed over. Two things took that away. (1) The gore tears apart every death it calls an explosion (a frag, launcher or plasma burst, every bolt blast, a lascannon shot) and a share of the melee and strafe deaths, and a torn death leaves no body: since a bolt weapon's round bursts at every enemy it strikes (`MusouDeathKind.BoltBlast`), most bolter kills of a big Ork left only a spray. (2) The Warboss's death clip, `WB_REC_Explode`, is a blast reaction that ends with him standing (seen at 1.0 s crouched, at 2.9 s up again). Slow motion: the run plays at the drawn speed over the clip's planted-foot speed at the look's scale (spec "Musou Mode: Ork movement feel"), so a Boss Ork drawn 3x at 4.4 m/s against the run's 16.5 to 18 m/s at 3x ran at 0.25 to 0.27x; the Warboss's walk was never measured (his rig's foot bones have other names) and ran at 0.77x of the 6 m/s fallback. Attacks, staggers and deaths play on the server's state clock at 1x and turns follow the server's facing: none of those was scaled. The simulation's speeds are not changed (gameplay; the other option, faster big Orks, is the lead's and the owner's to decide). Not seen by a human in a match; stage stills in `<media folder>\previews\musou-big-ork-deaths`.

Addition (the owner, 2026-11-09, with a screen recording of the shipped build on Ashfall, "Ashfall Citadel" in its summary): "boss enemies are getting stuck along objects and moving in slow motion". In the recording a Boss Shoota Boy at a raised walkway sways on the spot while he fires (his ranged hold, not a snag), and in the last 15 s two Boss Orks stand at a stair landing's parapet beside the player two steps above them without a blow. Measured on the Ashfall draft 10 walk graph (the generator alone; 12 crossings of 50 m or more per kind, 60 s each): no big Ork stood stuck where a Boy did not (the one 58 s stand, a target off the graph, was every kind's), but the Boss Orks moved at 3.80 to 3.84 m/s of their 4.4 (the Warboss 4.58 of 4.6, the Nob 4.38 of 4.4): real ground speed lost scraping along the walls on top of the slow stride. Causes and fixes in the rows below and in `MusouSim.BigBodies.cs`. The map's collision itself is not touched (the Ashfall session's).

### Musou Mode: the Orks' pace and charge (musou-big-ork-deaths, 2026-11-09; Musou Mode's war only (the 5-wave run as pinned); `MusouSim.Version` 35, to be renumbered at integration; no protocol, wire or per-Ork byte change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-09 (relayed by the lead): "make orks run 20% faster, and sprint to 'charge' the enemy when they reach within 30m of an enemy". The data has no sprint speed for the Orks (the Musou kinds' speeds are ours); the boy rig's sprint clip `BOY_1HM_NAV_Sprint_F_01` covers 9.91 m/s on its planted feet and its run `BOY_1HM_NAV_Run_F_*` 5.98 (measured, spec "Ork gait"), so the sprint is the paced run times that ratio, at most the clip's own speed. Server-authoritative; the client tells the sprint by the drawn speed (no byte). A side effect to weigh: TF3's box of six Guard squads against sixty Boyz (`GuardSimTests`) now goes to the Orks (the squads gone by 60 s, 21 Boyz left; before, the Guards won within 90 s); the Guard balance is not retuned here. Not seen by a human.

The rollback restores every bulk count that 2026-11-09's "80% of current" lowered; that change's other half, an Ork army of real Orks alone (no aggregates, no impostor formations), is kept. The Orks drawn bigger than a Boy: the Nob and the Big Shoota Nob (the co-op Nob models, 3.0 m against the Boy's 2.15 m) and the four Boss Orks (3x); the 'Ard Boy is a Boy's size and the Warboss stays one (the elite share of the crowds, waves and armies is unchanged). Measured (`OrkTotalsProfileTests`; this PC under another session's full load, so the times are high and only their ratios count): 180 s with a wave of 1000: at 80 % (before this) real Orks at most 1646, tick mean 4.2 ms, p99 28 ms; at 100 % with the old big spawns 2023, 4.2 to 5.0 ms, p99 9 to 22 ms; now 2091, 4.8 ms, 14 ms, the big Orks off the caps at most 108; 600 s: old 5.4 ms, p99 24.6 ms; now 6.2 ms, 24.4 ms (8 Boss Orks came, at most 3 alive: the Guardsmen kill them); with 8 Boss Orks that cannot fall placed at the start (`SM_ARMY_PROFILE_BOSSES=8`, their retinues and the Nobs' twins): 8.1 ms, p99 60 ms, against 6.9 ms and 48 ms for 2 under the old rules. The Guardsmen at full numbers: TF3's box (sixty Boyz, no Nobs) unchanged, six squads win in 34 s; the hold trial (`GuardHoldTrialTests`, 60 against 60 at the run's middle elite share) held **1** of 20 with the Nobs' twins (12 with one of each; target 8 to 12): `GuardRules.Strength` about **1.1** (was 0.875) brings it to 10 (1.0: 5, 1.25: 15, 1.4: 19); raised to 1.1 on the owner's word the same day ("Raise the guards to 1.1"; `TfwRules.Version` 64), the test at the twins again; the far clash weighs no elites (unchanged). No human has played it.

### Musou's arsenal: the base (W0, claude/arsenal-w0, 2026-11-10; Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change)

The owner approved docs/new-weapons-design.md as written (2026-11-10). W0 adds the base the four items are built on and no item yet: nothing a player meets changes, in Musou Mode or anywhere else.
- **The registry.** Four names, appended at the ends of Musou's lists by their milestones (no existing index moves): `sm_mp_exotic_auto_cannon` (W1, ours: the loyalist twin of the install's Chaos file), `sm_mp_melee_lightning_claw` (W2, ours), `sm_mp_melee_power_spear` (W3, ours), `sm_mp_eq_demolition_charge` (W4, the install's own file, which no class lists). `ArsenalRules` (SmSim) and `Arsenal` (SmContent) in `Extras/Musou/Arsenal/`; `Arsenal.Append` runs in the match tuning's load dispatcher before `MusouLoadout.Prepare`, under `ContentExtras.Musou` only.
- **Core hooks** (pinned in `ExtrasBoundaryTests`, each a no-op without Musou's content: the flag, or for the name-only content hooks our own names; the client's model and clip hooks check the Musou flag too, since the Remote Detonators' name is an install name): `MpClasses.ExtrasMeleeMap` (an added melee weapon on a data weapon's map), `Loadouts.ExtrasWieldsHammer` (the hammer's jump-pack rules), `PerkCatalog.ExtrasItems` (the customizer's rows, only for a content profile with Musou: `PerkCatalog.For`, `CustomizationCatalog.For`, `CustomizerServices.Catalog`) with `ProfileViews.ExtrasSetCatalog` (Musou's loadout set read and repaired with Musou's catalogue, so a Musou slot keeps an arsenal item; Classic's slots with the data's), `WeaponRig.ExtrasWeaponModel` (a model of another package or built in code, and the always-held flag), `NetworkView.ExtrasThrownVisual` (a thrown item's model), `AnimationAlias.ExtrasAnimationAlias` (the data weapon whose animations an added one plays: read by the hip-fire, sprint, reload and flinch name rules, the falls through the hip-fire family, and the client's hammer stance).
- **The clip-speed factor** (`MeleeTuning.WeaponMap.ClipSpeed`): an added map's strikes play that many times faster than their clips (every step's duration, hit and windows divided by it); 1 for every map of the data, whose reads stay byte-identical. The client poses a single-clip strike at the same rate (`NetworkView.MeleeClipSpeed`); a strike with distance variants is scaled to the step's duration already. The values (the claw 1.25, the spear 0.85) come with W2 and W3.
- **The animation seam** (lead 2026-11-10: the owner wants custom animations for the claw and the spear, authored to the design's hit times, used once he approves them): the claw's and the spear's strikes play the power sword's and the thunder hammer's clips as stand-ins (the borrowed maps' variant clips, and their light and heavy clip lists through `AnimationAlias`, `NetworkView.cs` and `NetworkView.Reactions.cs`); one client hook, `NetworkView.ExtrasMeleeClip` (in `OwnStrikeClip`, `NetworkView.MeleeLock.cs`), gives a strike (weapon, light or heavy, step) a clip of its own and its rate (1: authored to the simulation's timing), posed alone. The simulation never reads it: a custom clip changes no hit, window or duration. Each weapon's table is a partial of its own milestone (`LightningClawClip`, `PowerSpearClip`). Not in W0: a source for clips that are not in the install (the rig's clips are read from its packfile only); it comes with the approved clips.
- **Musou call sites** (no-op partial methods of `World.Arsenal.cs`, one implementer each): the cleave (`ArsenalCleave`), a weapon's own blast at every enemy a round strikes (`ArsenalShotBlast`, the bolt blasts' path), the jump pack's events (`ArsenalJump`), a projectile meeting an enemy or a contraption (`ArsenalProjectileMeets`), once a tick (`ArsenalStep`), and the per-item refill period (`ArsenalRefillSeconds`; 15 s for every item until W4).
- **Not yet hooked** (for W2 and W3 to raise with the lead): the jump pack's own moves (the dash attack, the ground pound, the air slash) are the pack's, not the weapon's, so the clip-speed factor does not reach them; the presentation name rules other than the five above (hit sounds, the power flash, the power sword's glow and idle sound) read the names as they are. Both are hooked by W0b (next section).

### Musou's arsenal: W0b, presentation by source and the pack moves' clip speed (claude/arsenal-w0b, 2026-11-10; client presentation only, Musou Mode only; no simulation, wire, protocol, config-hash or rules-version change)

The lead's brief (2026-11-10), after W1 to W3 met the two gaps above: the claw was silent ("sound note: wargear sm_mp_melee_lightning_claw not found"), and the autocannon's muzzle flash, tracer, casings, fire sound and HUD reticle and ammunition display never loaded, since the catalogues read only class-named wargear and `csm_mp_exotic_auto_cannon` is in no class.
- **Presentation by source.** Each added item names the install files it shows and sounds as (`Arsenal.PresentationSources`, `Extras/Musou/Arsenal/ArsenalPresentation.cs`); one client hook, `NetworkView.ExtrasPresentationSources` (`NetworkView.Presentation.cs`), asks for them, and only in a Musou match (the match config's `ContentExtras.Musou`) for the arsenal's names. The client reads the effect catalogue with those files beside the classes' (`EffectCatalogue.Load(gameDir, extraWargear)`) and both catalogues copy the first candidate's entries under the item's name (`EffectCatalogue.WithSources`, `SoundTriggers.WithSources`: the weapon's effects; the file's sound commands, its hit, shot-hit, melee-hit and charge-hit containers and its melee abilities' hit containers). The name rules read the first source's name (`NetworkView.PresentedAs`): the power flash's kind and scale, the sword's glow, flare, contact point and deployed effects (`NetworkView.MeleeFx.cs`), the idle hum and its quieter sword level (`HumOf`), the procedural hit sound (`--generated-melee-hit-sound` only). With no sources (every match without Musou) both loads are the same calls as before and the catalogues are the same objects; the name rules see the names themselves.
- **The HUD.** Two hooks under `Hud.Content` (the match's content, set each frame by the match view): `Hud.ExtrasReticle` and `Hud.ExtrasWeaponBox` give the autocannon the movie's own reticle and ammunition display (`Arsenal.Reticle`, `Arsenal.WeaponBox`). The core rules choose by `ui_data/weapon_type`, which is "grenade_launcher" in the twin, and know no autocannon, so a Classic HUD is unchanged.
- **The pack moves' clip speed** (`NetworkView.MoveClipSpeed`, hook `NetworkView.ExtrasMoveClipSpeed`, Musou match and arsenal names only): the melee weapon's map clip speed (`MeleeTuning.WeaponMap.ClipSpeed`) reaches the clips its strike map does not time. Presentation only; the simulation's timings are as they were.
- **The Y,Y finishers** were reached already: the simulation builds them with the map's clip speed (they are heavy steps), and the client poses them through `AttackVariants` (a single clip at `MeleeClipSpeed`, variants scaled to the step's shortened duration).
- **The hammer's animation rules by alias** (`AnimationAlias`, W0's hook, so the spear plays as the hammer): the hammer's own air slash clip (`HammerSlash`), the hammer's sprint attack for the charge (`HammerRush`), both hands on the haft (`HammerHoldsBothHands`, which also holsters the pistol: `WeaponRig.StowPistol`, so the bolt pistol leaves the left hand in the spear's stance and strikes, as with the hammer; W3's note), the `--old-strike-legs` stride rule and the transition probe's two-handed flag.
- **Not hooked:** Musou's predicted strike contact on Orks (`MusouContactRules.PredictsMelee`, a power-sword name rule in Musou's own code: W2's to raise); the kill feed's and weapon box's weapon picture (`UiArt.WeaponIcon` by `ui_data`, which our names lack; W1's name and picture work).

### Musou Mode: the dizzy boss (claude/musou-boss-dizzy, owner 2026-11-14; client only, no protocol or version change; Musou Mode only)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-14: "bosses turn around 180 degrees when stunned - fix that. create a new "dizzy" animation for them where they stand in place and stars appear above their head circling around, until they are no longer stunned." Cause of the turn: the sim's yaw never changed in a stun (`MusouSim.StepBossStun`); the crowd drew the Warboss's stagger clip, `WB_Att_Charge_wall_hit_exit`, whose pose turns the body round. A stunned boss now draws its idle clip. The install has no dizzy or daze clip (the Warboss rig's 48 clips and the Ork boy rig have none), so the sway is a procedural lean on the idle.

### The charge after a swing and the instant S cancel (charge-responsive; protocol 69, used by the simulation; every mode)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-12: "(Assault marine/raptor) Currently if you try to charge immediately after a light attack or light attack combo you cannot. You should immediately be able to charge after a melee attack, or vice versa."; "For tactical and assault/raptor, currently you have to hold S or back on stick for ~.5s to [cancel] the charge. The charge should be cancelled instantaneously as soon as the S key or back on left joystick is triggered. Basically, it should be easy and responsive to trigger the cancelling of the charge with backpedal."
Code: `ChargeCancel.CanChargeFromMelee`, `ChargeCancel.BackInstant`, `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (the charge press ends the attack), `Rush.Begin` (the instant S end), `SimConfig.ChargeAfterMelee` / `ChargeInstantCancel` (restore switches `--old-charge-after-melee`, `--old-charge-cancel-delay`). Tests: `ChargeResponsiveTests`.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cause of the wait after a swing | `Rush.CanStart` refused a body with a melee attack under way (`MeleeStep > 0`), so a charge press (Shift + W + F) during a light attack, its combo or a heavy strike was left unused and only the input buffer (0.3 s) replayed it after the whole clip (about 1 s of the swing). Not the cause: the melee wait (`MeleeLock`, up to the combo window), the charge's own 1 s spacing, the sprint or the jump-pack class rule (the Assault and Raptor charge from the ground, which they are after a swing) | s | per press | `Rush.CanStart`, `Combat.StepPlayerCore` | reproduced in the tests (a press at any tick of a swing did nothing) | observed | high |
| The charge after a swing | a charge press with the swing's hit landed (the attack time before the tick at least its hit time; on the install a light attack's hit is about 0.2 to 0.4 s in) ends the attack, its queued next attack and its melee wait and starts the charge on that very tick; a press before the hit does not (a swing is not thrown away unhit; the input buffer replays it at the hit when within 0.3 s). Every melee attack of the class counts: light attacks, any step of a combo, heavy strikes. The charge's other rules are unchanged (W held, on the ground, no jump-pack phase, no throw, no reaction, the 1 s spacing from the last charge) | s | per press edge | `ChargeCancel.CanChargeFromMelee`, `Combat.StepPlayerCore` | owner 2026-11-12; the hit as the earliest point and "every melee attack" ours | owner's decision (the gate ours) | estimate |
| A swing after a charge | a melee press ends the charge and swings at once (protocol 54, unchanged; its cancel wait for the cancelled clip's end keeps the swing after that from starting early). After an S cancel or the clip's end the next swing starts on the first tick (nothing waits: the melee wait of the swing the charge came from is cleared when the charge starts) | s | per press | `MeleeCancel.Apply`, `Combat.StepPlayerCore` | owner 2026-11-12 ("or vice versa") | owner's decision | medium |
| The S cancel at once | S held back ends the bull rush on the tick after its start or any later tick, with no wait for the stick branch (it was 0.467 s); keyboard S, S + A, S + D, a pad's stick in the back three of eight sectors and at least **0.5** of full length (`ChargeCancel.InstantBackStick`, so drift and a loose return through the middle do not cancel; the cancel at the old branch keeps the 0.1 dead zone). W, A, D alone and a weak back pull end nothing early. Not the dash attack's lunge (no input ends it, as before); the other phases keep their stick rules | - | per tick | `ChargeCancel.BackInstant`, `Rush.Begin` | owner 2026-11-12; the 0.5 ours | owner's decision (the value ours) | estimate |
| S held at the start | needs no rule: the start needs W (the stick's forward part at least 0.7; a keyboard's W + S cancel out), so S cannot be held on the press tick; no fresh press is needed after it, S from the second tick cancels | - | per tick | `Rush.CanStart` | ours | ours | medium |

### Melee cancels a charge at once, charge > melee chains, and Musou melee spam (charge-melee-chain; protocol 70, used by the simulation; every mode, the spam Musou Mode only)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-12: "The one second spacing should only apply to discrete combat moves." / "If I charge, then right click for melee light attack mid charge, it should happen immediately. The same for if I melee attack right at the end of a charge. I should not be able to charge and charge again in the middle of a charge. But I should be able to charge>melee>charge>melee and chain them together endlessly without any delays or cooldowns." / "In Musou mode only, a player should be able to spam melee attacks with no cooldown or delay."
Code: `ChargeCancel.MeleeEndsCharge`, `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (the cancel, the spacing reset, the spam), `SimConfig.ChargeMeleeChain` (restore switch `--old-charge-melee-chain`), `SimConfig.MeleeSpam` (hook `ExtrasMeleeSpam`, Musou) and `SimConfig.MusouMeleeCooldown` (restore switch `--musou-melee-cooldown`). Tests: `ChargeMeleeChainTests`.

### Musou Mode: Ork swing commit (musou/ork-swing-commit, 2026-11-12; `MusouSim.Version` 53, `TfwRules.Version` 78; no protocol or wire change; Musou Mode only)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-12: "Make Ork attacks commit to a direction. The current melee windup turns an Ork directly toward its target each tick, including just before checking whether the attack connects. That means circling around an attacker may not evade the swing as naturally as the animation suggests. I'd test bounded early tracking followed by a committed swing, so positioning and dodging feel more trustworthy." Before: `MusouSim.Behave`'s wind-up case re-faced the target every tick and then read that facing in the cone check, so the cone could never fail (a circling player was hit at every speed, 0 to 5 degrees off). Now the first part of the wind-up turns toward the target, then the facing is locked and the blow needs the target within reach and within the cone of the locked facing. Covers every melee Ork through that path (Boyz, Gretchin, Nobs, Boss Orks, the Warboss's ordinary swing); the Warboss's ground slam (a ring, no direction) and charge (line locked at its start) keep their own rules. The 5-wave run (no crowd rules) and Classic PvP are unchanged. The facing reaches the client in the entity record's yaw byte (already on the wire), so a drawn Ork shows the locked direction.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Musou: swing tracking share | the wind-up turns toward the target only in its first **0.3** (4 of a Boy's 15 ticks, 0.13 s of 0.5 s) | share of the wind-up | per wind-up | `MusouSwingRules.TrackShare` | owner 2026-11-12 (the idea); the value ours (0.4 first tried: a run at 5 m/s round a Boy at 1.2 m was still hit) | ours | estimate |
| Musou: swing tracking turn rate | **540** | degrees a second | per tick in the tracking share | `MusouSwingRules.TrackTurnDegrees` | ours (up to 72 degrees of re-aim in 0.13 s; an engaged Ork's walking turn is 480) | ours | estimate |
| Musou: swing entry | no snap to the target when the wind-up starts: the Ork turns from the facing it has, at the rate above, for at least 1 tick of the share (a wind-up of 3 ticks or fewer still turns); the Telegraph marker is sent at the start and shows the early aim, not the locked direction (no new wire field) | - | at wind-up start | `MusouSim.Behave` melee start, `MusouSwingRules.TrackTicks` | reviewer 2026-11-13 | ours | estimate |
| Musou: swing lock | after the tracking share the facing is held to the blow; the blow lands on a target within reach (`MeleeRange` + 0.3 m) and **60** degrees (`MeleeConeDegrees`, each side) of the locked facing | degrees | at the end of the wind-up | `MusouSim.Behave` wind-up case, `TrackSwing` | owner 2026-11-12; the cone as before | ours | estimate |
| Musou: measured dodge | a player circling a Boy at 1.2 m from the wind-up's start: hit at 0 to 3 m/s (41 degrees off at 3; unchanged by dropping the entry snap, as Orks already face the target when they start), dodged from **4.5** m/s (215 degrees a second; run 5, walk 3, sprint 8 m/s); the Warboss (reach 5.4 m) at 4.8 m and 6 m/s: still hit (27 degrees), dodged by stepping out of reach | m/s | per swing | `MusouSwingCommitTests` | measured | observed | high (the sim); the feel is to check in play |
| Restore switch | `--musou-ork-swing-tracking` (server and every client; hashed in Musou's block only when on) | - | - | `SimConfig.MusouOrkSwingTracking`, `MusouSim.OldSwingTracking` | ours | ours | - |
### Hit effects at range and 30 % stronger (onhit-range-intensity, 2026-11-13; client only, not simulated, no protocol or config-hash change)

Source: the owner, 2026-11-13 (verbatim): "i'm not seeing at range when shooting with lascannon and stalker bolter any on hit effects - armor and health yellow and red splashes and particles respectively. investigate this and in general increase the intensity of both by 30%". Cause found by capture (the Stalker and the Lascannon are hit-scan, so they take the same path as every weapon): the yellow hit spot (0.24 m radius), the red break and bare-armour glow and the particle effects were fixed sizes in metres, so at 40 to 80 m they covered a few pixels or none (a hip view at 80 m: the red glow 9 pixels against 339 at 20 m); and in Classic PvP the on-player particles are off at every range since the owner's decision of 2026-11-11, so only the model's glows remain there.

| Parameter | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Size kept at range | a hit effect is grown so that it is at least as large on screen as at the reference: factor = (camera distance x tan(fov/2)) / (12 m x tan(35 deg)), at least 1; the yellow hit spot's radius up to 6x, particle effects (armour-hit effects, sparks, health-hit burst, the data's own effects on the hit) up to 3x, the red glow card up to 1.5x; the armour break effect is not grown (it is large already). A scoped view (Stalker 10 deg, Lascannon 5.75 deg) grows little. `--old-hit-fx-range` restores the fixed sizes | factor | per frame (models), per hit (particles) | `HitFxScaleRules.RangeScale`, `NetworkView.HitFxModelScale`, `NetworkView.HitFxParticleScale` | owner 2026-11-13 (the request); the reference, the caps and the rule are ours | ours | low |
| Intensity | x1.3 on the yellow hit glow and the red break and bare-armour glow (shader brightness: `k_hit`, `k_brk`), x1.3 on the size of the particle effects played on a hit player and of the armour break effect; particle counts are the data's; the recharge glow is unchanged. `--old-hit-fx-intensity` restores 1.0 | factor | per hit | `HitFxScaleRules.Intensity`, `CharacterViewer.HitFxIntensity` | owner 2026-11-13 ("by 30%"); what "intensity" means for each effect is ours | owner's number / ours (definition) | medium |
| Spark particles on a hit player (Classic PvP; reverses the removal of 2026-11-11; its burst part is dropped again in the next row) | owner 2026-11-13 (verbatim): "bring back the spark and burst particles on hit". Classic PvP draws the on-hit particle effects on a player again by default: the armour-hit effects and spark fans on raised armour, the health-hit burst (`HealthHitBurst`) on a bare body, the weapon's own hit container effects (decals still only on the map). The bare-armour model flash and the break effect of 2026-11-11 stay. All at the range growth and x1.3 of the rows above. `--no-player-hit-fx` brings the no-particle look of 2026-11-11 back (`--player-hit-fx` is now the default and does nothing) | - | per hit | `PlayerHitFxRules.NoParticlesFlag`, `NetworkView.PlayerHitFxFlag` | the owner (2026-11-13) | owner's decision | high |
| Large burst on a hit player (Classic PvP; reverses the burst part of the row above) | owner 2026-11-13 (verbatim, after the first preview): "classic pvp mode: keep all on hit effects except the one in this reference image" and "there should only be large explosive visual effects on ranged weapon shots in musou mode. in classic pvp mode its only the yellow and red spawns and yellow and red glows that are triggered when a player is shot or meleed". Dropped in Classic PvP on a hit player: the health-hit burst (`HealthHitBurst`: red-orange sprites from `bolter_dmg_body_tough_mp`, `plasma_dmg_body_mp`, `sm_armor_dmg_bodyglow`, `sm_armor_dmg` with dark smoke), the old red streak splash, and the weapon's hit container on a body (the flesh and armour impact effects, e.g. the Stalker's cloud). Kept: the data's armour-hit and inactive-hit effects (`armourshield_hit`, `armourshield_inactive_hit`: yellow and red glows), the spark fans (`hit_ranged_armour_generic`, yellow on armour; the same fan tinted red on a bare body, ours), the model's yellow and red glows, the break effect. Musou Mode keeps the burst and container on ranged hits. `--player-hit-burst` brings the large look back in Classic | - | per hit | `PlayerHitFxRules.LookFor`, `NetworkView.HitBurstDrawn` | the owner (2026-11-13); the red sparks are ours | owner's decision / ours | high |
| Glow and sparks for every damage on a player (Classic PvP and Musou Mode; protocol 71) | owner 2026-11-13 (verbatim): "any melee damage should also trigger the glows", "charge/bull rush, air slash landing, ground pound, light melee combo, F stun strike moves, any sort of damage should trigger the sparks and glows". Driven only by damage the server confirms, no team, line-of-sight, radius or cone guessing (an earlier geometry-based version lit allies and players behind walls and was removed; the version after it read a started hit reaction, which light melee, hyper-armoured hits and kills never start, and always read yellow). (a) Protocol 71 adds a damage mark to every player's record (one byte after the evade byte; `PlayerState.DamageCount`, `DamageShield`, `DamageHealth`): a counter, modulo 8, that `Combat.ApplyDamage` raises at most once per tick per victim (`PlayerState.DamageFresh`, cleared at the start of every player tick in `Combat.StepPlayer`, on the server and in the client prediction: a many-pellet weapon or several sources in one tick cannot wrap it) for every damage that takes something (every weapon, melee kind, rush, blast, Musou enemy hit: all go through it; a damage that takes neither shield nor health, zero multipliers, leaves the mark alone), bits for whether the damages of that tick took shield and health (ORed over the tick; both can be set; the client reads red when health was hit, also when the shield broke in the same tick, else yellow; a mark with neither bit shows no glow), bit 5 = damaged already this tick, bits 6..7 zero. A change in another player's counter since the last record shows the glow and sparks on his model, with the right colour (`NetworkView.DamageMarkGlows`, `PlayerHitFxRules.MarkShowsGlow`); a first sight, a record after a death (a respawn keeps the counter; the alive flags tell it) and the killing blow (a corpse) show none; a player who left is forgotten each frame, so a rejoin with his id is a first sight; it survives lost snapshots (a change is a change). (b) The own hit report still draws the own melee and splash damage on its last victim at once (`NetworkView.OwnHitReportGlow`; a report names only the last victim of its tick, so the mark also covers any further victims). One glow per damage event per victim within 0.25 s (`PlayerHitFxRules.DedupePasses`, ours), stamped by every glow including a shot's, so a shot (which draws its own at the shot record) and a melee strike that both mark are drawn once; the mark path runs after the remote shots each frame. Not on the own body (not drawn); no falls (the sim has no fall damage). Musou Mode: the same code runs, so an Ork's strike on a Marine now glows that Marine in other players' views too (any damage), and Musou's own contact effects on Orks are untouched. Wire cost: the slim record 47 -> 48 bytes, the fullest 16-player snapshot 1193 -> 1195 bytes with one projectile record fewer (13 -> 12) and the 4 guaranteed shots kept; the config hash does not change. `--no-damage-glow` removes the glow and sparks of these damages (the behaviour before) | - | per damage | `Combat.ApplyDamage`, `Protocol` (slim record), `NetworkView.PlayerDamageGlow`, `PlayerHitFxRules` | the owner (2026-11-13); the 0.25 s, the counter's width and the reading of the bits are ours | owner's decision / ours | medium |
