### Hop rules: the ledge jump after a charge, the hop cutting the melee wait, the hop out of the aerial tackle (sim/hop-rules; protocol 72, used by the simulation; Assault Marine and Raptor)

Sources: the owner, 2026-11-14: "classic pvp and musou mode - you should be able to full jump as normal when you are charging off of a ledge. currently if you jump after charging off a ledge, you will not jump and will just fall straight down." / "when a assault marine/raptor is melee swinging, he should be able to follow it up hop>melee swing. currently, melee swing>hop>melee swing has a delay before the follow up melee swing. keep the cooldown on light combo attack melee swings but make a hop reduce it so that it feels more responsive, but not completely gone so that melee>hop allows you to rapidly spam melee attacks." / "arial tackle/flying tackle should cancel a hop as raptor/assault marine. currently if you try to hop while performing a flying tackle/arial tackle it does nothing and you must wait for the arial tackle/flying tackle animation to finish playing." (read as: a hop press cancels the tackle into a hop).
Code: `HopTuning`, `SimConfig.HopRules` (restore switch `--old-hop-rules`), `PlayerState.JumpAirOpen`, `JumpPack.Begin` (`airOpen`, `hopNow`), `Evade.Begin` (`ignoreLock`), `Combat.StepPlayerCore`. Tests: `HopRulesTests`.

| Rule | Value | Units | Timing basis | Where | Source | Kind | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cause of the old fall | a Jump press ended a bull rush held in the air (`MeleeCancel.Apply`) and the pack then had nothing to start: in Classic PvP the pack classes in the air only hop (sim/air-jumps), the long press that is the jump was refused, and the walk-off drop took the body straight down. Musou Mode's `JumpPackAirJumps` already let the long press lift the pack in a charge held in the air (synthetic run), so the rule below is Classic's change; Musou keeps its own | - | - | `JumpPack.Begin` (`airLong`) | measured | observed | high |
| Ledge jump after a charge | a fresh Jump press that ends a bull rush held in the air (not on the ground, the rush phase only) opens the air jump (`PlayerState.JumpAirOpen`): the hold past the hop's decision tick (5 ticks, 0.17 s, as on the ground) lifts the pack in the air, committed to the small jump and growing to the full one while Space is held, the cost, power and the dash spacing as on the ground; a tap is the hop as before. The opening lasts until the body lands, a jump phase or a hop starts, or a reaction or death; a plain fall (no charge) never has it. Classic PvP and Musou Mode | - | per press | `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (`chargeOffLedge`), `JumpPack.Begin` (`airOpen`) | owner 2026-11-14 | owner's decision (the opening's lifetime, and the hop's tap rule, ours) | medium |
| Ledge jump: a take-off pressed at the edge | a Jump press (a hold) made on the last grounded ticks of the charge's run, so the body leaves the ground during the 0.2 s take-off, now lifts off in the air when the delay is over (the jump the owner pressed); protocol 71 let the take-off fall straight down with the power spent (row "Take-off", `JumpPack.Begin`'s lift-off). Both modes | - | per press | `JumpPack.Begin` (lift-off) | owner 2026-11-14 | owner's decision (reading ours) | medium |
| Ledge jump: fuel | the air jump costs what the ground jump does (`CostAt` of the hold; a press with less than the zero hold's cost starts nothing in the air: the hop is free); the hop that cancels the tackle costs none. Before this change the air start (Musou Mode) was free at an empty pack: now gated too (`HopRules`) | power | per press | `JumpPack.Begin` | ours | ours | medium |
| Ledge jump: wire | the own record's jump byte, bit 6 in phase None (it is the cut's in the ascent, the small hang's in the hang): the air jump is open. Protocol 72; no size change (slim records, other players: not carried) | - | per record | `Protocol` | ours | ours | high |
| Hop cuts the melee wait | the start of a hop (the jump-pack dash, on the ground or in the air) cuts the melee wait still running (`PlayerState.MeleeLock`: the light combo's wait to its combo window, or a cancel's wait) to **0.5** of what is left, but not below **0.25 s**; a wait already at or under 0.25 s is left alone. The press that cancels the hop (`MeleeCancel`) is accepted once that wait is over, so swing > hop > swing needs about 0.25 s to 0.5 of the old wait instead of all of it. The swing after it sets its own wait as before | s | per hop start | `HopTuning.HopLock`, `Combat.StepPlayerCore` | owner 2026-11-14 (the cut, not the numbers) | ours (0.5 and 0.25 s are estimates) | estimate |
| Hop cut: why it cannot be spammed | the floor (a hop never leaves under 0.25 s of wait), the hop's own spacing (`min_time_between_activations` 0.8 s x the lock scale, one hop per swing at most), and the swing's own wait that each swing sets again. Measured on the synthetic spec (combo wait 0.4 s, hop spacing 0.8 s): the first swing > hop > swing 0.37 s (0.4 s without the hop), then 0.93 s per swing with hops, never below the floor or the spacing (`HopRulesTests.Hop_spamming_between_swings_stays_inside_the_cap`) | s | per swing | `HopRulesTests` | measured | observed | high |
| Hop out of the aerial tackle | a fresh Jump press in any phase of the dash attack (the aerial tackle: the lunge, its hit, wall stop and run-out, in the air or on the ground) ends it and starts the hop in that tick: no take-off, no tap-or-hold decision, from the stick of that tick, past the hop's spacing (`EvadeLock`, the 0.8 s x 0.7 one still running from the hop the tackle started in; the bypass is deliberate, the owner's intent); the spacing then runs again from the new hop. What bounds a tackle > hop > tackle loop is the tackle's own 1 s spacing (`RushLock`, `min_time_between_activations` of the dash attack), which the hop does not lift. Every dash phase counts: the lunge, its hit (`DashHit`), wall stop (`DashCollision`) and run-out (`DashStop`). The old rule cleared the tackle and refused the hop while the spacing ran, so the press did nothing but let the body fall. A melee press right after the hop still cancels it into a swing (`MeleeCancel`). Not the bull rush (its Jump press is the ledge jump above and the usual take-off) | - | per press | `Combat.StepPlayerCore` (`tackleCancel`), `JumpPack.Begin` (`hopNow`), `Evade.Begin` (`ignoreLock`) | owner 2026-11-14 | owner's decision (the spacing bypass ours) | medium |
| Aerial tackle's momentum | the hop is the usual dash from the state of the press tick: the tackle's speed is not carried, the dash's own travel (about 16.4 m/s along the stick, forward without one) takes over; the rise starts from the body's height | m/s | per press | `Evade.Step` | ours | ours | estimate |
| Musou Mode | the aerial tackle is off there (`AerialTackleOff`), so rule 3 never applies; the hop's cut of the melee wait is moot (Musou melee has no wait: `MeleeSpam`); rule 1 applies as in Classic (Musou already allowed it) | - | - | `SimConfig` | ours | ours | high |
| Restore switch | `--old-hop-rules` (server and every client; config hash only when on): the protocol 71 rules | - | - | `SimConfig.HopRules` | ours | ours | - |
